hazards: UTF-16 semantics: JS .length/slice/charCodeAt drive estimate.ts token counts, assistant-message-frame delta offsets, truncateErrorText, and shortHash (persisted tool-call IDs). Rust/Go strings are UTF-8, so convert offsets explicitly and add golden tests generated from TS.

JSON.stringify parity: key insertion order, omission of undefined fields, and JS number formatting. serde_json prints 1.0 where JS prints 1, and 1e21 is formatted differently. Integer-like object keys are reordered first in JS. Go map[string]any sorts keys. This affects auth.json credential round-trips (open-ended OAuth extra fields), transcript declarationsEqual, frames, and estimates.

WHATWG URL vs native parsers: Go net/url differs in href normalization, hostname lowercasing/IDNA and default-port handling, and url.Values.Encode sorts keys and escapes ~ and * differently. OAuth authorize URLs and test expectations depend on exact encoding and order.

Abort semantics carry reasons, and UIs and tests match exact strings: 'Login cancelled', 'Request aborted', 'The operation was aborted', the TimeoutError reason, '<Provider> sign-in timed out', 'OAuth callback server closed'. raceWithAbortSignal and the credential store stop waiting but keep the operation running, so do not drop in-flight futures that hold locks.

Timing-sensitive tests use vitest fake timers coupled to Date.now (device-code polling, provider-retry backoff, Copilot Retry-After, uuidv7 monotonic clock). Provide one injectable Clock+Sleeper where the virtual wall clock advances with virtual sleeps.

Tests mutate process env (vi.stubEnv for PI_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST, KIMI_CODE_OAUTH_HOST and proxy vars) and global fetch/crypto. Natively, inject an EnvSource, HttpClient and Rng. Rust 2024 makes set_var unsafe, and parallel tests race.

Fixed loopback ports (Anthropic 53692, OpenAI 1455 shared by codex and chatgpt, Radius 1456) are bound by real tests. Run serially. Bind failure must fall back to manual paste (anthropic/codex) or surface an error (radius); never pick another port.

Concurrency: JS single-threaded assumptions become explicit locks. These are the callback server's claimed/settled flags, EventStream queues, the per-provider credential-store chain, and uuidv7 global state.

Lone UTF-16 surrogates cannot exist in Rust/Go strings. serde_json rejects lone-surrogate escapes and Go replaces them with U+FFFD. sanitizeSurrogates semantics must move into the JSON decode policy for provider streams and TS-written session files.

Regex engines: Rust `regex` \d is Unicode (use [0-9]); Go \s is ASCII-only while JS \s is Unicode (used in no_proxy splitting and scope splitting); sanitize-unicode uses lookbehind; JSON Schema `pattern` needs an ECMAScript engine (regress/regexp2).

Transport error text: retry.ts classifies by message substrings tuned to Node/undici/SDK errors ('fetch failed', 'terminated', 'other side closed', 'socket hang up', 'ECONNREFUSED', 'timed out'). The native HTTP layers must format errors so the same classes stay retryable.

JS numeric parsing quirks must be reimplemented: parseFloat prefix parsing for Retry-After, Number(str) (hex, whitespace, Infinity) in validation coercion, Number.isSafeInteger in retryDelayMs, Math.trunc in TypeBox integer Convert, and Date.now()+expires_in*1000 producing non-integer or MAX_SAFE_INTEGER expires values.

TypeBox parity: validateToolArguments applies Value.Convert only to TypeBox-built schemas (hidden '~kind'). The Symbol.for('TypeBox.Kind') check is dead in typebox 1.x, so coerceWithJsonSchema always runs. Error messages and order come from TypeBox's en_US locale and traversal. The native port needs a non-serialized 'typebox-built' marker on schemas produced by the built-in tool schema builder.

Error-detail divergence: anthropic formatErrorDetails embeds JS error name/code/errno/cause/stack, and diagnostics stores error.stack. Exact text parity is impossible natively, so keep the structure and accept different detail text.
PI_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST is read at module load in anthropic.ts and openai-chatgpt.ts but per call in openai-codex.ts and openrouter.ts. Use lazy-once vs per-call reads to stay faithful.
Kimi notifies the raw verification_uri_complete while Meta, xAI and Copilot notify the normalized href. These small per-provider differences are covered by tests and must not be unified.
js_runtime_dependent: auth/oauth/load.ts: in TS, flow modules load through a variable-specifier dynamic import() with a .ts to .js rewrite, plus registerBundledOAuthFlowLoaders for Bun-compiled binaries (src/bun-oauth.ts). Native: each loadXxxOAuth returns the statically linked flow (createRadiusOAuth(options) for radius), and registerBundledOAuthFlowLoaders becomes a no-op.
auth/helpers.ts lazyOAuth: bundler-opaque lazy loading of Node-only flow code. Native: keep the API as a OnceCell-memoized wrapper (a failed load stays failed); no code splitting needed.
auth/context.ts: dynamic import('node:fs/promises') and import('node:os') via a variable specifier for browser safety. Native: direct std::fs/os calls; the browser branch is dropped.

auth/oauth/openai-codex.ts: at module init, lazily runs import('node:crypto'), and createState throws 'only available in Node.js' until that load finishes. Native: the RNG is always available, so drop this path.
utils/pi-user-agent.ts: process.getBuiltinModule('node:os') guarded for browsers, with a 'pi (browser)' fallback. Native: always the OS branch, with Node-style platform/arch names.

utils/provider-env.ts: Bun sandbox workaround that reads /proc/self/environ when process.env is empty (oven-sh/bun#27802). Native: unnecessary, so drop it and use the real environment plus an injectable override source.

utils/validation.ts: TypeBox Compile JIT-generates validator code with new Function (CSP fallback to an interpreter), and kinds are detected through the hidden '~kind' property. Native: an interpreted checker plus Convert hand-port, with an explicit non-serialized schema-origin marker instead of '~kind'.
utils/event-stream.ts: AsyncIterable built on Promise resolvers (Symbol.asyncIterator). Native: Rust futures::Stream; Go Next(ctx) plus iter.Seq.

Tests rely on vitest globals (vi.stubGlobal('fetch'), vi.useFakeTimers, vi.stubEnv, stubbing crypto.getRandomValues and globalThis.Function). Native: injectable HttpClient, Clock/Sleeper, EnvSource and Rng; the JS-JIT-specific validation assertions are dropped.

reports.summary:
The ai-api area is packages/ai/src/api: 37 files, about 12,450 lines. It holds every wire adapter that turns pi's provider-neutral TranscriptContext into a vendor HTTP, WebSocket or SDK request, and parses the vendor's streaming response back into pi's AssistantMessageEventStream. It also holds the classifier and image adapters and a small set of shared helpers.

Stream contract. Every chat adapter exports `stream(model, context, options)` and `streamSimple(model, context, simpleOptions)` with these rules:
- The stream is returned synchronously and filled asynchronously.
- The output AssistantMessage starts with stopReason "pending".
- Events run start, then text/thinking/toolcall start, delta and end, then exactly one terminal done or error.
- Failures are never thrown. They are encoded as an error event whose message has stopReason "error", or "aborted" when the caller's signal fired.
- Streaming scratch fields (index, partialJson, partialArgs, streamIndex, redacted byte buffers) are stripped before the terminal event.
- streamSimple maps the generic reasoning level and token budget onto vendor knobs through simple-options.ts, then calls stream. Only the synchronous auth checks in streamSimple may throw (pre-generation-error test).

Request pipeline, common to all adapters:
1. Normalize the transcript with utils/transcript.ts. System messages (with toolsAdded/toolsRemoved) are either sent natively mid-conversation or collapsed into the leading system prompt.
2. Run transform-messages.ts:
   - Images become placeholders for non-vision models.
   - Thinking blocks are dropped or converted when replaying across models; redacted thinking is kept only for the same model.
   - Tool-call ids are normalized through a provider-specific function, and the mapping is applied to tool results.
   - Errored and aborted assistant turns are dropped.
   - Orphaned tool calls get a synthetic "No result provided" error result.
   - System messages that land between a call and its results are held back until the results are in.
3. Build tools. constrained-sampling.ts creates strict JSON-schema variants (anyOf null for optional fields, full required list, additionalProperties false, unsupported keyword detection) and grammar custom tools (openai_lark, openai_regex). Grammar input is streamed back as a synthetic JSON delta.
4. Build the vendor payload, call `onPayload` (it may replace the payload), send through `retryProviderRequest` (408/409/429/5xx with retry-after), then call `onResponse` with the status and lowercased headers.
5. Parse the stream. Usage and cost come from `calculateCost`; diagnostics are appended; errors are formatted with `normalizeProviderError`/`formatProviderError`.

Adapters:
- **anthropic-messages** (Anthropic SDK; pi parses the SSE itself):
  - Auth modes: API key, OAuth token (Claude Code identity: canonical tool names and a system prompt prefix), GitHub Copilot bearer, and OIDC workload-identity federation (cached SDK client).
  - Beta flags: built-in list, or an override through a configured anthropic-beta header.
  - Cache_control breakpoints with 5-minute or 1-hour TTL.
  - Adaptive thinking, budget thinking, and mid-conversation effort and tool changes (`defer_loading` plus `tool_addition`/`tool_removal`).
- **openai-completions** (OpenAI SDK): a large compat matrix keyed on provider and baseUrl, covering about 11 thinkingFormat variants, reasoning_details, OpenRouter/Vercel routing, cache_control, prompt cache keys and retention, and vLLM priority.
- **openai-responses / azure-openai-responses** (OpenAI SDK; Azure uses the `api-key` header and `api-version` query parameter): share openai-responses-shared.ts, which handles message conversion, reasoning replay from thinkingSignature, the TextSignatureV1 JSON format, additional_tools and synthetic tool_search, and stream processing keyed by output_index.
- **openai-codex-responses** (no SDK):
  - Transports: SSE over fetch with a zstd-compressed body, or a WebSocket.
  - The WebSocket pool is keyed by session and account, with a 5-minute idle TTL and 55-minute maximum age. It continues with `previous_response_id` and only the new input items, falls back to SSE per session after a failure, and exposes debug stats and a cleanup hook.
- **bedrock-converse-stream** (AWS SDK ConverseStream):
  - Credentials from the profile, keys, bearer token or skip-auth.
  - Region from the ARN, then configuration, then the endpoint.
  - Proxy agents; custom-header and response-header middleware.
  - Cache points, redacted reasoning bytes stored as base64, and error metadata with a diagnostic.
- **google-generative-ai / google-vertex** (@google/genai):
  - Shared conversion in google-shared.ts: thought signatures, function-response merging, thinking level vs thinking budget, and function-calling mode.
  - Vertex authenticates with ADC or an API key, and resolves project, location and a custom base URL.
- **mistral-conversations** (fetch, chat/completions):
  - camelCase-to-snake_case remap.
  - Tool-call ids of 9 alphanumeric characters.
  - reasoning_effort, or prompt_mode "reasoning".
- **pi-messages** (fetch): pi's own protocol. It posts `{model, context, options}` to `{baseUrl}/messages` and reads back an SSE stream of serialized pi events, with error diagnostics.
- **Classifiers:**
  - System One over TypeSafe or Cloudflare Workers AI. Bool questions are sent as the wire type "noul".
  - llama-cpp-classify uses llama-server's tokenize, apply-template and completion endpoints with an n_probs label read-out and softmax.
- **Images:** openrouter-images is a non-streaming chat completion with modalities; generated images come back as data URLs.

Registration. Every adapter is exposed through a one-line `*.lazy.ts` that wraps a dynamic import in `lazyApi`/`lazyStream`. The goal is to avoid loading vendor SDKs at import time; a load failure becomes an error event with zero usage.
- In Rust and Go, these become static constructors that return a ProviderStreams trait object or interface. lazyStream's error wrapping is kept, because the async auth and setup failure path still needs it.
- Each *.lazy.ts is assigned to the unit of the adapter it wraps. lazy.ts goes to core.

Porting approach:
- Replace every vendor SDK with hand-written HTTP clients, except the AWS SDK for Bedrock (SigV4, credential chain and event-stream framing), where the official Rust and Go AWS SDKs should be used.
- All request bodies should be serde_json::Value (Rust) or ordered map/struct (Go) after construction, so that onPayload can replace them and key order can be kept.
- Many unit tests use vi.mock on 'openai', '@anthropic-ai/sdk', '@google/genai' and '@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime'. The native ports must provide an injectable HTTP transport (and a Bedrock client trait), and rewrite those tests to capture request JSON and replay recorded SSE or event-stream chunks.

Unit order: ai-api-core first, then the adapters. openai-codex depends on openai-responses-shared. The cross-adapter tests (fetch-option, pre-generation-error) go with ai-api-classifiers-images, which should be built last. All units depend on the ai-types and ai-utils areas: types.ts, models.ts (calculateCost, clampThinkingLevel), utils/event-stream, transcript, text, headers, provider-retry, error-body, json-parse (partial-json), hash, sanitize-unicode, diagnostics, provider-env, pi-user-agent, node-http-proxy, abort-signals, uuid, estimate, and session-resources.

units.notes:
Lazy registration (lazy.ts):
- lazyStream returns the outer stream synchronously, forwards inner events, and ends with inner.result().
- A setup rejection pushes `{type:error, reason:error}` with a message that has content [], zero usage, stopReason error and errorMessage = error.message.
- lazyApi has no dynamic load natively. Keep it as a wrapper over an async setup closure (auth resolution) and keep the fetchDeferred/cancelDeferred capability gating, including the error texts 'API does not support deferred responses' and 'API cannot cancel deferred responses'.

transformMessages:
- Normalizes null content to [] first.
- The image placeholder strings must match exactly. Consecutive images collapse into one placeholder, and a text block equal to the placeholder counts as the previous placeholder.
- Same-model means provider, api and id are all equal.
- Thinking rules: redacted is kept only for the same model. For the same model with a signature, keep even if empty. Empty or whitespace thinking is dropped. Cross-model thinking becomes text.
- Cross-model text blocks are rebuilt as `{type,text}`, which drops textSignature.
- Cross-model toolCall drops thoughtSignature, and its id goes through normalizeToolCallId with a map applied to later toolResults.
- Second pass: skip assistant messages with stopReason error or aborted. Synthesize a toolResult with isError true, 'No result provided' and timestamp Date.now(). Hold back system messages while tool calls are pending, and flush them after the synthetic results.

constrained-sampling:
- structuredClone becomes a deep clone of the JSON value.
- Error strings embed JSON.stringify output, so Go must disable HTML escaping.
- The grammar delta helper emits JSON.stringify(delta).slice(1,-1), i.e. JSON string escaping without the quotes.

simple-options:
- CONTEXT_SAFETY_TOKENS 4096, minimum maxTokens 1; contextWindow <= 0 skips clamping.
- buildBaseOptions copies about 20 option fields; keep the same field set in the native options struct.

Small helpers:
- openai-prompt-cache truncates to 64 Unicode code points, not bytes or UTF-16 units.
- github-copilot-headers: X-Initiator, Openai-Intent conversation-edits, Copilot-Vision-Request.

Cloudflare:
- cloudflare.ts holds only URL template constants. scripts/generate-models.ts also uses them, so export them publicly.
- cloudflare-ai-binding.ts wraps a Workers `env.AI` binding into a fetch. It is Workers-only: keep CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_BINDING_AUTH_SENTINEL and either omit createAiBindingFetch or expose it as a transport adapter over a user-supplied trait. Its test is in openai-completions.

Tests:
- context-estimate also exercises utils/estimate.ts (ai-utils area).
- providers.test.ts and telemetry-options.test.ts use lazyApi/buildBaseOptions but belong to the ai-models/providers area.

units.notes:
Request (the SDK is replaced by a hand-written client):
- POST {baseUrl}/v1/messages?beta=true, because the SDK beta endpoint appends ?beta=true.
- Headers:
  - accept: application/json, anthropic-version: 2023-06-01, anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true.
  - anthropic-beta = betas joined with ','.
  - Auth is x-api-key for API keys and Authorization Bearer for authToken (OAuth, Copilot, federation).
  - User-Agent comes from getPiUserAgent; OAuth uses claude-cli/<version> plus x-app cli.
  - Session affinity uses x-session-id (openrouter) or x-session-affinity.
  - The SDK's X-Stainless-* headers can be omitted.
  - Header merge is case-insensitive, and a null value deletes the header.
- The SDK is called with maxRetries 0; retryProviderRequest owns retries. timeout comes from timeoutMs.

OIDC federation:
- Configured by the ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, ORGANIZATION_ID, IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE, WORKSPACE_ID and SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID env vars.
- Must re-implement the SDK credential flow: read the identity token file, reject tokens over 16 KiB, POST {baseUrl}/v1/oauth/token with a JSON jwt-bearer grant (federation_rule_id, organization_id, optional service_account_id and workspace_id) and anthropic-beta set to the oauth and federation betas, then cache the token until expiry.
- Keep one cached client keyed by JSON of [baseUrl, config]. anthropic-federation-sdk.test asserts the token is exchanged only once across requests.
- Port the SDK's 401 hint text.
- PiAnthropic disables the SDK default credential chain (ANTHROPIC_PROFILE files). The native client must likewise never read the ambient Anthropic config.

SSE parser:
- Must handle CR, LF and CRLF line breaks, multi-line data, the event field and error events.
- Throws 'Anthropic stream ended before message_stop'.
- An unknown stop reason throws; refusal and sensitive map to error.
- Usage: message_start sets usage; message_delta overrides only non-null fields. cache_creation 1h tokens are priced as cacheWrite1h; thinking_tokens become reasoning.

Payload construction:
- Exact beta list logic and tool-name canonicalization for OAuth, plus reverse mapping on tool_use.
- Placeholder deferred tool __pi_deferred_placeholder__.
- System messages with an empty content array carrying output_config effort.
- Block binding drop_block.
- Cache_control on the system prompt, the last tool and the last user/system block (string content is converted to a block). TTL is 1h for long retention when supported.
- Strict-schema keyword whitelist (minItems only 0 or 1, format whitelist).
- Image-only tool result gets '(see attached image)'; consecutive toolResults merge into one user message.
- An empty-signature thinking compat flag.

streamSimple:
- thinkingBudget = min(budget, maxTokens - 1024) after clampMaxTokensToContext.
- forceAdaptiveThinking uses effort mapping.

Tests:
- The vi.mock('@anthropic-ai/sdk') tests (auth-token, federation, github-copilot-anthropic) should be rewritten against the injectable HTTP transport, asserting request headers and body.
- fireworks-models uses a local node:http server; port with a local test server.

Transport:
- Replace the openai SDK with POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions, Authorization Bearer, the pi User-Agent from defaultHeaders, and SSE 'data:' lines ending at [DONE].
- SDK error messages ('<status> <json body>' style) feed normalizeProviderError, so reproduce the status/body/headers error shape.

Compat matrix:
- detectCompat/getCompat derive flags from provider and baseUrl substrings (zai, together, moonshot, openrouter, cloudflare, nvidia, ant-ling, cerebras, deepseek, xai, chutes, opencode); model.compat overrides them.
- Port it as a pure function with a table-driven test.
- thinkingFormat variants each produce different payload fields (enable_thinking, chat_template_kwargs, reasoning_effort, reasoning {effort|max_tokens}, thinking {type}, and others).

Request fields:
- max_tokens vs max_completion_tokens.
- store false; stream_options.include_usage.
- prompt_cache_key, clamped to 64 code points; prompt_cache_retention '24h'.
- Anthropic-style cache_control on the last messages when compat requires it.
- provider (OpenRouter routing); providerOptions.gateway (Vercel).
- vLLM priority.
- samplingParams are merged last and override everything.
- tools omitted when empty, depending on compat (empty-tools test).

Response parsing:
- Reasoning from reasoning_content, reasoning or reasoning_text. The signature is the field name, except opencode-go maps reasoning to reasoning_content.
- reasoning_details is merged into the toolCall thoughtSignature by id.
- Usage: cacheRead from prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, then prompt_cache_hit_tokens, then cached_tokens; cache_write_tokens is subtracted.
- An unknown finish_reason becomes error 'Provider finish_reason: X'. A missing finish_reason gives 'Stream ended without finish_reason'.
- An OpenRouter error appends error.metadata.raw without double-printing.
- onProviderStreamEvent receives raw chunks; responseModel comes from chunk.model.

Message conversion:
- Kimi tool system message.
- requiresAssistantAfterToolResult inserts 'I have processed the tool results.'
- Tool-result images are sent as a follow-up user message headed 'Attached image(s) from tool result:'.
- Tool call ids: '|' ids are cut to 40, otherwise a prefix plus shortHash.

units.notes:
openai-responses-shared is also used by openai-codex, so its API must be public within the crate/package.

convertResponsesMessages:
- textSignature is JSON {v:1,id,phase}; legacy plain ids are accepted.
- Fallback message ids are msg_pi_<n>; ids over 64 characters become msg_<shortHash>.
- Reasoning items are replayed by parsing thinkingSignature as JSON.
- Tool call ids have the form 'callId|itemId'. Foreign item ids not starting with fc_/ctc_ become fc_<shortHash>.
- additional_tools, or a synthetic tool_search_call/tool_search_output pair with id pi_tool_load_<shortHash(seed:names)>.
- Grammar tools are sent as custom tools; custom_tool_call input is streamed as a synthetic JSON delta.
- Namespace handling (namespace test).

processResponsesStream:
- Slots are keyed by output_index.
- Reasoning encrypted_content is backfilled from output_item.done (Azure, issue 6409).
- Unfinished tool calls are rejected.
- Throws 'OpenAI Responses stream ended before a terminal response event'.
- incomplete with max_output_tokens maps to length.
- partialJson scratch is stripped.

openai-responses:
- POST {baseUrl}/responses.
- ChatGPT sign-in detection (provider openai, base api.openai.com/v1, key not starting with sk-) omits some fields and appends a usage URL to usage-limit errors.
- prompt_cache_options {mode:'explicit'} or {ttl:'30m'}; prompt_cache_retention '24h' only when supportsLongCacheRetention is set.
- Service tier cost multipliers: flex 0.5; priority 2, or 2.5 for gpt-5.5.
- Minimum max_output_tokens is 16.
- xai includes reasoning.encrypted_content.

azure-openai-responses:
- Uses the api-key header (not Bearer) and always appends ?api-version=<v> (default 'v1').
- The model name maps to a deployment through AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP 'a=b,c=d'.
- normalizeAzureBaseUrl appends /openai/v1 for Azure hosts.
- Env vars: AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL, AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME, AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION.
- The SDK constructor errors if apiVersion is empty; replicate only what tests assert.

Tests:
- assistant-message-frame and constrained-sampling drive processResponsesStream with typed event arrays; port the event structs or use serde Value fixtures.
- cache-retention, sampling-options and transcript-tool-changes are multi-adapter (anthropic, completions, responses). They capture payloads through onPayload and abort, and belong here because this is the last of those three units.

units.title: OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT backend) Responses adapter: SSE+zstd and cached WebSocket transport
skipped_tests: packages/ai/test/openai-codex-cache-affinity-e2e.test.ts -- real ChatGPT backend
packages/ai/test/codex-websocket-cached-probe.ts -- manual live probe script, imports coding-agent ModelRuntime
units.notes:
Endpoint and auth:
- Default base https://chatgpt.com/backend-api. URL normalization appends /codex/responses; WebSocket swaps https for wss.
- The account id comes from the JWT payload claim 'https://api.openai.com/auth'.chatgpt_account_id. It is decoded with atob, i.e. forgiving standard base64, not base64url. On failure the error is 'Failed to extract accountId from token'.
- Headers: Authorization Bearer, chatgpt-account-id, originator pi, User-Agent, session-id, x-client-request-id (uuidv7). OpenAI-Beta is 'responses=experimental' for SSE or 'responses_websockets=2026-02-06' for WebSocket.

SSE path:
- The body is zstd-compressed at level 3 with content-encoding zstd when available.
- Frames are split on blank lines and the data: lines joined.
- Retries: 1000ms x 2^attempt, honoring retry-after-ms and retry-after, capped at 60000ms by default. A terminal usage-limit regex stops retrying.
- parseErrorResponse produces the friendly 'You have hit your ChatGPT usage limit (<plan>). Try again in ~N min.'

WebSocket path:
- A module-global session cache keyed by sessionId and accountId, with 5-minute idle TTL, 55-minute maximum age, and in-use tracking.
- Continuation sends previous_response_id plus only the delta input items when the prefix matches.
- On failure, the session falls back to SSE permanently (websocketSseFallbackSessions).
- Close code 1009 means message too big. Connect timeout defaults to 15000ms (websocketConnectTimeoutMs).
- Debug stats getters and reset are exported; closeOpenAICodexWebSocketSessions is registered through registerSessionResourceCleanup.
- Use tokio-tungstenite / coder/websocket with custom headers and HTTP(S) proxy CONNECT support, honoring resolveHttpProxyUrlForTarget, because the Bun proxy subclass exists for exactly this.

Events:
- mapCodexEvents converts response.done and response.incomplete to response.completed, reads end_turn, and feeds processResponsesStream.

Request body:
- instructions default 'You are a helpful assistant.', text.verbosity 'low', include ['reasoning.encrypted_content'], parallel_tool_calls true, tool_choice 'auto', prompt_cache_key clamped.
- max-thinking test: the reasoning effort clamp through clampThinkingLevel.

Tests:
- openai-codex-stream.test (2696 lines) uses fetch mocks and a fake WebSocket class. The native port needs injectable HTTP transport and WebSocket connector traits, plus a clock/timer abstraction for the TTL tests.

units.title: Amazon Bedrock ConverseStream adapter
skipped_tests: packages/ai/test/bedrock-models.test.ts -- live Bedrock calls gated on AWS credentials
units.notes:
Port on the official AWS SDKs (aws-sdk-bedrockruntime / aws-sdk-go-v2 bedrockruntime) and keep the ConverseStream request shape.

Credentials and region:
- Env vars: AWS_PROFILE, AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK (bearer token auth instead of SigV4), AWS_BEDROCK_SKIP_AUTH (unsigned, for proxies), AWS_BEDROCK_FORCE_HTTP1, AWS_BEDROCK_FORCE_CACHE. The env may come from options.env rather than the process env; tests inject it.
- Region order: ARN region, then options/env, then parsed from a custom endpoint host bedrock-runtime(-fips).<region>.amazonaws.com(.cn), then us-east-1.
- Proxy uses a NodeHttpHandler with an http(s) proxy agent. Natively, use a custom HTTP client with the proxy and an HTTP/1 forcing option.

Middleware:
- Custom headers are added at the build step. Reserved names are skipped: x-amz-*, authorization, host.
  - Rust: an Intercept::modify_before_signing interceptor.
  - Go: smithy Build middleware.
- Response headers are captured after deserialize to feed onResponse.

Payload:
- Cache points (ttl '1h' when long retention) only for supported Claude models, detected through model id or model.name for application inference profiles.
- '<empty>' placeholder for empty text.
- Adaptive thinking by model-id match (opus-4-6/7/8, opus-5, sonnet-4-6, sonnet-5, fable-5), otherwise budget thinking. xhigh maps to effort xhigh. GovCloud omits display. anthropic_beta interleaved goes in additionalModelRequestFields.
- Tool ids are sanitized and cut to 64.

Stream:
- reasoningContent.redactedContent bytes are buffered and stored as a base64 thinkingSignature, then the scratch is stripped on every terminal path.

Errors:
- Prefixes per exception name (Internal server error, Model stream error, Validation error, Throttling error, Service unavailable).
- A data-retention docs hint.
- bedrock_response_failure diagnostic with metadata (httpStatusCode, requestId).
- Body-blind gateway errors surface the raw body (provider-error-body-regression).

Lazy wrapper: setBedrockProviderModule and the variable-specifier import exist only for bundlers; drop them and register statically. Optionally gate behind a cargo feature or Go build tag to keep the AWS SDK out of minimal builds.

Tests: they vi.mock '@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime'. Define a narrow BedrockClient trait/interface (converse_stream(input) -> event iterator, plus config inspection for region/credentials/endpoint) so tests can inject fakes. Endpoint and credential tests assert the resolved client config.

units.title: Google Gemini API and Vertex AI adapters with shared conversion
skipped_tests: packages/ai/test/google-thinking-disable.test.ts -- all suites gated on GEMINI/ANTHROPIC/Vertex credentials
units.notes:
Replacing @google/genai means reproducing its param-to-REST mapping: - The camelCase GenerateContentParameters {model, contents, config:{systemInstruction, tools, toolConfig, thinkingConfig, temperature, maxOutputTokens, ...}} becomes the REST body {contents, systemInstruction, tools, toolConfig, generationConfig:{...}}. - POST //models/:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse (Gemini) with header x-goog-api-key. - Vertex: https://-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/

/locations//publishers/google/models/:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse with an ADC Bearer token. Location 'global' uses aiplatform.googleapis.com. API-key (express) mode uses the publishers/google/models path with the key. - A custom baseUrl uses ResourceScope.COLLECTION semantics (base + models/...). apiVersion '' when the base already contains a /vN segment; a baseUrl containing '{location}' is ignored. - Verify the exact URLs against node_modules/@google/genai before porting. Auth (Vertex): - GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS keyFilename, otherwise ADC (gcloud user credentials, metadata server). - Project from GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or GCLOUD_PROJECT; location from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION. - The API key marker 'gcp-vertex-credentials' and placeholder keys '<...>' are ignored. - Custom fetch is rejected unless it is the global fetch. Natively, reject an injected transport for Google, or support it but keep the test semantics. google-shared: - Thought signatures must match the base64 regex with length % 4 == 0. - requiresToolCallId for claude-*, gpt-oss-* and gemini-3+. - Gemini 3 unsigned tool calls are replayed as text (test). - Multimodal functionResponse parts for gemini 3+; otherwise a separate 'Tool result image:' user part. - sanitizeForOpenApi when not using parametersJsonSchema. - Function-calling mode VALIDATED in strict mode. - retryGoogleRequest clears error.headers before retrying. Thinking: - usesGoogleThinkingLevel matches gemini-3(.x)-pro|flash, gemma4 and -latest ids. - Budgets: 2.5-pro {128, 2048, 8192, 32768}; 2.5-flash-lite {512, ...} on the Gemini API only; 2.5-flash {128, 2048, 8192, 24576}; otherwise -1 (dynamic). Usage: output = candidates + thoughts; input = prompt - cached. Tool-call ids are generated as name_Date.now()_counter, with a module counter; tests need a deterministic clock or loose matching. Tests: google-raw-stop-reason and google-vertex-api-key-resolution vi.mock '@google/genai'. Rewrite them with an injectable transport and a credential-provider seam.

units.title: Mistral chat adapter (hand-written HTTP) and pi-messages native protocol adapter
units.notes:
Mistral:
- POST {baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions with a 60s default timeout combined with the caller signal.
- The payload is built camelCase, then remapped to snake_case by delete-and-reinsert, which moves remapped keys to the end. Keep the key order if byte-compat of onPayload output matters.
- Headers: x-affinity from sessionId; prompt_cache_key = sessionId.
- Errors: 'Mistral API error (<status>): <body>', with the body truncated at 4000 chars (UTF-16 units in JS).
- SSE events are split by a regex on blank lines.
- Tool call ids are 9 alphanumeric chars derived from shortHash, with collision retries.
- Tool results are prefixed '[tool error] ' and use image-omitted texts.
- reasoning_effort when the model has a thinkingLevelMap, otherwise prompt_mode 'reasoning'.
- A mistral-tool-schema test captures tool parameter serialization through onPayload.

pi-messages:
- POST {baseUrl}/messages (optional ?debug=1) with body {model, context, options:{temperature, maxTokens, reasoning, cacheRetention, sessionId, toolChoice}}.
- The context is pi's own TranscriptContext JSON, so it must serialize byte-identically to the TS on-disk/wire message format, including key order and optional field omission.
- The response is SSE (\r\n normalized) of serialized AssistantMessageEvents. createEventConverter rebuilds partial messages, and toolcall deltas are re-parsed with parseStreamingJson.
- Terminal done/error events.
- PiMessagesResponseError carries diagnostic version 1 with the body truncated at 8192 chars plus an ellipsis.
- pi_messages_rewrite diagnostic.
- Cache retention resolves from options, falling back to the PI_CACHE_RETENTION env.
- Used by the Radius gateway provider.

Tests: mistral-http-transport and pi-messages mock fetch, so map them directly onto the injectable transport.

units.title: Classifier adapters (System One via TypeSafe/Cloudflare, llama.cpp logprob classifier) and OpenRouter image generation
skipped_tests: packages/ai/test/images.test.ts -- live image generation gated on API key
units.notes:
Imports outside this unit: the source files import only types/models/utils. The adapter files listed in depends_on are needed only by the cross-adapter tests fetch-option and pre-generation-error, which is why this unit is built last.

system-one-shared (classifySystemOne):
- Validates the api, then the apiKey ('No API key for provider: X'). Bool questions become type 'noul' on the wire.
- Optional onPayload replacement.
- POST with headers authorization Bearer and content-type, merged with model and options headers.
- timeoutMs is combined with the signal. A timeout produces a TimeoutError 'Request timed out after Nms'.
- retryProviderRequest with maxRetries default 2. A non-ok status throws '<label> returned <status>' with the body attached.
- Usage is parsed before answers, because a malformed answer was still billed.
- parseAnswers validates choice, score and bool ('noul' probability) answers with exact error texts.
- The result object is returned (never thrown) with stopReason error or aborted.

Transports:
- typesafe: URL {baseUrl}/systemone, payload {model, ...request}.
- cloudflare: URL {baseUrl}/run, payload {model, input}; unwraps {result} and requires result.state 'Completed'.

llama-cpp-classify:
- Endpoints /tokenize, /apply-template, /completion. Request: n_probs depth, n_predict 1, cache_prompt.
- Label sets: A-Z, a-z, 0-9 for choices, digits for scores, Yes/No for bools.
- Depth max(256, 16 x labels), escalating to 4096 then 32768.
- UNDERFLOW_LOGPROB -1e30. Softmax with temperature; peakConfidence.
- renderQuestion uses JSON.stringify(state, null, 1), so Go/Rust need a JS-compatible indent-1 pretty printer with key order kept. Appends '</think>' when the template ends with '<think>'.
- labelTokenCache is a module-level map of promises; use a once-cell per key.
- Exports llamaServerRoot, renderQuestion, labelProbabilities, peakConfidence and answerFromProbabilities, which coding-agent's llama extension uses.

openrouter-images:
- Non-streaming POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions with modalities ['image','text'] or ['image'].
- Images are parsed from message.images[].image_url (string or {url}) data URLs.
- Its own usage/cost math is per million tokens, with cache_write subtracted from cached tokens.
- Errors go through formatProviderError without a prefix.

Tests:
- openrouter-images and provider-error-body-passthrough vi.mock 'openai'; port them against the fake transport.
- fetch-option: Google adapters must reject a custom transport.
- pre-generation-error: streamSimple throws synchronously on missing auth for 7 adapters.

hazards: The SDKs are mocked at module level in tests (vi.mock of 'openai', '@anthropic-ai/sdk', '@google/genai', '@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime' in about 30 test files). Native ports need explicit seams: an HTTP transport trait/interface in StreamOptions (replaces options.fetch), a WebSocket connector, a Bedrock client trait, a Google credential provider, and a clock. Tests must be rewritten to assert request JSON and headers and to replay SSE/event-stream frames.

JSON key order and omission. Payloads are built from object literals, so insertion order matters, and undefined fields are dropped. Mistral's camel-to-snake remap moves keys to the end. Rust needs serde_json with preserve_order, or ordered structs with skip_serializing_if. Go maps sort keys, so use ordered structs or an ordered map type. Stable byte output also matters for provider prompt-cache prefix hits.

JSON.stringify parity. Go's encoding/json escapes <, >, & and U+2028/U+2029 by default; use an Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false). Number formatting must match JS (integers without '.0', exponent forms). Grammar tool deltas rely on JSON.stringify(delta).slice(1,-1). llama-cpp renderQuestion uses JSON.stringify(state, null, 1), i.e. an indent of one space.

String length units. JS .length/.slice count UTF-16 code units: tool-id truncation to 64 or 40, Mistral body truncation at 4000, pi-messages at 8192, and others. clampOpenAIPromptCacheKey uses code points (Array.from). Rust and Go index bytes, so implement UTF-16-aware truncation helpers to keep outputs and error strings identical for non-ASCII input.

Error message text is part of the observable contract. Tests assert exact errorMessage strings produced by the SDK error shapes ('<status> <body>'), normalizeProviderError/formatProviderError, Bedrock exception-name prefixes, the Codex friendly usage-limit text, Anthropic 'stream ended before message_stop', Responses 'stream ended before a terminal response event', and Completions 'Provider finish_reason: X'.

Errors-as-events contract. Adapters must never return Err/throw after the stream is handed out. Every failure becomes a terminal error event with stopReason 'aborted' when the caller signal fired, otherwise 'error'. Scratch fields must be stripped on every terminal path. Only streamSimple's synchronous auth precheck may fail eagerly.

SSE parsers differ per adapter and must not be unified carelessly:
- Anthropic: full CR/LF/CRLF handling with the event field.
- Codex: splits on blank lines.
- Mistral: regex boundary.
- pi-messages: normalizes CRLF first.
- OpenAI and Google: SDK parsers ('data:' lines, [DONE]).
UTF-8 must be decoded across chunk boundaries (TextDecoder stream mode).

Module-level mutable state:
- Codex WebSocket session cache, debug stats and SSE-fallback set.
- Anthropic federation client cache.
- llama labelTokenCache.
- Google tool-call counter.
- Codex cached WebSocket constructor.
Use a Mutex/RwLock/sync.Map, expose reset hooks for tests, and register Codex cleanup with session-resources.

Time and randomness in outputs: Date.now() timestamps on messages and synthetic tool results, Google tool-call ids name_<ms>_<n>, uuidv7 x-client-request-id, retry backoff timers and Codex TTL/max-age checks. Inject a clock to port deterministic tests.

Auth precedence and env sources. Credentials come from options.env (ProviderEnv) or the process env through getProviderEnvValue. Examples: Bedrock profile/keys/bearer/skip-auth, Vertex ADC vs API key with marker and placeholder rejection, Anthropic OAuth detection by 'sk-ant-oat' substring, federation env set, ChatGPT sign-in detection (non-'sk-' key on api.openai.com). Never read ambient SDK config files that the TS code disables (Anthropic profile chain).

Google REST mapping is hidden inside @google/genai: the config fields move into generationConfig; systemInstruction, tools and toolConfig sit at top level; URL construction covers apiVersion '', ResourceScope.COLLECTION, Vertex global vs regional hosts, and API-key express mode. Verify against node_modules/@google/genai source before porting.

Bedrock parity depends on AWS SDK behavior that differs across languages: the default credential chain order, region providers, retry policy (TS relies on SDK defaults here, not retryProviderRequest), and the event-stream exception mapping. Confirm the Rust and Go SDK exception type names match the TS name-prefix mapping.

Numeric types. Token counts and costs are JS doubles; providers may send floats or nulls. Use f64 for cost math and tolerant integer parsing for tokens, matching the `|| 0` and Math.max(0, ...) semantics. Anthropic message_delta overwrites only non-null fields.

onPayload may return an arbitrary replacement payload. Build typed requests, convert to a JSON value, run the hook, and send the (possibly replaced) value. onResponse receives the status and lowercased header record; onProviderStreamEvent receives raw vendor events.

The Codex JWT is decoded with atob, which uses the standard base64 alphabet and accepts missing padding. A base64url character makes it throw, which is mapped to 'Failed to extract accountId from token'. Replicate this forgiving-base64 behavior rather than using a base64url decoder, unless parity is consciously changed.
js_runtime_dependent: lazy.ts and every *.lazy.ts dynamically import adapter modules to avoid loading SDKs at startup. Native handling: static registration functions that return ProviderStreams/ProviderClassifier/ProviderImages trait objects or interfaces. Keep lazyStream's async-setup error wrapping (error event with zero usage), and the fetchDeferred/cancelDeferred capability gating with the same error texts.

bedrock-converse-stream.lazy.ts uses a variable-specifier import plus setBedrockProviderModule as a bundler workaround (Bun compile, browser smoke). Native handling: drop both and link Bedrock statically, optionally behind a cargo feature or Go build tag to exclude the AWS SDK from minimal builds.

cloudflare-ai-binding.ts adapts a Cloudflare Workers `env.AI` binding into a fetch function, which exists only inside the Workers runtime. Native handling: keep CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_BINDING_AUTH_SENTINEL, and either omit createAiBindingFetch or expose an optional transport adapter over a user-implemented binding trait. Its test is ported only if the adapter is kept.

Codex WebSocket: getWebSocketConstructor picks Bun's WebSocket subclass with a proxy option, or the global undici WebSocket with a headers option. Native handling: a single tokio-tungstenite / coder/websocket connector with custom headers and HTTP CONNECT proxy support driven by resolveHttpProxyUrlForTarget, behind an injectable connector for tests.

Codex zstd compression uses process.getBuiltinModule('node:zlib').zstdCompressSync and falls back to an uncompressed body when unavailable. Native handling: always compress with the zstd crate or klauspost/compress at level 3, keeping the content-encoding header.

The custom `fetch` option (StreamOptions.fetch, ClassifierOptions.fetch, ImagesOptions.fetch) is passed into SDKs or used directly. Native handling: an HttpTransport trait/interface in the options. Google adapters reject a custom transport, matching the TS rejection of non-global fetch.

Callbacks onPayload, onResponse and onProviderStreamEvent are JS closures, possibly async. Native handling: boxed async closures (Rust) or func fields (Go) in the options structs. These are used by native extensions and by tests, not by user TS.

structuredClone (constrained-sampling strict schema), AbortSignal.timeout/AbortSignal.any (Mistral, System One, Codex combineAbortSignals) and TextDecoder streaming. Native handling: deep clone of a JSON value, CancellationToken plus tokio timeout / context.WithTimeout, and a byte buffer with UTF-8 boundary handling.

The SDK classes PiAnthropic, OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, GoogleGenAI and BedrockRuntimeClient are instantiated per request with defaultHeaders, maxRetries 0 and timeout. Native handling: thin hand-written request builders (or the AWS SDK for Bedrock) that reproduce the same URL, headers and body. SDK-internal X-Stainless-* telemetry headers can be dropped.

reports.summary:
The small-pkgs area covers six packages around the core ai/coding-agent pipeline: agent (pi-agent-core), telemetry, protocol, server, client and evals. About 9.1k TS source lines in total, split into 9 work units.

agent (pi-agent-core, about 2.7k lines)
- agent-loop.ts is a stateless pipeline: runAgentLoop / runAgentLoopContinue(prompts, context, config, emit, signal, streamFn).
- Each turn does the following:
  1. Drains the steering queue.
  2. Streams the assistant response: transformContext, then convertToLlm, then normalizeContext, then streamFn with apiKey = getApiKey(provider) || config.apiKey. The partial message is pushed into context.messages and replaced on every update. Event payloads are shallow copies. The final message gets thinkingLevel attached.
  3. Stops on stopReason error/aborted.
  4. Runs the tool calls:
     - Prepare: lookup, prepareArguments, validateToolArguments, beforeToolCall (block/terminate).
     - Execute: sequential, or parallel. In parallel mode, preparation runs sequentially, tools run concurrently, tool_execution_end is emitted in completion order, and tool-result messages are emitted in source order. A tool with executionMode sequential forces the whole batch to sequential.
     - Finalize: afterToolCall merges content/details/usage/terminate/isError, dropping stale structuredContent.
     - stopReason length fails every tool call with a fixed message.
     - The batch terminates only if every result sets terminate=true.
  5. finishTurn / prepareNextTurn hooks may end the run or swap model, tools or system prompt. Tool loadout changes are recorded on system messages via toolsAdded / toolsRemoved.
  6. When there are no more tool calls, the follow-up queue is polled.
- Event sequence: agent_start, turn_start, message_start/update/end, tool_execution_start/update/end, turn_end, agent_end.
- agent.ts wraps the loop in a stateful Agent:
  - subscribe listeners are awaited serially with the run signal.
  - Steering and follow-up queues support all and one-at-a-time modes.
  - Also: abort, waitForIdle, reset (keeps the baseline system message), prompt, continue.
  - Failures produce a synthetic assistant message with stopReason error/aborted plus turn_end/agent_end.
- proxy.ts is a StreamFn that POSTs to {proxyUrl}/api/stream and rebuilds an AssistantMessage from compact SSE events.

telemetry (935 lines, no dependencies)
- TelemetryContext.startSpan(options, callback). The span is admitted at call time.
- NOOP context. InMemoryTelemetryContext records spans with sequence numbers, attribute merging, and automatic error status.
- Typed schema helpers are compile-time only.
- testing/ holds a runner-independent conformance suite.

protocol (880 lines)
- Wire format of the experimental client/server.
- Strict CBOR subset: definite lengths only, safe integers as major types 0/1, every other number as float64, string keys only, no tags, no float16/32, no undefined. Limits on bytes, entries and depth.
- 4-byte big-endian length framing, plus a FrameDecoder state machine.
- TypeBox message schemas, PROTOCOL_VERSION 8. Client messages: hello, request, cancel. Server messages: hello, hello_error, response, service_update, attachment.
- Sticky-failing validated message decoders.
- Uses chord isJsonValue.

server (about 2.0k lines)
- Server accepts ByteConnections from ServerListeners and enforces a handshake with a 5 s timeout.
- Requests are routed either to host.serverServices (target {serverId}) or, through SessionRouter, to a session attachment (target {serverId, sessionId, attachmentId}).
- SessionRouter: serializes operations per client, shares session opening, waits for in-flight operations before releasing, and invalidates sessions on terminated.
- Service subscriptions ($chord.service subscribe/unsubscribe/catalogue) become delta-encoded service_update frames via the chord ServiceStateEncoder.
- Unix transport:
  - Binds a hashed temp path, links it to the public path and chmods it 0600.
  - Detects stale sockets by probe-connecting.
  - Cleans up with an inode check.
  - Enforces pending-byte backpressure and closes gracefully with a final frame.
- testing/ exports in-process harnesses that client and coding-agent tests use.

client (about 1.15k lines)
- Connection is a handshake state machine over a ByteTransport.
- Client handles request/cancel correlation with abort signals, service subscriptions (updates buffered until the snapshot is hydrated and then until start), attachment notifications, and a chord RemoteServiceTransport adapter.
- Unix transport with backpressure, plus discoverUnixServers: probes <uuid>.sock files with bounded concurrency and ignores dead servers.

evals (about 2.6k lines, private)
- A documentation-lift experiment. Each vitest-evals case runs in Docker, in a without_docs image and a with_docs image, possibly several times.
- cli.ts: builds the images, discovers cases, runs an alternating task plan, collects Vitest JSON plus vitest-evals metadata into observations, and writes protocol / expected-runs / observations / report.json / report.txt.
- harness.ts: drives a real coding-agent AgentSession inside the container. It isolates the environment, drops root via setgroups/setgid/setuid, seeds a workspace, and strips or verifies the <docs> block in the system prompt.
- Eval suites under evals/ hit real models. A local acme HTTP fixture emulates an OpenAI-compatible provider.

Port order
1. telemetry and protocol. protocol needs chord json/types.
2. agent, after ai types, event-stream, transcript, validation, json-parse and the faux provider for tests.
3. server, after protocol and chord services/context.
4. client. Its tests need the server.
5. evals, last, after the coding-agent SDK.
6. agent examples, after mcp and codemode.

Cross-cutting decisions

Value model and key order
- Use one JSON value model with insertion-ordered maps (serde_json preserve_order / IndexMap in Rust; an ordered map type in Go).
- Numbers are f64 semantically. Integer-valued finite doubles must encode as CBOR integers.
- AgentMessages flow into session JSONL, so the TS key order and the omission of undefined fields must be reproduced exactly:
  - thinkingLevel is appended after timestamp.
  - Tool result order is role, toolCallId, toolName, content, details, usage, isError, timestamp.
  - The proxy partial message has its own order.

Concurrency
- Rust uses tokio with CancellationToken; Go uses goroutines with context.Context.
- Guarantees that TS gets from single-threaded microtasks must be enforced explicitly:
  - serialized event emission and awaited listeners
  - per-client operation chains in SessionRouter
  - socket write tails
  - FIFO event-stream queues
- Error message strings are part of observable behaviour (tests and wire error messages) and must be copied verbatim.

Evals reimplementation
- evals depends on vitest, vitest-evals, @vitest-evals/core and Docker images that build the TS repo.
- A native port needs a small eval runner (describeEval, judges, harness run records), images that build the Rust/Go binaries, and adapted suites. The extension-authoring suites conflict with the no-TS-extensions decision.

units.title: Agent types, default stream fn, and the agent loop (agentLoop/runAgentLoop/runToolCall)
units.notes:
TYPES
- types.ts maps to Rust traits/enums and Go interfaces/structs.
- AgentMessage = pi-ai Message plus CustomAgentMessages (declaration merging). Use an enum with a Custom variant: Rust Custom{role, raw ordered JSON}; Go a CustomMessage struct implementing the AgentMessage interface. Coding-agent defines the concrete custom roles.
- AgentTool:
  - Rust trait with name/label/description/parameters (JSON Schema value), optional prepare_arguments, execute(id, args, cancel, on_update) returning Result<AgentToolResult>, execution_mode, replay (never|safe).
  - Go: an interface plus an optional PrepareArguments interface.
- AgentToolResult.details needs three states: absent, null, value. The afterToolCall merge uses ??, so an explicit null falls back to the original. Rust: Option<Value>; Go: a pointer or json.RawMessage plus a present flag.
- ThinkingLevel strings: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max.

DEFAULT STREAM FN
- stream-fn.ts global: Rust OnceLock<RwLock<Option<Arc<dyn StreamFn>>>>; Go a package var guarded by a mutex.
- Copy the error text verbatim: No default stream function configured. Pass streamFn explicitly or call setDefaultStreamFn().

LOOP
- agentLoop / agentLoopContinue return an EventStream. In TS a rejection inside runAgentLoop leaves the stream never ended. The native port should close the stream (with an error) rather than hang; document the divergence.
- agentLoopContinue throws:
  - Cannot continue: no messages in context
  - Cannot continue from message role: assistant
- emit is awaited for every event. Rust: emit returns a future awaited inline. Go: a synchronous callback.
- Parallel tool mode (the default):
  - Preparation is strictly sequential in source order: lookup, prepareArguments, validateToolArguments, beforeToolCall.
  - Execution is concurrent (JoinSet / goroutines + WaitGroup).
  - tool_execution_end is emitted in completion order.
  - toolResult message_start/end are emitted in source order after all calls finish.
  - All emits must go through a single serialized sink (mutex or channel) because Rust and Go have no single-threaded event loop.
  - Any tool with executionMode sequential makes the whole batch sequential.
- onUpdate: updates arriving after the tool settles are ignored, and pending update emits are awaited before tool_execution_end.
- beforeToolCall receives the validated args by reference. Mutations made by the hook are executed WITHOUT revalidation (tested). In Rust pass &mut Value; in Go pass a map that is reused.
- If prepareArguments returns the identical object, keep the original toolCall. Rust: compare by pointer identity or a returned Option.
- afterToolCall merge: content/details/usage/terminate use ??. structuredContent = after.structuredContent ?? (after.content ? undefined : original). The key is deleted when undefined. If the hook throws, the result becomes an error tool result with the error message.
- Terminate the run only when ALL results have terminate=true.
- stopReason length: every tool call fails with this exact text: Tool call "<name>" was not executed: the response hit the output token limit, so its arguments may be truncated. Re-issue the tool call with complete arguments.
- Other fixed strings:
  - Tool <name> not found
  - Operation aborted
  - Tool execution was blocked
- createErrorToolResult = {content:[{type:text,text}], details:{}}.
- Tool result message key order: role, toolCallId, toolName, content, details, usage(optional), isError, timestamp(ms).
- streamAssistantResponse:
  - The partial message is pushed into context.messages and replaced on each update. Events carry shallow copies; in Go deep-copy content slices.
  - The final message is annotated with thinkingLevel = config.reasoning ?? off via Object.assign, so the key lands LAST in JSON (after timestamp) unless it was already present. Rust/Go struct field order must not silently move it; this affects session JSONL byte-compat.
- normalizeContext, toToolDeclaration, getCurrentTools and getToolStateChanges come from the ai port; use them, do not duplicate.

TESTS AND PACKAGING
- agent-loop.test.ts uses a MockAssistantStream built on EventStream. Port it with an in-memory stream helper.
- index.ts becomes lib.rs / package doc. It re-exports modules from agent-agent-proxy; add those mod declarations when that unit lands.
- README/CHANGELOG/package.json/tsconfig/vitest.config are carried over as crate/module docs and metadata. vitest.config aliases pi-ai to source; this has no native equivalent and needs none.

units.title: Stateful Agent class and proxy stream function
skipped_tests: packages/agent/test/utils/get-current-time.ts -- not imported by any test; relies on Intl toLocaleString time-zone formatting
packages/agent/test/utils/wait-for-tick.ts -- not imported by any test
units.notes:
AGENT CONSTRUCTION
- Defaults:
  - convertToLlm keeps roles system/user/assistant/toolResult.
  - streamFn falls back to getDefaultStreamFn().
  - steering/followUp mode one-at-a-time; transport auto; toolExecution parallel.
  - DEFAULT_MODEL has id/name/api/provider unknown and contextWindow 0.
- Initial state: if messages[0] is not a system message, prepend createInitialSystemMessage(systemPrompt, tools.map(toToolDeclaration)).
- The systemPrompt getter reads getCurrentSystemPrompt.
- reset() keeps getCurrentSystemMessage as the baseline.

LISTENERS AND STATE
- subscribe listeners are invoked sequentially and each is awaited with the active AbortSignal.
  - Rust: Vec<Arc<dyn Fn(AgentEvent, CancellationToken) -> BoxFuture<()>>> behind a mutex; never hold the state lock across await.
  - Go: func(ctx, AgentEvent), called serially from the run goroutine.
- processEvents reduces state:
  - streamingMessage
  - messages pushed on message_end
  - pendingToolCalls as a copied set
  - errorMessage taken from turn_end
  - It throws Agent listener invoked outside active run if there is no run.

PROMPT AND CONTINUE
- prompt accepts a string+images, a message, or an array.
- Exact error strings:
  - Agent is already processing a prompt. Use steer() or followUp() to queue messages, or wait for completion.
  - No messages to continue from
- continue() when the last message is an assistant message drains steering (skipInitialSteeringPoll) and then follow-up; otherwise it throws the matching error.

RUN LIFECYCLE
- runWithLifecycle owns an AbortController. Map it to a CancellationToken / context.CancelFunc.
- handleRunFailure emits a synthetic assistant message (message_start, message_end, turn_end, agent_end) with stopReason aborted or error and errorMessage.
- waitForIdle resolves after agent_end listeners finish.
- createLoopConfig forwards sessionId, onPayload, onResponse, onProviderStreamEvent, transport, thinkingBudgets, maxRetryDelayMs. It wraps prepareNextTurn / prepareNextTurnWithContext to inject the agent signal.

PROXY
- POST {proxyUrl}/api/stream with Authorization: Bearer and body {model, context, options}. Options is a whitelist: temperature, samplingParams, maxTokens, reasoning, cacheRetention, sessionId, headers, metadata, transport, thinkingBudgets, maxRetryDelayMs.
- Non-OK responses: Proxy error: <status> <statusText>, or Proxy error: <data.error> when the body is JSON with an error field.
- SSE parsing:
  - Split on newlines, keep the trailing partial line, flush the last unterminated line at EOF, accept only lines prefixed with data: .
  - Decode UTF-8 in streaming fashion: Rust bytes_stream plus a manual utf8 carry buffer; Go bufio.Reader.
- Partial message key order: role, stopReason(pending), content, api, provider, model, usage, timestamp.
- toolcall_delta uses parseStreamingJson from ai.
- toolcall_end merges the provider toolCall object over the partial one, keeping extra provider keys such as namespace and existing key order, and deletes partialJson.
- Fixed strings:
  - EOF without done/error: Connection closed by proxy server before the response completed
  - Abort: stopReason aborted with Request aborted by user
- done/error carry an optional providerThinkingLevel.

TESTS
- proxy.test stubs global fetch. Natively, inject an HTTP client or use a local server (axum / httptest). Regression for issue #8996 must be kept with its issue comment.
- e2e.test uses the faux provider (registerFauxProvider, fauxAssistantMessage) from ai compat. It is NOT a real-provider e2e test: port it once ai faux exists.
- calculate.ts evaluates expressions with new Function; replace it with a tiny arithmetic evaluator (Rust meval/evalexpr or hand-written; Go hand-written or govaluate).
- agent.test uses compat getModel and models.generated; depends on the ai model registry port.

units.title: Telemetry span API, NOOP and in-memory recorder, conformance suite
units.notes:
API
- AttributeValue = string | f64 | bool | Vec<string> | Vec<f64> | Vec<bool>. Attributes with value undefined are skipped when copying.
- TelemetryContext.startSpan(options, callback) returns the callback result.
  - Rust: async fn start_span<T, F: FnOnce(Span) -> Fut>(&self, opts, f) -> Result<T>, with an object-safe dyn variant using boxed futures.
  - Go: StartSpan(ctx, opts, func(Span) (any, error)) or a generic helper function.
- Admission (the parent-settled check, span id and start sequence) happens synchronously at call time, before the callback runs.
- NOOP: a frozen noop span. The callback runs synchronously, and a synchronous throw becomes a rejected promise. In Rust/Go just return the error; optionally recover panics in Go.

IN-MEMORY RECORDER
- Span ids start at 1. Global start/end sequence counters; endSequence is assigned at settlement.
- setAttributes merges atomically (all or nothing on a validation failure).
- An explicit setStatus wins over the automatic status. The automatic error status is {status:error, error:{name,message}} and applies only to Error instances. Natively, define a NamedError trait / interface (Rust: name() default Error; Go: errors.As against an interface with Name()) so name stays deterministic.
- Children of a settled parent become noop spans.
- getSpans returns detached deep copies.

TYPED SCHEMAS
- defineTelemetrySchema / createTypedSpanStarter are pure type-level machinery (InferStartAttributes, UniqueTelemetrySchemas) with no runtime validation.
- Rust: a macro or generic struct implementing a ToAttributes trait. Go: generic StartTyped[T Attributes].

TESTING MODULE
- testing/ is a public conformance suite consumed by other packages' tests.
- Rust: pub mod testing behind a cargo feature. Go: a telemetrytest subpackage returning []Case.

TESTS
- telemetry.test.ts expectTypeOf blocks are compile-time assertions. Replace them with compile tests or drop them.
- Conformance cases that use JS Proxy unreadable objects (throwing getters) have no native analogue. Drop them or model them via a failing ToAttributes implementation.

CONSUMERS
- ai/src/types.ts (telemetryContext option) and ai/src/api/simple-options.ts.
- Port this unit before the ai provider layer, or stub it.

units.title: Strict CBOR codec, length framing, protocol message schemas and validated codecs
units.notes:
Hand-port the CBOR codec; do not use ciborium or fxamacker/cbor, because the exact encoding and rejection rules are byte-observable.

ENCODER
- Major type 0/1 is used only for finite numbers with Number.isInteger and not -0. Values beyond ±2^53-1 are rejected (Decoded CBOR integer is outside the safe range / encoder equivalent). Every other number is float64 (0xfb), including -0, 1.5 and integral values above the safe range.
- writeArgument always picks the minimal-length argument (1/2/4/8 bytes).
- Strings must be valid Unicode scalars (lone surrogates are impossible in Rust/Go strings; Go must still reject invalid UTF-8 bytes in a string).
- Byte strings (Uint8Array) are major 2.
- Arrays: dense, no undefined elements.
- Maps: plain objects only. Keys in JS own-key order: integer-like keys (canonical array index strings < 2^32-1) ascending first, then insertion order. Entries with undefined values are skipped.
  - The native value model needs an ordered map AND must emulate the integer-key-first ordering when encoding values originally produced by JS. Decoded maps keep wire order.
- Cycles rejected (impossible natively).
- Output is capped by maxByteLength with the same errors (Unsupported CBOR value type, etc.).

DECODER
- Definite lengths only. Rejects:
  - tags
  - float16/32
  - undefined (0xf7) and other simple values
  - non-string map keys
  - duplicate keys
  - non-finite float64
  - float64 that should be ints? (verify encoder/decoder symmetry rules in decoder.ts)
  - trailing data
  - truncation
- Limits: maxByteLength 16 MiB, maxContainerEntries 1,000,000, maxDepth 64 (configurable maximum 512). options.ts RangeError text: <name> must be an integer between 0 and <maximum>.
- Text decoding: fatal UTF-8 with ignoreBOM, so a leading U+FEFF is preserved.
- __proto__ keys are data. Natively fine, but do not special-case them.

FRAMING
- 4-byte big-endian length prefix; zero-length frames are allowed.
- FrameDecoder states: open, ended, failed. Errors:
  - Frame decoder has ended
  - Frame decoder has failed
  - Frame length N exceeds configured limit of M
  - Truncated frame at end of stream
- Payloads are copied, not aliased. The TS decoder reads in 64 KiB blocks; this does not affect output.

CODEC
- parseClientMessage / parseServerMessage replace TypeBox Check with hand validators that reject additional properties, plus chord isJsonValue for the opaque call/result/update fields.
- ServerId: lowercase UUIDv4 regex. version is an integer >= 0. Request id has minLength 1. hello_error.code has minLength 1.
- response ok:true has an optional result; ok:false has error {code,message}.
- ValidatedMessageDecoder fails stickily with:
  - Invalid <kind> protocol frame: <msg>
  - Invalid <kind> protocol framing: <msg>
- boundedErrorMessage truncates at 500 chars (first 497 + ...). Count UTF-16 code units to match JS slice, or document the divergence.
- PROTOCOL_VERSION = 8. isSupportedProtocolVersion.

TESTS
- cbor.test has RFC 8949 Appendix A vectors plus rejection cases; port them verbatim as hex fixtures.
- Rust: the value model can be serde_json::Value with preserve_order, but numbers must be handled as f64 semantics (Number::from_f64) to make int-vs-float encoding identical. Go: decode to an ordered map type plus float64.

units.title: Protocol server, session router, Unix listener transport and testing harness
units.notes:
SERVER LIFECYCLE
- start(): listeners start sequentially; on failure, the started ones are closed and errors aggregated (AggregateError: Rust Vec<Error> wrapper; Go errors.Join).
- accept / close / closed future.

HANDSHAKE
- Timeout defaults to 5000 ms (unref'd timer, so it must not keep the process alive; with tokio this is automatic). On timeout it sends invalid_request Handshake timeout.
- The first message must be hello. Requests received before the handshake completes are queued. A second hello is a protocol error.
- A version mismatch gives code version with message: Unsupported protocol version X; expected 8.
- After hello it calls host.serverServices.attachClient(presentation{attachSession, detachSession, prepareSessionRemoval}, TODO_CONTEXT).
- failProtocol closes the connection after a FINAL hello_error frame (graceful end with final chunk).

REQUESTS
- Errors:
  - Duplicate active id: Request ID is already active
  - Invalid call: Invalid service call
  - Wrong server: WrongServerError
  - Cancel: code cancelled, message RPC request cancelled
- Context comes from chord withAbortSignal; port it on top of chord's native Context (Rust CancellationToken, Go context.Context).
- $chord.service control calls via decodeServiceControlCall:
  - Subscribe buffers updates until the subscribe response is sent, then installs createServiceStateEncoder per subscription.
  - Unsubscribe deletes the encoder.
- toProtocolError:
  - ServerError and RemoteServiceError codes pass through.
  - ProtocolValidationError becomes invalid_request.
  - Anything else becomes internal_error Internal server error (never leak messages).
- resolveOptions validation messages are preserved verbatim.

SESSION ROUTER
- runForClient chains operations per client. Rust: a per-client tokio Mutex or an mpsc actor; Go: a per-client goroutine or mutex.
- Attachments get randomUUID ids; publishAttachment sends attachment frames.
- releaseAttachment awaits in-flight operations, then lease.release. It is memoized (releasing promise; use Shared futures / sync.Once with a result).
- acquire shares an opening promise per session id.
- open closes the handle if the server is draining (SessionCleanupError aggregation).
- handle.terminated invalidates the session and releases all its attachments in the background.
- close aggregates errors: Failed to close routed Sessions.
- Client identity is an object reference; use an opaque ClientId.

UNIX LISTENER
- mkdir 0700.
- removeStaleSocket: probe-connect with 1 s timeout; if it fails with ECONNREFUSED, rename to stale-xxxxxx and verify the inode matches before unlinking.
- Bind to bind-<sha256(path) hex[0..8]> in the same dir, hard-link (fs.link) to the public path (atomic, fails if it exists), chmod 0600 (skipped on win32; ENOSYS/ENOTSUP ignored), then unlink the bind path.
- Cleanup renames to cleanup-xxxxxx after a dev/ino check.
- Rust: std::os::unix::net plus nix/rustix for link, lstat, chmod, and MetadataExt ino/dev. Go: syscall.Link, os.Lstat with Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t).
- UnixByteConnection:
  - pendingBytes limit; maxPendingBytes must be >= maxFrameLength + 4.
  - Serialized write tail.
  - Graceful close writes the final chunk then end, with a default 5000 ms timeout.
- getUnixSocketPath(directory, serverId) = <dir>/<serverId>.sock.

TESTING MODULE
- testing/ (ProtocolTestClient, connectUnixTestClient, TestServerHost, createTestServerServices with pi.session-management attach/detach, Deferred) is public API used by client tests and coding-agent experimental tests.
- Rust: export under a testing feature. Go: a servertest package.

TESTS
- unix.test forks fixtures/stale-socket-server.mjs over IPC and SIGKILLs it to leave a stale socket. Replace it with a helper process: Rust test binary re-exec with an env var or a small [[bin]]; Go TestMain helper-process pattern. Keep the .mjs only as reference.
- unix-connection.test mocks a socket with EventEmitter; use an in-memory duplex (tokio::io::duplex / net.Pipe).

units.title: Protocol client, connection state machine, Unix transport and server discovery
units.notes:
CLIENT
- The constructor validates serverId: serverId must be a canonical lowercase UUIDv4.
- Ids are counters: request-N and service-N.
- request(target, call, {signal}):
  - On abort it sends a cancel envelope and rejects with signal.reason or an AbortError. Map to a cancellation error type that carries the reason.
  - A response without a pending request fails the connection: Response has no matching request.
- Attachment frames for another server fail the connection.
- onConnectionStateChange / onAttachmentChange listeners.
- Service subscription flow:
  - The subscribe call returns a wire snapshot, parsed with parseWireServiceSubscriptionSnapshot.
  - service_update frames received before hydration are queued, then queued again until the consumer calls start(), then applied through createServiceStateDecoder.
  - Ordering must be preserved exactly. Use a per-subscription queue, not concurrent tasks.
- createClientServiceTransport adapts the client to chord RemoteServiceTransport; it depends on the chord native trait design.

CONNECTION
- States: disconnected, connecting, connected.
- maxFrameLength must be between 1 and 2^32-1.
- hello is sent after the transport opens. Data received before hello is sent fails the connection.
- Server hello serverId mismatch: Connected server X does not match Y.
- hello_error becomes ServerError(code, message). Other errors:
  - Unexpected handshake message
  - Byte transport closed (decoder.end errors take precedence)
- errors.ts: ServerError(code), DisconnectedError(cause), ClientDisposedError. Rust: a thiserror enum with source chain; Go: typed errors with Unwrap.

UNIX DISCOVERY
- discoverUnixServers({directory, timeoutMs=1000}):
  - Unsupported on win32 (throw).
  - readdir ENOENT returns [].
  - Candidates match <uuidv4>.sock and must be sockets per lstat.
  - At most 16 concurrent probes (Rust: Semaphore / buffer_unordered(16); Go: a semaphore channel).
- Each probe ignores (walking the cause chain):
  - timeout
  - ProtocolValidationError
  - DisconnectedError without cause
  - ServerError code version
  - ENOENT, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, EPIPE, ETIMEDOUT
  Rust: io::ErrorKind plus raw_os_error; Go: errors.Is with syscall.Errno.
- Results are sorted by serverId with localeCompare. Ids are lowercase hex UUIDs, so byte order equals locale order; plain string sort is fine.

UNIX TRANSPORT
- createUnixTransportFactory({path, maxPendingBytes = 4 * 16 MiB}).
- Serialized writes with a pending-bytes limit and drain waits.

TESTS
- client.test uses MemoryByteServer (support.ts); port it as an in-memory fake.
- unix.test imports server source and forks the .mjs fixture. Use the same helper-process approach as server-core-unix. Build after server-core-unix.

units.title: Coding-agent eval harness, local acme provider fixture, configured runtime helpers and eval suites
units.notes:
HARNESS
- Built on vitest-evals createHarness, normalizeHarnessRun and toJsonValue.
- Creates a coding-agent session: createAgentSessionServices, then createAgentSessionFromServices with SessionManager in memory, ModelRuntime, readStoredCredential to InMemoryCredentialStore, and getAgentDir.
- An InlineExtension uses before_agent_start to rewrite the system prompt. With native extensions this is a Rust trait / Go interface implementation registered in-process (allowed: it is not a user TS extension).
- applyIsolatedEnvironment: scrub env vars, temp HOME.
- Sandbox when running as root:
  - setgroups, setgid, setuid to an unprivileged id; chmod of vite SSR cache files.
  - Rust: nix::unistd::{setgroups,setgid,setuid}.
  - Go: syscall.Setgroups/Setgid/Setuid (Linux, Go >= 1.16 applies to all threads). Do the uid drop before spawning worker threads, or use a child process.
- seedWorkspace copies fixtures. promptAgent records usage, timings and the transcript.
- System prompt markers:
  - verifySystemPrompt expects \n<rules>\n and \n<docs>\nPi documentation (read only.
  - excludePiDocumentation cuts between \n<docs>\n and \n</docs>, before \n<cwd>\n.
  - These are tied to the coding-agent system-prompt port; keep them identical.
- DOCUMENTATION_EVAL_TOOLS = read, write, edit, grep, find, ls.
- PI_SESSION_SNAPSHOT_ARTIFACT comes from report.ts.

FIXTURES AND HELPERS
