hazards:
JSON key order is byte-observable in session JSONL and RPC:
- agent-loop appends thinkingLevel via Object.assign, so it lands after timestamp.
- Tool result order is role, toolCallId, toolName, content, details, usage, isError, timestamp.
- The proxy partial message has key order role, stopReason, content, api, provider, model, usage, timestamp.
- toolcall_end merges provider toolCall keys onto the partial.
Rust serde structs and Go structs serialize in declaration order. Either declare fields in the de-facto order or carry raw ordered maps; preserve_order / IndexMap are needed for passthrough values.

Absent vs undefined vs null:
- TS omits undefined fields when serializing and uses ?? merges, where null also falls back.
- AgentToolResult.details, structuredContent, usage and terminate need Option plus skip_serializing_if (Rust) or pointer / omitempty with care (Go), so null and absent stay distinguishable where JSON-visible.

Concurrency ordering that TS gets for free from a single-threaded event loop must be explicit:
- serialized event emission in parallel tool execution
- listeners awaited serially
- per-client operation chains in SessionRouter
- socket write tails
- subscription update queues buffered until hydrate and start
- EventStream FIFO
Do not emit events from multiple tasks or goroutines without a single ordered sink.

Parallel tool execution semantics:
- Preparation is sequential in source order, including beforeToolCall.
- Execution is concurrent.
- tool_execution_end is emitted in completion order; tool-result messages in source order.
- One sequential-mode tool forces the whole batch to sequential.
- terminate requires every result to set it.
- stopReason length fails all calls with a fixed message.

beforeToolCall may mutate validated args in place, and the mutated args are executed without revalidation (tested). The native API must hand out a mutable reference to the same value used for execution.
agentLoop in TS never ends the EventStream when runAgentLoop rejects. Native ports should close the stream with an error; document this as an intentional divergence.

CBOR number model:
- JS has only f64. Finite integral values that are not -0 and within ±(2^53-1) encode as major 0/1. Everything else is float64; -0 is float64.
- Decoded integers outside the safe range are rejected.
- Rust serde_json Number (u64/i64/f64) and Go float64/json.Number must be normalized to these semantics before encoding, or bytes will differ from the TS server/client.

CBOR map key order follows JS own-property order: canonical array-index keys ascending first, then insertion order. A native encoder fed from an ordered map must reorder integer-like keys to match JS when interoperating with JS peers or reproducing test vectors.

Strict UTF-8:
- fatal decoding with ignoreBOM, so a leading BOM is preserved.
- Encoder rejects lone surrogates (impossible in Rust; Go strings can hold invalid UTF-8 and must be validated).
- Error message truncation at 500 chars counts UTF-16 units in JS.

TypeBox Check is reimplemented by hand for protocol messages:
- additionalProperties false everywhere
- the ServerId UUIDv4 lowercase regex
- version integer >= 0
- id/code minLength 1
- the opaque call/result/update must pass chord isJsonValue (finite numbers, plain objects, dense arrays).

Error message strings are observable:
- wire hello_error and response errors
- test assertions
- RPC clients
Copy verbatim, including:
- Handshake timeout
- Unsupported protocol version X; expected 8
- Request ID is already active
- RPC request cancelled
- Internal server error
- Response has no matching request
- Connected server X does not match Y
- Frame length N exceeds configured limit of M
- Agent is already processing a prompt...
- Proxy error: ...

Unix socket specifics:
- bind to a hashed temp name, then hard-link to the public path (atomic no-clobber)
- chmod 0600, ignoring ENOSYS/ENOTSUP
- stale socket probe with a 1 s connect timeout, then rename to stale-xxxxxx with a dev/ino check
- inode-checked cleanup on close
- maxPendingBytes >= maxFrameLength + 4
- win32 unsupported (discovery throws)
macOS sun_path length limit (104 bytes) applies to temp paths in tests.

Unref'd timers (handshake timeout, probe timeout, close timeout) must not keep the process alive. In Rust use tokio::time inside the task; in Go use time.AfterFunc / context timeouts and make sure goroutines exit on close.

AbortSignal / DOMException AbortError semantics:
- Client.request rejects with signal.reason if one is set.
- The server maps cancel to code cancelled.
Map to CancellationToken / context.Context with a carried reason (context.Cause in Go).

AggregateError usage (server start failure, SessionRouter close/removeSession/release): Rust needs an aggregate error type; Go uses errors.Join or a custom type with a message prefix such as Failed to close routed Sessions.

Tests fork Node .mjs fixtures with IPC (client/server unix.test). Replace with a helper process (Rust re-exec of the test binary or a small bin target; Go TestMain helper-process) that signals readiness on stdout.

Telemetry: the automatic error status uses JS Error name/message; native errors need a deterministic name (NamedError trait/interface, default Error). Type-level schema inference and Proxy-based unreadable-attribute cases are not portable.

evals:
- Number formatting uses JS toFixed / toPrecision(15) and padStart. Implement JS-compatible formatters; Rust/Go rounding differs for some halfway cases.
- The report text uses ANSI bold.
- protocolDigest is sha256 over JSON.stringify output, so key order and number formatting must match JS.

evals sandboxing calls setgroups/setgid/setuid in-process as root. Go applies setuid to all threads only on Linux with Go >= 1.16. Rust must drop privileges before spawning threads (tokio runtime) or run the agent in a child process.
Agent test utils: calculate.ts uses new Function (needs a small arithmetic evaluator); get-current-time.ts uses Intl time-zone formatting but is unused and skipped.
The agent e2e.test.ts uses only the faux provider; it is not a real-provider e2e test. Port it after the ai faux provider and model registry (compat getModel) are available.
js_runtime_dependent: evals Docker image and entrypoint run vitest/vite over TypeScript *.eval.ts files and install packed TS release packages (install-runtime.mjs, Dockerfile npm ci/build:offline). Proposal: build the Rust/Go pi binaries in the image and replace vitest-evals with a native eval binary that compiles the suites in, writing a native report JSON that cli/report read.

evals harness rewrites the system prompt through an InlineExtension (before_agent_start). Proposal: implement it as an in-process native extension (Rust trait / Go interface) registered through the native SDK. This is allowed because it is not a user TS extension.

extensions.docs.eval.ts and the footer customization in tui.docs.eval.ts ask the model to write TypeScript extensions loaded by pi. User TS extensions are not loaded under the decisions. Proposal: rewrite these evals to target the native configuration/extension surface (settings, models.json, keybindings), or drop them and flag this to the user.
agent examples (mcp-codemode) execute model-written JavaScript through codemode. Proposal: run it via the quickjs-wasi WASM module under wasmtime (Rust) / wazero (Go), as decided for codemode.

agent CustomAgentMessages relies on TS declaration merging to extend AgentMessage. Proposal: a Custom variant carrying role plus ordered raw JSON (Rust enum variant / Go struct implementing the AgentMessage interface) that coding-agent's native custom message types convert to and from.

telemetry createTypedSpanStarter/defineTelemetrySchema type inference and expectTypeOf tests are compile-time TS only. Proposal: Rust macro or generic ToAttributes trait, Go generic helper; drop the expectTypeOf tests.
Test helper calculate.ts evaluates expressions with new Function. Proposal: a tiny native arithmetic parser in the test support module.

reports.summary:
Chord (packages/chord) is a standalone runtime for composing applications. It has about 8.8k source lines and no pi dependencies; esbuild is its only runtime npm dependency. Several packages consume it:
- durable persists delta Ops to JSONL/sqlite.
- protocol uses isJsonValue.
- server uses ServiceStateEncoder, ServiceCall and ServiceProviderUpdate over CBOR.
- coding-agent's experimental plugins use bundleFacetPackage, readFacetBundleArtifact and createFacetBundleLoader. Their facet entries are session and tui, and they ship presentationFacetBundles to clients.

The package has six layers.

1. Foundation
- types.ts holds every public interface for state, services, wire and facets.
- json.ts provides copyJson and isJsonValue. copyJson makes a strict copy with no shared references and rejects cycles, sparse arrays, accessors, symbols, non-plain objects and non-finite numbers.
- context/index.ts is a Go-style Context: a value chain plus an AbortSignal. It provides BACKGROUND and TODO, withContextValue, withAbortSignal (AbortSignal.any), withoutAbortSignal, withCancel and awaitWithContext. toString strings are exact.
- services/errors.ts defines RemoteServiceError with 8 string codes.

2. Delta protocol (delta/index.ts, diff.ts, apply-immutable-trusted.ts, revision-validator.ts)
- Ops are JSON tuples:
  - r: replace root
  - s: set at path
  - d: delete at path
  - a: append text
  - t: trim N UTF-16 units from the front of a string
  - p: splice
  - m: permute, where new[i] = old[perm[i]]
- Validation is strict:
  - The reserved segments __proto__, constructor and prototype throw UnsafePathError.
  - Array indices must be integers no greater than the length; violations throw PathError.
- Applying ops comes in three forms: mutable apply, copy-on-write applyImmutable/applyImmutableBatches, and a trusted fast path.
- The WireOp encoder/decoder is stateful, one pair per stream:
  - On a path's second use it emits ["#",id,path] and refers to the path by number afterwards.
  - Within a batch, an op omits its path when it repeats the previous op's path.
  - An r op resets both dictionaries.
- diffRevisions computes ops between two immutable revisions and depends on shared-reference identity:
  - Strings: append, or overlap-based t+a.
  - Arrays: positional match, then identity subsequence, LIS anchors and bounded semantic LCS, producing p ops; pure reorders become m.
  - A cost model falls back to r.

3. Tracker (delta/tracker.ts, 2205 lines)
- API:
  - track(value) returns a Tracker.
  - tracker.beginChange() returns a Change {state: Draft, prepare(), abort()}.
  - prepare() returns a Prepared {base, baseRevision, value, ops}.
  - Other entry points are adopt(prepared) (pointer swap) and prepareReplace.
- Draft is a copy-on-write Proxy overlay:
  - Each object node tracks its writes and deletes, plus a re-added set.
  - Each array uses a piece-table treap with deterministic xorshift priorities. Array mutators emit minimal p, m and s ops, and string edits emit a/t.
- Limits trigger a fallback to r: MAX_DELTA_OPERATIONS 4096, MAX_SIMPLE_OBJECT_NODES 128, and dense regions (at least 256 candidates at 50% density).
- A mutation under a reserved key becomes a set on the nearest safe ancestor.
- Change contexts are held as WeakRefs, pruned with a budget, and carry the status open, prepared, consumed, aborted or stale.

4. Replicated state and service provider (services/state*.ts, wire.ts, provider.ts)
- MutableReplicatedStateImpl wraps a tracker. change(fn) is synchronous: reentrancy and a returned Promise are rejected. A non-empty batch is published with sequence+1.
- Publishers send a hydration snapshot and then updates:
  - Exact-source listeners are called synchronously.
  - Public subscribers get a bounded async queue (100 entries) that coalesces on overflow.
- ReplicatedStateReplica enforces sequence continuity and validates every revision.
- RemoteServiceProvider:
  - It holds a catalogue of {serviceId, mode} with singleton or keyed instances; keyed instances have monotonic generations.
  - It classifies members from the sorted keys: a function is a method, a registered state is state.
  - subscribe returns an atomic snapshot and buffers updates until activate(). Update 101 becomes a reset, and snapshotSequences suppresses updates the snapshot already covers.
  - It also handles invoke (args plus a trailing Context) and replace, spawn and close.
- createRemoteServiceEndpoint serves the "$chord.service" control calls (catalogue, subscribe, unsubscribe) as well as plain calls.
- wire.ts has strict parsers with exact key sets.
- state-codec.ts converts Op updates to and from WireOp updates, with one codec per (instance, member) stream.

5. Consumer and facet host (consumer.ts, handle.ts, instances.ts, loopback.ts, facets/host.ts, api.ts)
- RemoteServiceBindingImpl turns a transport into stable Proxy facades:
  - Methods are callable MemberSlots.
  - State members expose .value and .subscribe backed by replicas.
  - Keyed services go through InstanceDirectory, with one cancellable observer task per instance.
  - It supports ready, rebind and dispose.
- FacetKernel:
  - Runs each facet's synchronous setup(env). The env provides use, observe, provide, provideMany, replicatedState, own, onActivate and onDeactivate.
  - Validates the dependency graph, rejecting duplicate providers, mode mismatches and cycles.
  - Resolves missing services from external RemoteServiceSources and activates facets in Kahn topological order.
  - Binds local singletons through ServiceSlot proxies, local keyed services through a registry, and remote-visible services through a provider plus a loopback binding.
  - reload() is a hot swap that keeps the service shapes, with a cutover step; a failure after cutover terminates the host.
- api.ts holds the public helpers: createFacetHost, combineFacetLoaders, createStaticFacetLoader, defineFacet, defineService and replicatedState.

6. Node bundles (node/*.ts)
- bundleFacets runs esbuild once per entry and emits CJS. Output files are named facet-<sha256(entry)[0:12]>-[hash].cjs.
- It writes chord-facets.json (format chord.facet-bundle, version 2) with sha256-base64 integrity, sorted external imports and optional source maps. The output directory is replaced atomically.
- bundleFacetPackage derives entries and externals from the package.json "chord" config and peerDependencies.
- createFacetBundleLoader verifies integrity and then executes the CJS with vm.compileFunction and a restricted require. Artifacts (a manifest plus inline file contents) can be materialized to a temp dir and loaded.
- This is the only code that executes JS at runtime.

Native plan
- JSON values:
  - Rust uses an enum with Arc-shared containers; Go uses pointer-backed nodes. Either way, identity checks must work.
  - Keys follow JS ordering: integer-like keys first, then insertion order.
  - Lengths are counted in UTF-16 units, and numbers are formatted the JS way.
- Draft becomes an explicit mutation API that feeds the same treap and object overlays, so the emitted ops are identical.
- Services become trait objects (Rust) or interfaces (Go), each with an explicit member table. Remote facades become dynamic handles with typed wrappers.
- Facets become a native Facet trait or interface.
- The bundle loader keeps the manifest and artifact formats and the integrity checks byte-compatible. Instead of executing JS, it resolves facets from a native registry keyed by plugin id and entry.
- Go can bundle with the esbuild Go API at the same version. Rust spawns the esbuild binary.

units.title: Chord foundation: public types, strict JSON, Context, errors, delta ops/apply/codec/diff
skipped_tests: packages/chord/test/boundary.test.ts -- scans the TS import graph for forbidden pi package imports. Replace it with a Cargo.toml/go.mod check that chord depends on no pi crate or module
units.notes:
Two outside imports come from re-exports. types.ts re-exports the RemoteServiceProvider type from provider.ts, and delta/index.ts re-exports track, Change, Prepared and Tracker from tracker.ts. Natively, split types.ts by domain (context, delta, state, services, facets) and keep the tracker as the submodule delta::tracker (Rust) or inside the same Go package delta.

JSON value model
Rust: enum Value { Null, Bool, Number(f64), String(Arc<str>), Array(Arc<Vec<Value>>), Object(Arc<ObjMap>) }. Use Arc::ptr_eq for the `===` identity checks that diffRevisions, applyImmutable sharing and JsonRevisionValidator caching depend on.
Go: Value as an interface holding *Array / *Object pointer types, so pointer equality gives identity.

Object key order
The map must reproduce JS own-key order. Canonical array-index keys ("0" up to 2^32-2) come first in ascending numeric order, then the other keys in insertion order. This order decides the order of emitted ops and the serialized bytes. Use a custom IndexMap wrapper (Rust) or an ordered map (Go).

Numbers
Serialization must match JS Number#toString: ryu-js in Rust. In Go, strconv 'g' output differs, so write a port of the JS shortest-roundtrip formatting. -0 serializes as 0.
Path checks use Number.isInteger semantics, so a parsed 1.0 is a valid index.

Strings
The counts in a/t ops, overlap(), and the jsonCost used by diffRevisions are in UTF-16 code units. Compute UTF-16 offsets explicitly (encode_utf16 in Rust, utf16.Encode in Go). A t op that splits a surrogate pair is representable in JS but not in UTF-8. Either use a WTF-8 / Vec<u16> string representation in the delta layer or reject such ops with an error, and document the divergence.

diffRevisions constants must match exactly: overlap scan 65536, probe 64, max 8 candidates; MAX_IDENTITY_CANDIDATES 200000 with a greedy fallback; MAX_SEMANTIC_CELLS 65536; delta-cost threshold 65536 versus jsonCost(after)+6. Tests assert exact op arrays.

Wire encoder/decoder
The path dictionary key is JSON.stringify(path). The order of #-definition ops and short-form omission must match byte-for-byte because they cross CBOR. apply splices in chunks of 10000; this is irrelevant natively.

copyJson
Rejects non-finite numbers, sparse arrays and non-plain objects. In a native immutable tree, cycles, accessors, symbols and null-prototype cases cannot occur. Skip the json.test cases about __proto__ own properties and null prototypes, but keep the rejection of RESERVED_SEGMENTS (__proto__/constructor/prototype) in paths.

Context
Rust: Arc<ContextNode> with parent links, value entries keyed by a unique ContextKey id, and a tokio_util CancellationToken plus a stored abort reason.
Go: wrap context.Context, using WithCancelCause for reason propagation and a value chain for keys.
Preserve the toString formats exactly: "[Context BACKGROUND_CONTEXT]", "<parent>.WithValue(<desc>)" and the others.
awaitWithContext maps to tokio::select! (Rust) or select on ctx.Done() (Go). It rejects with the reason when the reason is an Error, otherwise with an AbortError.

Other types
The type-only RemoteServiceContract check becomes trait bounds, or has no native equivalent.
RemoteServiceError codes must be the exact strings.
The package.json exports (., ./context, ./delta, ./bundler, ./node) map to Rust modules and Go subpackages.

units.notes:
Native ports have no Proxy, so Draft<T> becomes an explicit mutation API over node handles.
Rust: `change.state()` returns a DraftObject/DraftArray/DraftValue view with get/set/delete/keys/len, the array mutators (push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, reverse, sort_by, fill, copy_within) and string helpers (append, set_text).
Go: the same as methods on *DraftNode.
These API calls must update the same internal structures as the JS Proxy traps, so the emitted ops match exactly. Tests assert exact op arrays, such as ["t",["text"],3] and ["a",["text"],"xyz"].

Port the following exactly:
- The piece-table treap: base and insert pieces with step +/-1.
- The xorshift priority generator seeded with 0x9e3779b9. Use u32 wrapping arithmetic to reproduce JS `>>>0`, `<<` and `^` on int32 (Rust: wrapping ops; Go: uint32).
- The emission order: remove runs, then the permutation (m), then insert runs, then overrides.
- Dense-region detection: at least 256 candidates at density 50% or more.
- MAX_DELTA_OPERATIONS 4096 and MAX_SIMPLE_OBJECT_NODES 128, both falling back to r.
- The rule that a mutation under a reserved key folds into an s op on the nearest safe ancestor.

Materialization uses applyImmutableTrusted, except batches containing p or m, which go through applyImmutable. Untouched subtrees must stay shared (Arc / pointer identity), because diff identity anchors and tests rely on it.

clonePlacement validates placed values through copyJson (alias-free). Natively, values are immutable and shared, so the placement copy can become structural sharing, but validation (non-finite numbers) must remain.

Change lifecycle
Status is open, prepared, consumed, aborted or stale. Reusing a stale handle must throw with the same messages. Do not port the WeakRef context registry with its prune budget of 256 literally:
- Rust: Weak<RefCell<ContextState>> or generation ids in an arena.
- Go: an epoch counter on the tracker, with handles holding the epoch and checking it. Go 1.24 weak.Pointer is optional.

Test porting
tracker.test.ts (1454 lines) has many JS-only cases: property descriptors, prototype behaviour, Reflect and generic receivers, valueOf coercion order, `then` lookups, isProxy, Array.isArray, and JSON.stringify through the proxy. Skip those subcases. Port lifecycle, emission, safety, splice/permutation, text and root-array cases.
In delta-apply-immutable.test.ts, skip the Object.keys monkeypatch and frozen-object cases.
In delta-clone.test.ts and state-value.test.ts, skip the isFrozen, accessor and null-prototype parts; keep the alias-freedom and validation parts.
state-fuzz.test.ts uses a seeded mulberry32 PRNG with seeds 1..100: `seed=(seed+0x6d2b79f5)|0`, Math.imul. Port the PRNG exactly so the fuzz sequences match.

units.title: Chord replicated state, wire parsers/codec, RemoteServiceProvider and endpoint
units.notes:
The tests import the replicatedState() and defineService() helpers from src/index.ts, which lives in api.ts in chord-services-consumer-facets. Natively, either build MutableReplicatedState and Service tokens directly in the tests, or define those two constructors in this unit's module.

State delivery semantics
- Publisher sequence 0 is the hydrate.
- Publications go into a FIFO queue; a publish from inside a listener is queued, not nested.
- Exact-source listeners are called synchronously.
- Public subscribers have a 100-entry pending cap. On overflow the queue keeps an unstarted hydration plus the newest delivery.
- Async listeners deliver one at a time.
- Errors go to onError, otherwise they are rethrown from a queueMicrotask.
- MutableReplicatedStateImpl.change rejects reentrancy and a PromiseLike return with a TypeError, and does not publish when the change is a no-op.
- AttachedReplicatedStateImpl fails and disposes when it detects a cursor gap.
- ReplicatedStateReplica:
  - Hydrate requires a base batch.
  - Update requires sequence+1; otherwise it clears and throws.
  - Every revision is validated.

Rust
These semantics assume a single-threaded event loop. Run them on a tokio current_thread runtime with a LocalSet and Rc<RefCell> registries, or use Arc<Mutex> with care that locks are never held across listener calls. Model the microtask rethrow as an error sink.

Go
Use a mutex-protected publisher with a goroutine per async subscriber drain.

The JS tests flush microtasks with `await Promise.resolve()`. Rewrite them with explicit flush or yield helpers, or with channels and wait-for.

state-internals.ts is a WeakMap registry from a state object to its internals (snapshot, subscribe). Natively, ReplicatedState is a concrete type that exposes internals through a crate-private trait (Rust) or an unexported interface (Go).

Provider
- Subscription:
  - The snapshot is atomic; updates buffer until activate().
  - Update 101 replaces the queue with {type:"reset",snapshot}.
  - snapshotSequences suppresses updates already covered by the snapshot.
- Keyed generations increase per key.
- Keyed snapshot instances are sorted with localeCompare. This needs ICU root collation: icu_collator (Rust), golang.org/x/text/collate with language.Und (Go).
- Member classification uses Object.keys(impl).sort(), which sorts by UTF-16 code units. Natively, implementations register an explicit member table (name to Method(async fn(args, ctx)) or State(handle)) sorted by UTF-16 code-unit order.
- invoke appends the Context as a trailing argument.
- createRemoteServiceEndpoint swallows publish failures.

Wire
- The control serviceId is "$chord.service", with members catalogue, subscribe ([subscriptionId, serviceId, mode]) and unsubscribe.
- Parsers use exact key sets and their error messages are asserted. Parse from a generic JSON value rather than relying on serde/encoding/json struct decoding.
- Integer rules: update sequence >= 1, snapshot sequence >= 0, generation >= 1.
- A reset must contain exactly one r op per member.

Serialization field order is part of the wire format and must be preserved:
- ServiceCall: {serviceId, instance?, member, args}
- update: {type, instance?, member, sequence, ops}
- snapshot: {serviceId, mode, instances:[{instance?, members:[{name, kind, sequence, ops}]}]}
Optional fields are omitted, never null. In Rust, use declared field order with skip_serializing_if. In Go, use struct field order with omitempty, or a custom marshaller where a zero value is legal.

state-codec
The codec registry key is JSON.stringify([key??null, generation??null, member]); a tuple key works natively. Codecs reset on snapshot, reset, replaced and unavailable. On closed, only that instance's codecs are removed.

units.title: Chord service consumer binding, service slots, instance directory, FacetKernel host and public API
skipped_tests: packages/chord/test/services.test.ts (case 'checks remote JSON contracts only at compile time') -- uses @ts-expect-error to check TS types; natively this is enforced by trait bounds or has no equivalent
units.notes:
Consumer facades
In JS these are dynamic Proxies: methods are callable MemberSlots that require a trailing Context, and state members expose .value and .subscribe.
Rust: a RemoteServiceHandle with `call(member, Vec<Value>, &Context) -> impl Future<Output=Result<Value>>` and `state(member) -> StateView`. Add a macro (for example chord_service!) that generates typed wrappers per contract.
Go: a *RemoteFacade with Call(ctx, member, args...) and State(member).
Facades must stay stable across rebind and provider replacement. They are cleared on unavailable or disconnect, and later access throws the same RemoteServiceError codes. isContext is a duck-type check for the trailing argument; natively the argument is typed.

KeyedBinding uses revision fencing: an update with a stale generation is dropped. InstanceDirectory runs one observer task per instance under withCancel(BACKGROUND) and reports errors only if that context was not aborted. In Rust, use a tokio task with a CancellationToken. In Go, use a goroutine with context.WithCancel.

ready() loops until the readiness revision is stable. dispose aggregates errors; AggregateError becomes a multi-error type (Rust: a Vec in a custom error; Go: errors.Join).

ServiceSlot (handle.ts)
In JS, ServiceView/ValueView proxies give a stable facade over a mutable implementation pointer, guarded by assertAccess.
Rust: Arc<ArcSwapOption<dyn T>> (or RwLock) plus a lifecycle phase check.
Go: generic ServiceSlot[T] with atomic.Pointer and a phase check.
Error strings are asserted, for example "Facet ${id} service handles cannot be used while setting_up".

FacetKernel
- Phases: setup, assembling, connecting, activating, active, reloading, disposing, dead.
- setup must be synchronous. Rust: `fn setup(&self, env: &mut FacetEnvironment) -> Result<()>`. Go: `Setup(env *FacetEnvironment) error`. onActivate and onDeactivate register async callbacks.
- validateFacets rejects duplicate providers, mismatched modes and cycles.
- Activation uses a Kahn topological sort. Its tie-break order must match declaration order, because tests assert activation and disposal order. Facets are retired in reverse.
- own() disposables run LIFO.
- External sources come from catalogues; a source with acceptsUnavailableServices is the deferred source.
- Remote provisions go through a provider plus a loopback binding. Local singletons go into a ServiceSlot; local keyed services go into LocalKeyedServiceRegistry.
- reload is a shape-preserving replacement: validate candidates, including remote member shapes; activate them; cut over singletons via provider.replace; then retire the old facets in reverse. A failure after cutover terminates the host; a failure before cutover keeps the old generation.

combineFacetLoaders loads in order. On failure it disposes the facets already loaded in reverse and raises a multi-error. disposeLoadedFacets uses allSettled semantics.

defineService rejects an empty id and any id starting with '$chord.', and returns a frozen {id, local}. Natively this is a Service<T> token struct holding an id and a local flag.

index.ts is the public surface; it maps to lib.rs or the root chord.go re-exports. The tests rely on vi.fn spies and microtask flushing; replace them with recording closures and explicit flushes.

units.title: Chord facet bundle manifest, esbuild bundler, package resolver, and bundle/artifact loader
skipped_tests: packages/chord/test/bundle.test.ts (cases 'builds independent content-addressed entries and loads fresh reloadable generations', 'loads host externals through the controlled CommonJS require', and the invalid-module-export half of 'rejects corrupt entries and invalid module exports') -- these execute bundled JS via vm.compileFunction; native loaders do not run JS. Port their manifest, file naming and integrity assertions only
units.notes:
Formats must stay byte-compatible.

Manifest
- Constants: format "chord.facet-bundle", formatVersion 2, file name "chord-facets.json".
- Content: {format, formatVersion, plugin:{id, version?}, entries:{name:{file, integrity:"sha256-<base64>", externalImports:[sorted, deduped], sourceMap?}}}.
- Written as JSON.stringify(manifest,null,2)+"\n". Entries are sorted with localeCompare (ICU collator).

Artifact
- Format "chord.facet-bundle-artifact", version 2.
- coding-agent sends artifacts in JSON as presentationFacetBundles, so keep their fields and order the same.
- Validators reject unknown fields with exact messages.

Output file names are facet-<sha256hex(entryName)[0:12]>-[esbuild hash].cjs, with an optional .map.

Atomic output replacement
1. Build into the temp dir .<name>.tmp-<uuid>.
2. Rename any existing output to .<name>.old-<uuid>.
3. Rename the temp dir into place.
4. Remove the backup.
On Windows, a directory rename over an existing path fails, which is why the backup step exists; keep it.

esbuild options must stay identical so that hashes match:
- absWorkingDir, bundle true, format cjs, banner js '"use strict";', legalComments none
- entryNames facet-<hash12>-[hash]
- external = dedupe(['@earendil-works/chord','@earendil-works/chord/*', ...options.external])
- outExtension .js->.cjs, platform (default node)
- target: node22.19 for node, es2022 otherwise, or the user value
- supported {dynamic-import:false}, metafile true
- sourcemap 'external' or false, minify, define

Go: call github.com/evanw/esbuild/pkg/api at v0.28.2 with the same options. Map platform, target, Supported and OutExtension, and read Metafile JSON for imports with external=true.
Rust: there is no faithful crate. Spawn the esbuild 0.28.2 binary (resolve from node_modules/@esbuild/<platform>/bin/esbuild or PATH) with the equivalent CLI flags (--bundle --format=cjs --banner:js=... --entry-names=... --out-extension:.js=.cjs --supported:dynamic-import=false --metafile=...). If esbuild is unavailable, return an explicit unsupported error.
Integrity is sha256 of the file bytes, base64 encoded.

package.ts (bundleFacetPackage)
- Reads package.json name, version and peerDependencies (keys sorted) and the 'chord' config {facets, external, sourceMap}; unknown fields are rejected.
- Externals are the peers plus '<peer>/*'.
- Default entries apply only when the file exists. Configured entries override them, and false removes one.
- Path escapes are checked with realpath (Rust std::fs::canonicalize, Go filepath.EvalSymlinks + Abs).
- coding-agent passes DEFAULT_PLUGIN_FACETS {session:'src/session.ts', tui:'src/tui.ts'}.

Loaders
- readFacetBundleManifest and readFacetBundleArtifact port 1:1: validation and integrity verification.
- createFacetBundleLoader and createFacetBundleArtifactLoader cannot execute CJS natively. Port them as loaders that:
  1. validate the manifest or artifact,
  2. verify integrity,
  3. optionally materialize the artifact into a mkdtemp 'chord-facet-' directory,
  4. resolve facets from a NativeFacetRegistry keyed by (plugin.id, entryName),
  5. return an explicit error when no native facet is registered.
- Keep facetsFromModule's validation (unique ids, setup present) for registry results.
- resolveExternalTarget, validatePackageSpecifier and isBuiltin exist only for the JS require path. Keep validatePackageSpecifier for manifest validation, because externalImports must be valid specifiers.

hazards: Delta Ops are persisted by packages/durable (JSONL and sqlite) and sent over CBOR by packages/server via ServiceStateEncoder. Five things must match TS byte for byte: op tuple shapes, the encoder interning order (['#',id,path] on a path's second use, then numeric refs), short-form path omission within a batch, the dictionary reset on r, and JSON number formatting.

Tests assert exact op arrays from the tracker and from diffRevisions. To match, port these exactly: the treap priority PRNG (xorshift seeded 0x9e3779b9, u32 wrapping), the dense-region heuristics (256 candidates, 50% density), the limits (4096 ops, 128 simple-object nodes), and the diff constants (overlap 65536/64/8, identity candidates 200000, semantic cells 65536, cost threshold 65536 vs jsonCost+6).

JS own-key ordering puts integer-like keys first in ascending order, then other keys in insertion order. It affects op emission order, Object.keys().sort() member classification (UTF-16 code-unit compare), and serialized JSON. Native maps must emulate it.

String lengths and offsets in a/t ops, overlap() and jsonCost are UTF-16 code units. A t op can split a surrogate pair in JS, which UTF-8 strings in Rust and Go cannot represent. Use WTF-8 or u16 storage in the delta layer, or reject such ops explicitly.
localeCompare (ICU root collation) orders keyed instance snapshots and manifest entries. Plain byte or code-unit sorting changes the output when keys contain mixed case, punctuation or non-ASCII.

Identity semantics: diffRevisions anchors, applyImmutable structural sharing, the JsonRevisionValidator cache and tracker adoption all depend on `===` identity of containers. Natively, use Arc::ptr_eq (Rust) or pointer equality (Go). Deep-cloning values breaks diff quality and test expectations.

Ordering depends on the microtask queue. State delivery calls exact-source listeners synchronously, queues reentrant publishes FIFO, and drains async subscribers in sequence. Provider subscription buffering, activate() and the reset at update 101 depend on it, as does rethrowing listener errors from a queueMicrotask. Natively, use a single-threaded executor or careful locking; locks must never be held across listener callbacks.

Error message strings, AggregateError composition and RemoteServiceError codes are asserted in tests. Examples: 'Facet ${id} service handles cannot be used while setting_up', UnsafePathError and PathError messages, and parser unknown-key messages.

Wire JSON field order and omission: ServiceCall {serviceId, instance?, member, args}; update {type, instance?, member, sequence, ops}; snapshot {serviceId, mode, instances}. Optional fields are omitted, not null. Parsers reject unknown keys and enforce integer bounds (update sequence >= 1, snapshot sequence >= 0, generation >= 1).

Manifest and artifact JSON must be written as JSON.stringify(x,null,2)+'\n', with the same key order and optional sourceMap/version omission. coding-agent ships artifacts to clients as presentationFacetBundles.

Atomic directory replacement uses .tmp-<uuid> and .old-<uuid> renames. Windows rename semantics and cross-device renames differ, and the realpath-based escape checks must canonicalize the same way on macOS (/private/var) and Windows.
Rust has no faithful esbuild. Unless the esbuild 0.28.2 binary with the same flags is used, output file names (which embed esbuild's [hash]) and integrity values will differ from TS-produced bundles.

Context cancellation reasons: awaitWithContext rejects with the signal reason when it is an Error, otherwise with DOMException AbortError. withAbortSignal combines signals (AbortSignal.any), and the exact toString formats are asserted in tests.

Facet setup must stay synchronous, and activation order (Kahn sort with declaration-order tie-break) and reverse disposal order are asserted. Reload failure semantics also differ by phase: a failure before cutover keeps the old generation, while one after cutover terminates the host.

types.ts and delta/index.ts form import cycles with provider.ts and tracker.ts (type re-exports). Natively, split modules so there are no circular crate or package imports; Go forbids import cycles between packages.
js_runtime_dependent: node/bundle-loader.ts createFacetBundleLoader runs CJS facet bundles through vm.compileFunction with a restricted createRequire that maps @earendil-works/chord, chord/* and host externals such as @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/experimental/plugin. Native handling: keep manifest reading, validation and sha256 integrity checks, then resolve facets from a compile-time NativeFacetRegistry keyed by (plugin.id, entry). Return an explicit 'JavaScript facet bundles are not supported' error when no native facet is registered. User TS plugins are not loaded.

createFacetBundleArtifactLoader materializes an artifact (a manifest plus inline files) into a mkdtemp directory and executes it. Native handling: port materialization, integrity checks and cleanup, then use the same registry lookup. The presentationFacetBundles that coding-agent sends to clients become inert data for native clients.

resolveExternalTarget uses import.meta.resolve and isBuiltin to satisfy require() calls inside bundles. Native handling: drop it; keep only validatePackageSpecifier for validating externalImports in manifests.

node/bundle.ts and node/package.ts bundle TS facet sources with esbuild. Native handling: Go calls the esbuild Go API v0.28.2 directly with identical options, giving identical hashes and manifests. Rust spawns the esbuild binary with equivalent flags, or reports bundling as unsupported. This is needed only if pi-native must still produce bundles for TS clients.

The Draft<T> Proxy in delta/tracker.ts intercepts plain JS property and array operations. Native handling: an explicit draft API (Rust DraftObject/DraftArray handles inside a `change(|d| ...)` closure; Go *Draft methods) that drives the same overlay and treap structures, so emitted ops are identical.

Service facades (the MemberSlot and ServiceFacade Proxies in consumer.ts, the ServiceView and ValueView Proxies in handle.ts) and member classification by reflecting over Object.keys(impl). Native handling: an explicit member table registered per implementation, a dynamic RemoteServiceHandle (call(member, args, ctx), state(member)), and macro-generated typed wrappers in Rust or hand-written wrappers in Go. Local services become Arc<dyn Trait> or Go interfaces inside a stable ServiceSlot.

Facets are JS objects with setup(env), and loaders import modules. Native handling: a Facet trait or interface (id(), setup(&mut FacetEnvironment)) plus static loaders (createStaticFacetLoader, combineFacetLoaders) over natively constructed facets.

state-internals.ts keeps a WeakMap registry from a state object to its internals, and the tracker keeps WeakRef contexts with a GC-pruned budget. Native handling: a crate-private trait or unexported interface on the concrete ReplicatedState type, and epoch or Weak-based stale detection. The GC retention tests are skipped.

The type-level RemoteServiceContract check (@ts-expect-error tests) enforces at compile time that service args, results and state are JSON-compatible. Native handling: trait bounds such as Into<Value>/TryFrom<Value> in Rust, or runtime JSON validation at the provider boundary in Go.

reports.summary:
packages/durable (@earendil-works/pi-durable 1.0.0) is the durable runtime under the experimental durable agent in coding-agent (coding-agent/src/experimental/**). It has 59 TS source files (17,662 lines) and 6 subpath exports: ".", "./env", "./env/node", "./tools", "./storage/{memory,jsonl,jsonl/node,sqlite,sqlite/node}", "./testing". Dependencies: in-repo chord (delta ops, Draft tracking, Context/abort, replicated state) and pi-ai (message types, Models, the retry/overflow/estimate/transcript/validation utils), plus external diff 8.0.4 and typebox 1.3.27. Five layers follow.

1) Core model (src/types.ts and friends). These are plain JSON records, all keyed by one global numeric ID space; ROOT_CONVERSATION_ID = 1, minted IDs start at 2, and commit Seq starts at 1:
- ConversationRecord (forks: parent {conversationId, at}; ownership: owner {conversationId, taskId})
- EntryRecord (append-only, with optional head marker for resets)
- SubmissionRecord (input/write inbox lifecycle)
- TaskRecord (versioned state machine)
- DocumentRecord (session/conversation/task scope, singleton or keyed family, history latest|rewindable, fork asOf|current|initial)

Storage is a small async interface: commit(StorageWrite[]) -> Seq, mintId, point reads, and cursor scans. Entry scans walk fork ancestry newest-first, capped at each parent.at. Document reads take "current" or a historical Seq and rebuild the value from the newest base plus chord delta ops.

2) Session kernel (src/session). createSession wraps a Storage. One serialized mutation line runs commit callbacks against a Transaction (Tx):
- Table reads are banned after the first table write (ReadAfterWrite).
- Documents are staged through chord Tracker/Draft objects.
- checkpointWhen chooses a base or a delta.
- Fork document copies are planned (forks.ts).

The writes are then assembled into StorageWrite[] and committed. In-memory state is adopted only after the commit succeeds. Commit listeners are notified synchronously, and the session is poisoned on any storage error other than StorageRejected. observation.ts adapts committed state to chord ReplicatedStateSource; CommittedWatch serializes frames, capped at 100 pending before falling back to a snapshot.

3) Storage backends.
- MemoryStorage: detached, deep-frozen clones with sorted indices, plus a synchronous prepareCommit/apply.
- JsonlStorage: wraps MemoryStorage over the env FileSystem. It writes per-commit markers to main.jsonl and doc-<id>.jsonl / task-<id>.jsonl sidecars (format 1). Sidecars are written before the marker, with optional fsync. Superseded sidecars are reclaimed via a .reclaim temp file and rename. Recovery truncates torn tails and confirms sidecar records by (file, seq, ordinal).
- SqliteStorage: a portable SqliteDatabase facade with STRICT-schema migrations and JSON record columns. Indexed strings are JSON-encoded. document_revisions holds base/delta rows. node.ts adapts node:sqlite (WAL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, serial op queue, wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) on close).
- testing/: a runner-independent conformance suite (24 cases) shared by all three backends, plus benchmark seeding.

4) Harness (src/harness). Harness.open(storage, {models, registry, env?, settings}) extends the Session with built-ins:
- Documents: pi.agent, pi.live, pi.inbox, pi.usage
- Entries: pi.user, pi.assistant, pi.system, pi.tool-result, pi.reset, pi.compaction
- Tasks: pi.generation, pi.tool, pi.compaction

TaskScheduler (1337 lines) drives durable task state machines. States are pending/running/waiting/completing/terminal; outcomes are completed/failed/aborted/orphaned/faulted. It covers:
- phases, memos, abort marks, owned child tasks and conversations, cascades
- failFast/allSettled waits, idle waits
- migration of an old task version when it is reserved
- "no durable progress" faults

Each task type is one file:
- GenerationTask: prepare/request/retry/poll/tools phases; 100ms partial throttle; deferred polling; retry policy; threshold and overflow compaction.
- ToolTask: call/execute phases; replay safe/unsafe; beforeTool/afterTool hooks; head/tail output bounding with UTF-8 accuracy; adaptive Progress commits; diagnostics rendering.
- CompactionTask: select/summarize/retry; cut selection; summary placement through the inbox.

Submissions/inbox handle whenBusy steer/followUp/reject, postTools/final boundaries, stale-head detection, and requestId dedupe. The registry holds extensions (tools, prompt sections, hooks, wraps, task kinds) and resolves the per-conversation agent (model, thinking, tools, instructions). Observation provides watchEvents (an ordered AgentEvent stream), ConversationView mounts, and a TaskGraph replicated state.

5) Env and tools. ExecutionEnv = FileSystem + Shell, both Result-returning. NodeExecutionEnv resolves the shell (Git Bash on Windows), kills the whole process tree on abort or timeout, and spills large output to a temp file. Tools: read/write/edit/bash, a per-file mutation queue, jsdiff-based edit diffs, and image sniffing.

Port shape: one Rust crate pi-durable (modules mirror files; feature flags "node-env", "sqlite", "jsonl", "testing") and one Go module. In Go, core types, session, and harness must share one package because types.ts and harness/types.ts import each other. env, storage/jsonl, storage/sqlite, testing, and tools can be subpackages.

Order: core -> session -> memory storage + conformance -> jsonl/sqlite -> env/tools -> harness model -> scheduler -> tasks -> observation. Hard prerequisites from other areas:
- chord delta (Op apply, track/Draft, overlap), context (abort), and replicated state
- pi-ai faux provider, Models, utils

Byte compatibility hinges on JSON serialization:
- JSONL files and SQLite record and indexed-string columns must match JSON.stringify exactly: key order, number formatting, escaping.
- edit patches must match jsdiff.
- Error message strings are asserted by tests and persisted in task outcomes.

units.title: Core record types, storage/session/tx contracts, document/entry/task definitions, errors, IDs, public index, package assets
skipped_tests: packages/durable/test/storage-runtime-boundary.test.ts -- scans the TS import graph for node: imports; replace with a Cargo feature / Go build-tag compile check (portable modules must build without node-env/sqlite features)
units.notes: types.ts defines every persisted record plus the StorageWrite union (conversation | entry | task | submission | document.create | document.copy | document.change | document.retire), CommitPublication, and the Tx/Session/Storage interfaces. Use ID newtypes: Rust #[serde(transparent)] u64 for ConversationId/EntryId/TaskId<T>/SubmissionId/DocumentId/Seq; Go named int64 types. They must serialize as bare JSON numbers. Treat all IDs as JS safe integers: max 2^53-1, and 'ID space is exhausted' is checked against Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Discriminated unions use serde tag='type'/'status'/'kind'. Field order in Rust structs and Go structs must equal the JS object-literal construction order, because records go straight into JSONL/SQLite via JSON.stringify. Optional fields are omitted, never null: skip_serializing_if / omitempty with pointer types. documents.ts details: defineDoc/defineDocFamily validate that version is a positive safe integer. resolveAddress parses overloaded arguments; in native code, use explicit enum arguments. addressId = JSON.stringify([kind, scopeKind, owner|null, key|null]) is used as an in-memory map key only. materializeDocumentValue runs migrate(value, fromVersion) and then copyJson(omitUndefinedProperties). Error classes are StorageRejected, ReadAfterWrite (message "Tx.${method}() cannot read tables after the first table write"), and ConversationBusy ("Conversation ${id} is busy"). Tests check error.name === 'StorageRejected', so expose a stable kind/name. index.ts becomes lib.rs re-exports; in Go there are no re-exports, so document the root package API instead. types.ts imports harness/types.ts and harness/types.ts imports types.ts, a type-only cycle: fine in one Rust crate; in Go both must live in the same package. types.test.ts is mostly expectTypeOf type-level assertions; port only the runtime-observable parts (serde round-trips of each variant) and drop pure type tests. docs/*.md are reference assets; spec.md (4601 lines) is the normative behavior spec for the whole area.

units.title: Session kernel: mutation line, Transaction staging/assembly/adopt, fork document copies, committed-state observation
units.notes: SessionImpl serializes all commits through one promise-chain 'mutation line'. Port it as an actor: Rust tokio task + mpsc, or a Mutex held across the async commit; Go goroutine + channel or sync.Mutex. Commit ordering and publication must be FIFO and exact. The Transaction runs these steps: (a) table reads are allowed until the first table write, after which they throw ReadAfterWrite; (b) document access goes through chord track() Trackers giving Draft proxies (beginChange/prepare/adopt/abort); (c) assemble StorageWrite[] including fork copies, checkpointWhen base-vs-delta, version migration bases, and retirements; (d) storage.commit -> Seq; (e) adopt prepared trackers (pointer swap); (f) publish to commit listeners synchronously before the commit promise resolves. Non-StorageRejected storage errors poison the session; StorageRejected aborts only that commit. The Draft proxy is the hardest part. Rust/Go need chord's native tracked-mutation API (explicit set/insert/delete ops recorded as Op), and user callbacks get a typed draft wrapper. forks.ts: an asOf copy reads the parent document at the entry's commitSeq, from the conversation the entry belongs to; a current copy reads the parent's current value; initial gets the seed. observation.ts implements the chord ReplicatedStateSource/Attachment. CommittedWatch delivers exact frames serially; with more than 100 pending (MAX_PENDING_WATCH_FRAMES) it replaces the queue with a snapshot. Retirement is published as ops [["r", null]]. Watch tests depend on microtask ordering (flush helpers). In the ports, use explicit await points / channels and deterministic test hooks rather than sleeps. ControlledStorage in session-support.ts is a storage wrapper with gating hooks; port it as a test double implementing the Storage trait/interface. Examples are runnable scripts (not vitest); port as cargo examples / Go Example tests.

units.title: MemoryStorage and JSONL file storage (main marker + sidecars, reclaim, recovery)
units.notes:
MemoryStorage behavior:
- nextId starts at 2 and seq at 1.
- Records are stored as detached deep-frozen clones (null-prototype objects; defineProperty for __proto__ keys).
- Sorted id index arrays support scans.
- prepareCommit(writes) returns {writes, apply()}; apply is idempotent and returns the same Seq.
- Documents are kept as base + delta list per document, replayed with chord applyImmutableBatches.
- Validation messages: 'ID ${id} already belongs to ${type}', 'Document address already has a current incarnation', 'version transition requires a base', 'does not retain historical content'.

Native ports clone instead of freezing. The memory-storage test asserting that mutation of a prepared write throws is JS-specific; port it as 'prepared writes are not aliased'.

JSONL on-disk format must stay byte-compatible:
- File main.jsonl holds one line per commit: {"format":1,"type":"commit","seq":N,"writes":[...]}.
- conversation, entry, submission, and document.retire writes are inline. Terminal tasks are inline as {type:'task',value}.
- Non-terminal tasks go to task-<id>.jsonl, with {type:'task.sidecar',id,ordinal} in the marker.
- document.create and document.change go to doc-<id>.jsonl as {format:1,type:'record',seq,ordinal,payload:{type:'document',id,content}}, with {type:'document.create',record,ordinal} or {type:'document.change',id,ordinal} in the marker.
- Write order: sidecars first, flushed if fsync is set, then the main marker is appended.

Reclamation runs after publish, best-effort. Current-only documents (non-conversation scope or history 'latest') are rewritten to their latest base on a base change and emptied on retire; terminal tasks' sidecars are emptied. Each rewrite writes <file>.reclaim and then renames it over the sidecar.

Recovery:
- Truncate a torn final line.
- Decode UTF-8 fatally (invalid bytes raise JsonlCorruptionError).
- Confirm each sidecar record by key JSON.stringify([file,seq,ordinal]).
- Ignore or clean stray .reclaim files and unreferenced sidecars matching /^(doc|task)-(0|[1-9]\d*)\.jsonl$/.
- After a failed write the storage is poisoned (JsonlStoragePoisonedError 'JSONL storage is poisoned and must be reopened').

All file I/O goes through the ExecutionEnv FileSystem interface (appendFile, truncateFile, flushFile, renameFile, readTextLines, openTextLineReader), so the port depends on env/index. node.ts = openNodeJsonlStorage(dir) over NodeExecutionEnv(cwd=process.cwd()). jsonl-storage.test.ts writes crafted corrupt files; JSON output must match JS byte-for-byte for those fixtures to line up.

units.title: Portable SQLite storage: database facade, migrations, SqliteStorage, node:sqlite adapter
units.notes:
The schema must be byte-identical so existing DB files open:
- durable_metadata(singleton, next_id TEXT default '2', next_seq INTEGER default 1)
- durable_schema version table, with a contiguous-version check; reject a DB newer than the code
- record_ids(id, record_type)
- conversations(id, owner_conversation_id, owner_task_id, record)
- entries(id, conversation_id, head, commit_seq, record)
- tasks(id, conversation_id, kind, status, abort_requested, background, record)
- submissions(id, conversation_id, request_id, status, record)
- documents(id, kind, family, key_value, scope_kind, owner_id, created_at, retired_at, record)
- document_revisions(document_id, seq, kind, version, content)
- all STRICT, plus the indexes in INITIAL_SCHEMA

Indexed strings (task kind, request_id, document kind, key_value) are stored as JSON.stringify(value), which keeps lone surrogates lossless. owner_id is 0 for session scope. family is 1 when key !== undefined. key_value encodes "" when there is no key. The record column is JSON.stringify(record); revision content is the JSON base value or the JSON ops array.

commit runs one transaction:
- read metadata
- checkGlobalIds (conversation/entry/document IDs unique; task/submission may be upserted but not change type)
- checkDocumentActions (StorageRejected when a copy source is changed in the same batch; live-incarnation count per address)
- table upserts
- document actions: copy materializes the source inside the tx and is wrapped in StorageRejected on failure; current-only documents delete old revisions on base or retire
- metadata update

nextId is adopted in memory only after success. document() reads inside a transaction so the record and its revisions come from one committed state. admitRead counts multi-query reads, and close waits for them to drain.

node.ts adapter:
- DatabaseSync; mkdir of the parent dir
- PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, wal_autocheckpoint (default 1000), busy_timeout 5000
- BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK; on rollback failure throw AggregateError
- SerialOperationQueue: ops run in call order and wait behind an active tx; calls made synchronously from inside the tx join it; a tx handle used after settle rejects
- statement cache per connection (prepare once)
- close runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)

Rust: rusqlite (bundled) behind a tokio Mutex or a dedicated thread, using prepare_cached. Go: database/sql + modernc.org/sqlite with SetMaxOpenConns(1), or a single *sql.Conn guarded by a mutex; explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE via Conn.ExecContext. Tests assert EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN index usage, WAL file size after checkpoint, page reuse, and bounded DB size; these are sqlite-version-sensitive, so keep the same pragmas. Integer columns: SQLite INTEGER maps to i64; JS uses number, so stay within 2^53.

units.title: Storage conformance suite and storage benchmark seeding (public ./testing export)
skipped_tests: packages/durable/test/storage.bench.ts -- vitest bench timing harness; optional port as cargo bench (criterion) / go test -bench, not a correctness test
packages/durable/test/storage-memory.ts -- node --expose-gc heap measurement script for MemoryStorage scales; JS-heap specific
units.notes:
createStorageConformance returns 24 named cases, each run via withStorage(use). They cover:
- root ID reservation
- atomic mixed-table rollback
- detachment of written and read values
- __proto__/constructor keys
- out-of-order entry indexing
- cursor continuation after newer commits
- conversation owner scans
- deep fork history caps
- task replace and status scans
- request-ID index
- passive write submissions
- rewindable documents and half-open incarnations
- long tails across root-replacement deltas
- document.copy semantics with StorageRejected on ambiguous or mismatched source
- version-transition bases
- logical address and scope indexes
- create+retire empty lifetime
- rollback of secondary indexes
- lossless indexed strings with lone surrogates
- global ID namespace and exhaustion at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
- rejection after close

Rust: export `pub fn storage_conformance_cases() -> Vec<Case>`, where Case holds a name and an async fn(Box<dyn Storage>), plus a macro_rules! that generates one #[tokio::test] per case for each backend. Go: `func RunStorageConformance(t *testing.T, open func(t *testing.T) Storage)` using t.Run per case. The expect-adapter files (assertions.ts, runner.ts, types.ts) collapse into the native test frameworks. The prototype-pollution case reduces to 'keys named __proto__/constructor round-trip as ordinary keys' (needs an ordered map JSON object type in Go). The lone-surrogate case ("\ud800" vs "\ud801" as task kind/requestId/doc key) cannot be represented in Rust String or Go string via encoding/json; it needs a decision (see hazards). storage-benchmark.ts is public API (seedStorageBenchmark, STORAGE_READ_BENCHMARKS, STORAGE_WRITE_BENCHMARKS, STORAGE_MEMORY_SCALES, TIMING_SCALE); port it as data and functions so the bench ports can share it.

units.title: ExecutionEnv interfaces, NodeExecutionEnv (fs + shell), truncate utils, coding tools (read/write/edit/bash)
skipped_tests: packages/durable/test/fixtures/delete-buffer.ts -- deletes globalThis.Buffer to simulate a browser runtime; no native equivalent

packages/durable/test/fixtures/utf8-byte-length-without-buffer.ts -- subprocess fixture for the no-Buffer utf8ByteLength path; native ports have one UTF-8 length path (drop the matching env-truncate case)
units.notes:
env/index.ts:
- Result<T,E> = {ok:true,value} | {ok:false,error}. Map to Rust Result and Go (T, error) with typed *FileError / *ExecutionError.
- FileError codes: aborted, not_found, permission_denied, not_directory, is_directory, invalid, not_supported, unknown.
- ExecutionError codes: aborted, timeout, shell_unavailable, spawn_error, callback_error, unknown; carries an optional spillPath.
- FileSystem: about 20 async methods (absolutePath, joinPath, readTextFile, openTextLineReader, readTextLines, read/write/append/truncate/flush/rename, fileInfo, listDir, canonicalPath, exists, createDir, remove, createTempDir/File, cleanup).
- Shell.exec(command, {cwd, env, inheritEnv, timeout in seconds, onOutput, spill {afterBytes, afterLines}}).

NodeExecutionEnv (id 'node:local'):
- resolvePath expands ~ and accepts file:// URLs.
- errno codes map to FileError codes.
- Shell discovery: custom path; on Windows, Git Bash candidates then where/which; legacy WSL bash runs via stdin -s; otherwise /bin/bash, falling back to sh -c.
- Spawn detached (setsid/process group) and kill with kill(-pid, SIGKILL); on Windows use taskkill /F /T.
- Exit code = code ?? 128+signo ?? 1.
- Timeout validation (max 2147483647 ms); error message 'timeout:${timeout}'.
- After exit, wait a 100ms stdio grace, re-armed while spill is still draining.
- Spill to tmpdir/pi-output-<uuid>.log once afterBytes or afterLines is exceeded; 1 MiB high-water mark with pause/resume backpressure.
- NodeTextLineReader is strictly LF-delimited and reads 64 KiB chunks with positional reads.
- Missing cwd message: 'Working directory does not exist: ${cwd}\nCannot execute bash commands.'

Rust: tokio::process with process_group(0) + nix::sys::signal::killpg. Go: exec.Cmd with SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} + syscall.Kill(-pid); build-tagged Windows file.

truncate.ts: truncateHead never returns partial lines; byte counts are UTF-8; formatSize uses toFixed(1) with B/KB/MB.

Tools:
- Schemas are typebox Type.Object; port as literal JSON Schema with identical descriptions, since the tool declarations go to models.
- read: image sniffing (jpeg, non-animated png, gif, webp, bmp) returns an unsupported_image diagnostic; offset/limit continuation diagnostics; first-line-too-long path uses characterEnd from harness/output.
- edit: prepareArguments repairs edits sent as a JSON string, a single object, or a legacy top-level oldText/newText. Matching is exact first, then fuzzy (NFKC, trailing whitespace, smart quotes, dashes, unicode spaces) with preservation of untouched lines. BOM and CRLF are restored. details carry diff (custom numbered display) and patch (jsdiff createTwoFilesPatch with context 4, FILE_HEADERS_ONLY).
- bash: commandPrefix and prepare hooks; tail retention; full_output diagnostic.
- file-mutation-queue: a process-global map keyed `${env.id}\0${canonicalPath}`, with a canonical-parent fallback for files that do not exist yet. Rust: a static Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>; Go: a sync.Map of chans or mutexes.
- path-utils: unicode-space normalization, leading @ strip, and read fallbacks (narrow NBSP before AM/PM, NFD, curly apostrophe).

All string index math (indexOf, substring, slice in edit-diff and the fuzzy match) is UTF-16 in JS. Native code can use byte offsets internally as long as results are identical; NFKC can change lengths, and the code already handles that through line spans.

units.title: Harness public types, agent settings/resolution, usage, inbox, submissions, live doc, prompt planning, context derivation
units.notes:
harness/types.ts defines the harness public surface:
- SubmissionDraft, ToolRegistration (name, description, parameters schema, prepareArguments, outputLimits, replay, execute(args, api, ctx))
- PromptSection, Extension (tools, sections, hooks, wraps, tasks), Registry, AgentState/AgentChange/Agent, Settings, HarnessOptions, TaskInspection, ContextView, Conversation, Harness

Per the user decision these become native Rust traits / Go interfaces. Closures (execute, hooks, section render) are boxed async fns (Rust Arc<dyn Fn ... -> BoxFuture>) or Go func values.

agent.ts:
- AgentDoc (pi.agent: rewindable/asOf, checkpoint always) with defaults.
- configure/applyChange: null clears a field, undefined leaves it.
- Task-owned conversations copy the owner conversation's agent.
- resolveAgent: extension selection, wraps with a rename check, tool filter, and the 'instructions' section.

usage.ts: UsageDoc (pi.usage) keyed `${provider}/${modelId}` or by tool name; addUsage sums the Usage fields.

It imports convertPartial from generation.ts and SchedulerOutcome from scheduler.ts (a cycle: same Rust crate / same Go package).

Section-key regex /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/; 'instructions' is reserved. Draft-based document updates in this unit need chord's native tracked mutation API.

units.title: Harness open/root/conversations, TaskScheduler durable task engine, registry, define helpers, utilities
skipped_tests: packages/durable/test/examples/22-subagent-foreground.ts#OPENAI_API_KEY-branch -- real OpenAI branch; port only the faux-provider path
packages/durable/test/examples/23-subagent-background.ts#OPENAI_API_KEY-branch -- real OpenAI branch; port only the faux-provider path
units.notes:
TaskScheduler is the riskiest file:
- A #live mirror of non-terminal tasks, running invocations, and a reserve/step/decide loop with precedence rules: abort marks, owner cascades, waits, completing drains.
- Task versions are migrated at reservation.
- A step that makes no durable progress (jsonEqual of before and after checkpoint) faults the task.
- Memos are first-writer-wins.
- Orphaned outcomes follow when an owner is missing.
- reconcile and finalize are scheduled via queueMicrotask.
- Waiters resolve idle/settled promises.
- Sleeps loop in chunks of MAX_TIMER_DELAY = 2^31-1 ms, cancelled with AbortSignal.any.
- Faults store {message, ...} error objects whose message text is persisted.

Rust: a single scheduler actor task owning #live, woken through a Notify; cancellation via tokio_util CancellationToken; deferred reconcile via tokio::task::yield_now or a queued self-message. Go: one goroutine with a select loop; context.Context for abort.

harness.ts:
- HarnessImpl extends SessionImpl: in Rust use composition with Deref or delegation; Go embeds *Session.
- Harness.open verifies BUILTIN_TASKS (pi.generation, pi.tool, pi.compaction) are registered, opens tasks, and closes on failure.
- root() is created lazily with agent change + init in one commit; conversation/fork creation; boundConversation.

registry.ts: createRegistry/install/uninstall/reload with snapshots and validateExtension (duplicate names, section key regex, 'instructions' reserved). define.ts holds defineTool/defineExtension/section/hook helpers. json.ts: assignJson writes leaf-by-leaf into a Draft so that ops are minimal. util.ts: Waiters, scanAll pagination, closedError.

Tests use the pi-ai faux provider (packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts), so its native port must exist first. Recovery tests close and reopen the harness over the same storage mid-task and assert exact resumed phases. spec-usage.test.ts is a compile-only check of docs/spec.md snippets: port it as a compile test exercising the same API calls, or drop it if the API shape differs by design.

units.title: Built-in tasks: generation (streaming/retry/poll/tool rounds), tool execution (output bounding/progress), compaction

packages/durable/test/tool-output-bench.ts -- node --expose-gc throughput/heap benchmark script, not a correctness test

packages/durable/test/examples/19-json.ts#OPENAI_API_KEY-branch -- real OpenAI branch; port only the faux path
units.notes:
GenerationTask:
- Phases: prepare (plan system entries and tools, threshold compaction), request (stream via Models; commit partial AssistantMessage to pi.live at most every 100ms), retry (isRetryableAssistantError/retryDelayMs; defaults enabled, maxRetries 3, baseDelay 2000, maxAgentDelay 60000), poll (deferred responses; DEFAULT_POLL_AFTER_MS 5000), tools (startToolRound spawns pi.tool children and waits; finishToolRound handles terminate/handoff/addTools).
- appendAssistant records usage.
- On context overflow it triggers overflow compaction.
- convertPartial is shared with live.ts.

ToolTask:
- Phases call/execute. Execute: readCall, prepareArguments, validateToolArguments (pi-ai), the beforeTool hook (may block or replace), run with ToolExecutionApi (output(), diagnostic(), progress details, env), the afterTool hook, finalResult, settle.
- Replay 'safe' re-runs after a crash; 'unsafe' yields an error result.
- publishProgress uses chord overlap(prev, next, 65536) to emit a front-trim + append op instead of a full rewrite (harness-live-deltas asserts the exact ops).
- appendToolResult renders diagnostics as `<harness>\n[severity] message\n</harness>`. boundContent caps text content.

output.ts:
- sanitizeOutput regex /[\x00-\x08\x0b-\x1f￹-￻]/g.
- boundOutput keeps a head/tail window on UTF-8 bytes, cutting on whole lines when possible, else on character boundaries via characterEnd/characterStart. Tests compare against Buffer behavior, including surrogate edge cases.
- OutputBuffer decodes UTF-8 split across chunks with a streaming TextDecoder.
- Progress throttles commits: the first change commits immediately, later ones wait at least 100ms and enough time for the written size at 100 KiB/s. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers, so inject a clock/timer trait (Rust) or an interface (Go) for deterministic tests.

CompactionTask:
- Phases select/summarize/retry. Default policy: reserve 16384, keepRecent 20000, background 32768.
- selectCut/isCandidate/estimateContext use pi-ai calculateContextTokens and estimateMessageTokens.
- serializeConversation truncates tool results to TOOL_RESULT_MAX_CHARS 2000 in UTF-16 code units.
- The summarization prompts and SUMMARY_PREFIX/SUFFIX are verbatim text; copy them exactly.
- placeSummary appends directly when blocking, else admits a submission with requestId `compaction:${taskId}`.

All faux-provider tests port; there are no real-provider tests in vitest files.
