external_deps.npm: N-API .node prebuilds (in-repo C/ObjC, no npm package)
external_deps.used_for: Clipboard text/image/file paths and modifier-key state (darwin AppKit/CoreGraphics, win32 user32/kernel32, linux XCB)
external_deps.rust_suggestion: objc2 + objc2-app-kit + core-graphics (macOS); windows-sys (Win32 clipboard, GetAsyncKeyState, SetConsoleMode); x11rb or libloading of libxcb.so.1 (Linux). arboard is a fallback but lacks identical semantics.
external_deps.go_suggestion: cgo or ebitengine/purego for AppKit/CoreGraphics; golang.org/x/sys/windows for the Win32 APIs; github.com/jezek/xgb for X11. golang.design/x/clipboard is a fallback (cgo, different semantics).

hazards: UTF-16 code-unit offsets are observable: Editor/Input cursorCol, AutocompleteProvider (lines, cursorLine, cursorCol) consumed by coding-agent, word-navigation return values, paste-marker '[paste #N C chars]' counts and the >1000-char threshold, latex position math. Store UTF-8 internally but convert at every API boundary, or keep UTF-16 buffers for editor lines.

Byte-exact escape output: render diffs, synchronized output, cursor moves, SGR resets (`\x1b[0m\x1b]8;;\x07` segment reset, table wrap reset), Kitty/iTerm2/OSC 8/OSC 52/OSC 0/OSC 9;4 sequences. Build golden tests by capturing TS output.

Unicode data version: width, grapheme, emoji (RGI_Emoji) and Script_Extensions results depend on Node 22's ICU/V8 Unicode version. Crates and stdlib tables may be newer or older, so generate tables from the pinned UCD.

JS regex features with no direct Rust regex / Go regexp equivalent: lookbehind/lookahead (latex, marked, markdown strikethrough), /v set subtraction, \p{RGI_Emoji}, JS \s/\w sets, sticky/global lastIndex semantics. Use hand scanners, fancy-regex, or regexp2.
Intl.Segmenter word segmentation uses ICU dictionaries for CJK/Thai with isWordLike. Go has no equivalent and Rust needs icu_segmenter, so CJK word navigation and selection may diverge.

Timer and microtask ordering: process.nextTick render coalescing, the 16ms throttle, StdinBuffer 10ms/50ms timeouts, the 150ms Kitty negotiation fragment timeout, autocomplete debounce, Loader setInterval, unref'd ScrollView and flash timers. Tests await nextTick+20ms, so use a single UI event loop with an injectable clock.

Single-threaded mutable object graph: components hold closures and back-references (SettingsList submenu done(), Loader → TUI.requestRender, Editor → tui). Rust needs Rc<RefCell>/Weak and must avoid re-entrant borrow panics during callbacks such as onSubmit → setText; Go needs one owning goroutine.
Component identity (=== on objects) drives focus, overlays, removeChild and the Box line-identity cache. Use Rc::ptr_eq or pointer equality, and do not derive PartialEq on content.

Process-global singletons mutated by tests and coding-agent: keybindings manager, kittyProtocolActive, terminal capabilities and cell dimensions, Kitty image id counter and metadata registry, width cache, native helper cache. Rust tests run in parallel by default; serialize them or use thread-local overrides.

Env read at call time (TERM*, TMUX, WT_SESSION, SSH_*, DISPLAY, COLUMNS/LINES, PI_TUI_*, PI_HYPERLINKS/PI_IMAGE_PROTOCOL/PI_TRUE_COLOR, TERMUX_VERSION, ZELLIJ, STY, WEZTERM_PANE). Tests mutate process.env, and Rust set_var is unsafe and racy, so inject an env provider.

Math semantics: Math.round rounds half toward +inf; Math.floor/trunc on negatives; Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER sentinels in stack sizing (avoid usize overflow); float transcendental ULP differences in Oklab conversions.
Lenient Node base64 decoding and Buffer.byteLength(base64) formula; pathToFileURL percent-encoding; os.homedir '~' shortening. All must match Node exactly.
Sorting: Array.prototype.sort is stable and localeCompare uses ICU collation. Go sort.Slice is unstable.

Raw TTY handling: UTF-8 chunks split across reads, Windows VT input enablement via the native helper, SIGWINCH self-signal with ignored EACCES/EPERM, synchronous stdout writes, drainInput before exit.
Crash/debug artifacts and their names and formats: pi-tui-crash.log, PI_TUI_DEBUG and PI_TUI_DEBUG_REDRAW logs under /tmp/tui/render-*.log, PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG raw write log.
Async autocomplete: provider promises, AbortController, request tokens and snapshot validation. Results arriving after the text changed must be dropped exactly as in TS.

Test infrastructure: the node:test suites depend on @xterm/headless emulation details (wrap, wide chars, scrollback, right-trimmed rows) and chalk's exact SGR nesting. Expect some expectation adjustments when switching emulators.
js_runtime_dependent: native-platform.ts and native-module-path.ts load per-OS N-API .node prebuilds with createRequire and search candidate paths (installed package, bundle dir, execPath). Native handling: compile platform clipboard and modifier code into the Rust/Go binaries with the same NativeClipboard tri-state semantics; drop the module path search and the .node, napi.h and build scripts.

Custom Component, EditorComponent, AutocompleteProvider, theme functions and overlay components can be supplied by coding-agent TS extensions at runtime. Per the user decision, expose Rust traits and Go interfaces (Component, Focusable, EditorComponent, AutocompleteProvider, SlashCommand argument completers) for native and built-in implementations only; do not load TS.

Symbol.for-keyed protocol methods (LAYOUT_NODE on Stack/ScrollView, VIEWPORT_TUI brand) and duck-typed optional methods (handleInput?, handleMouse?, wantsKeyRelease, focused, dispose). Handle these with trait default methods and an Option-returning layout_node(); in Go, use optional interfaces checked by type assertion.

The marked library's JS lexer and extension hooks are used directly and re-exported (Marked, Token, Tokens) to coding-agent mermaid.ts. Ship a native hand-ported lexer module with equivalent token types.
V8-specific memory optimizations (flattenLines rope flattening, WeakRef token cache in Markdown, string identity comparisons in the Box cache) become no-ops, plain caches, or content comparison.

The process.nextTick, setTimeout, setInterval and timer.unref event-loop semantics used for render scheduling and component timers. Replace them with an explicit single-threaded scheduler; non-blocking (unref) timers must not keep the app alive.
The structuredClone deep copies in Editor history and UndoStack become derived Clone (Rust) or explicit deep-copy methods (Go).

reports.summary:
This area covers four parts. Two are standalone packages, packages/mcp (MCP client SDK, 3127 src lines) and packages/codemode (QuickJS sandbox plus TypeScript declaration rendering, 1644 lines). The other two are inside coding-agent: the built-in extensions under packages/coding-agent/src/extensions (codemode tool, tool_search, llama.cpp, MCP; 6975 lines) and the `pi mcp` CLI subcommand.

packages/mcp
- McpClient (client.ts) is a JSON-RPC 2.0 peer over a McpTransport interface (start/send/close plus message/error/close events).
- connect() sends initialize with LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2025-11-25. It also accepts 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05, then sends notifications/initialized.
- Request ids are numeric and start at 1. When onProgress is set, progressToken equals the request id.
- Timeouts default to 30s and are renewed by progress. Abort sends notifications/cancelled, except for initialize.
- listTools/listResources/listResourceTemplates paginate up to 1000 pages and reject a repeated cursor. The client answers ping and roots/list itself.
- protocol/content.ts turns MCP content blocks into LLM text/image content using fixed placeholder strings.
- There are three transports:
  - in-memory, for tests.
  - stdio: cross-spawn, newline framing, 16MiB message cap, 64KiB stderr ring buffer, process-group kill with SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation, taskkill on Windows.
  - streamable HTTP: POST that returns JSON or SSE, a GET stream opened after initialize, Last-Event-ID resume with exponential reconnect, Mcp-Session-Id and MCP-Protocol-Version headers, DELETE on close, and 401/403 insufficient_scope handling through an AuthProvider.
- oauth/ is a port of the MCP TS SDK 1.29 auth flow (MIT license in LICENSES/):
  - Discovery of protected-resource and authorization-server metadata (RFC 9728 / RFC 8414 / OIDC).
  - Dynamic client registration, PKCE S256, authorization code and refresh grants with client_secret_basic/post/none.
  - RFC 9207 iss check, error-driven retries, step-up scope merging.
  - adaptOAuthProvider (one shared in-flight refresh) and a loopback OAuthCallbackServer.

packages/codemode
- parseCodemodeSource accepts a `// @options: {json}` first line with max_output_tokens/timeout_ms. CODEMODE_SOURCE_GRAMMAR is a Lark grammar used for constrained sampling.
- renderDeclarations converts JSON Schemas into TypeScript declaration text, including local $ref resolution and size caps.
- CodemodeSandbox (runtime/host.ts) starts a Node worker (runtime/worker.ts). The worker runs quickjs-wasi's quickjs.wasm and evaluates PRELUDE_SOURCE, an embedded JS program that defines the script API: the tools proxy, text/image/exit/console, store/load, ALL_TOOLS and namespaced globals.
- The user script is wrapped as an async function. Host and VM talk through a single `bridge(kind,...)` host function (call/global/output/done) and worker messages.
- Interrupts use a SharedArrayBuffer flag polled from host_interrupt. Memory and stack limits are set through qjs_* exports.
- Native port: embed the same wasm and drive it with wasmtime (Rust) or wazero (Go) on a dedicated thread/goroutine. The native code must reimplement quickjs-wasi's JS glue: env imports host_call/host_interrupt/host_promise_rejection/host_module_*/host_get_timezone_offset, a minimal wasi_snapshot_preview1 shim, WTF-8 string marshalling, and handle lifetime.

coding-agent extensions
- builtInExtensions (extensions/index.ts) registers, in order: llama.cpp, codemode, tool-search and mcp. The last three are marked replaceable.
- codemode:
  - Registers the `codemode` tool, inactive by default, with exposure model-only.
  - The description is built from the active tools and a token budget catalog; the input schema is `{code}`.
  - executeCodemode runs the sandbox. Nested tool calls go through ctx.executeTool, so hooks and permissions apply.
  - Extra script globals: searchTools/describeTool/describeNamespace (via the tool_search BM25 ranker) and models.* (classify/generateImages through the model registry).
  - Store writes are persisted as `codemode-store` custom session entries and replayed per branch.
  - Output is truncated to a token budget, with the full text spilled to a tmp file. renderer.ts provides the TUI renderers.
- tool-search: a BM25 index over tool name, description, namespace and schema text. searchAndLoad activates the matched tools.
- llama:
  - A provider "llama.cpp" for the llama-server router: /models with load/unload/download and SSE progress, /props for chat template thinking detection.
  - A Hugging Face GGUF search, and a `/llama` TUI command with LlamaView/HuggingFaceSearch.
- mcp: the main runtime.
  - config.ts loads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and the trusted project's .pi/mcp.json, and edits them preserving indentation.
  - runtime.ts has McpServerConnection, a lazily connecting state machine (connecting/connected/disconnected/needs-auth/failed/closed). It retries transient HTTP failures, retries once on an expired session, records list_changed and log notifications, and resolves auth from OAuth or provider tokens.
  - oauth.ts has the credential store mcp-auth.json, keyed `namespace|url`, and a cross-process refresh lock based on proper-lockfile.
  - tools.ts maps MCP tools to pi tools named `mcp__server__tool` (≤64 chars, hashed on collision) and converts results with 20KiB middle truncation and binary spill files.
  - resources.ts provides Codex's list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates and read_mcp_resource.
  - index.ts wires session lifecycle hooks:
    - session_start loads config and starts background connections.
    - before_agent_start waits up to 10s for servers with direct tools and writes the `mcp_servers` system-prompt section.
    - tool_call makes codemode scripts, tool_search and resource tools wait for the servers they need.
    - turn_start picks up out-of-process sign-ins; mcp_servers_change handles servers registered by extensions.
    - It also provides the `/mcp` command with a TUI manager (ui.ts).
  - cli.ts implements `pi mcp add|remove|list|login|logout` with exact help text, JSON output and exit codes.

Port order (one-way dependencies):
1. mcp-core-stdio
2. mcp-http-oauth (owns the package facade index.ts)
3. codemode-package
4. coding-agent codemode/tool-search
5. llama, which is independent of mcp and codemode
6. mcp runtime
7. mcp extension and CLI, last

The coding-agent units depend on core files from other areas (extensions/types.ts ExtensionAPI trait, auth-storage, mcp-servers validation, settings, session-manager, keybindings, theme and components) and on ai/agent/tui types. Faux-provider suite tests need the test/suite/harness.ts port from the agent-session area.

units.title: MCP client core: JSON-RPC protocol, content conversion, McpClient, in-memory and stdio transports, package scaffolding
units.notes:
Crate/module scaffolding:
- package.json exports ".", "./oauth" and "./testing". Map them to a Rust crate pi-mcp with pub mods oauth and testing, and a Go module with packages mcp, mcp/oauth and mcp/mcptest.
- The facade src/index.ts lives in unit mcp-http-oauth because it re-exports StreamableHttpTransport. Tests in this unit import modules directly.

McpClient (client.ts):
- Numeric request ids from 1. Pending map keyed by id.
- LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION="2025-11-25". Supported versions: 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05. An unsupported negotiated version is a connect error.
- Sends notifications/initialized after initialize.
- When onProgress is set, progressToken = request id. Timeout default 30000ms, reset on progress when resetTimeoutOnProgress; Infinity or <=0 disables it.
- Abort sends notifications/cancelled {requestId, reason?}, never for initialize.
- Pagination is capped at MAX_LIST_PAGES=1000 and rejects a repeated cursor; nextCursor "" or null ends it.
- A missing resource name falls back to the uri. A missing CallToolResult.content becomes [].
- Built-in request handlers: ping and roots/list (roots from options).
- Incoming requests are handled fire-and-forget (no ordering guarantee between concurrent handlers). Unknown methods answer -32601.
- Error classes and exact messages: McpError(code,message,data), McpConnectionClosedError "MCP connection closed", McpTimeoutError "MCP request timed out after ${ms}ms", McpAbortError (name AbortError).

toLlmContent (protocol/content.ts):
- Exact placeholder strings: `[audio <mime> omitted]`, resource_link -> `name: uri`, `[binary resource uri (type) omitted]`, `[unsupported MCP content <type>]`.
- structuredContent is rendered as JSON.stringify(v,null,2). Needs key-order-preserving JSON (serde_json preserve_order; ordered map in Go) and JS number formatting.

InMemoryTransport:
- Delivers via structuredClone + queueMicrotask, so send() resolves before the peer sees the message.
- Native: unbounded channel plus a spawned delivery task, deep-copying the JSON value.

StdioTransport:
- Spawned through cross-spawn: resolve PATHEXT and .cmd/.bat shims on Windows; Rust uses the `which` crate plus hand-ported cmd escaping, Go uses exec.LookPath.
- Env is merged with process.env.
- Newline-delimited JSON; lines over DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (16MiB) error out. stderr is kept in a 64KiB ring buffer and included in close and exit errors.
- Process groups: detached + kill(-pid). Rust: CommandExt::process_group(0) + libc::kill(-pid). Go: SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} + syscall.Kill(-pid). On win32: `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`.
- Close sequence: end stdin, wait a 500ms grace period, SIGTERM the group, then SIGKILL after grace + closeTimeoutMs (2000). Keep this timing.
- A process-exit hook kills live groups. Native: a global registry drained from the exit path and signal handlers.

Tests:
- client.test.ts uses vi.useFakeTimers. Use tokio::time::pause in Rust and an injectable clock or short real timeouts in Go.
- stdio fixtures are Node .mjs scripts. Rewrite them as native helper programs (Rust: a test bin via CARGO_BIN_EXE_*; Go: TestMain re-exec of os.Args[0] keyed by an env var) with identical JSON replies. The stubborn-server test stays POSIX-only.
- coding-agent/test/mcp-command.test.ts also reuses stdio-server.mjs; expose the native fixture so that unit can use it.

units.title: MCP streamable HTTP transport with SSE, OAuth 2.1 auth flow, callback server, and package facade
units.notes:
StreamableHttpTransport requests:
- POST with `accept: application/json, text/event-stream` and content-type application/json.
- A JSON response body may be a single message or an array.
- 202/204 to a request (as opposed to a notification) is an error.
- Session header Mcp-Session-Id. After initialize, MCP-Protocol-Version is sent.
- close() sends DELETE with a 1s timeout. 404 on a request that carried a session -> McpSessionExpiredError. Other failures -> McpHttpError(status, body).

GET stream:
- Opened after notifications/initialized. 405 means the server offers none.
- Reconnect delay 1000*2^n ms capped at 30000, maxRetries 5. A server `retry:` field overrides the delay. Resume with Last-Event-ID.
- Retryable: status 408, 429, >=500, network errors (TypeError), error codes starting E* or UND_ERR*. Native code needs a typed network-error kind.

consumeSseStream (exported, tested directly):
- Handles CRLF/CR/LF, BOM and comments.
- An `id` containing NUL is ignored. `retry` must be all digits.
- Byte limits are counted in UTF-8 bytes. Event fields: event/data/id/retry.

Auth:
- On 401, or 403 whose WWW-Authenticate matches /(?:^|[\s,])error="?insufficient_scope"?/i, call authProvider.onUnauthorized({response, serverUrl, fetch, token}) once and retry; a second failure raises McpAuthRequiredError.
- The Cloudflare `fetch` receiver fix (#10188) is JS-only and does not apply natively.

OAuth discovery (port of MCP TS SDK 1.29, keep LICENSES text and attribution):
- Protected resource: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource{path}, then the root.
- Authorization server: oauth-authorization-server{path}, openid-configuration{path}, {path}/.well-known/openid-configuration.
- 4xx and 502 count as a miss. Send the MCP-Protocol-Version header.
- Issuer comparison ignores a trailing slash (OAuthIssuerMismatchError).

OAuth flow:
- PKCE: verifier = base64url(32 random bytes), challenge S256. DCR via POST registration_endpoint (default /register).
- Token requests are application/x-www-form-urlencoded (URLSearchParams: space as +). Client auth: client_secret_basic (Basic base64(urlencode(id):urlencode(secret))), client_secret_post or none, chosen from token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.
- Check RFC 9207 `iss` on the callback.
- Retries: invalid_client/unauthorized_client clear all state and rerun; invalid_grant clears tokens and reruns.
- stepUpScope merges granted and challenged scopes.
- adaptOAuthProvider shares a single in-flight refresh. McpOAuthProvider serializes its writes and binds state to the exact server URL string.
- Use WHATWG URL semantics (Rust `url` crate; Go needs careful net/url handling of path, trailing slash and origin).

OAuthCallbackServer:
- HTTP on 127.0.0.1, port 0 or configured. IPv6 hosts are bracketed in redirect URIs.
- 5 minute timeout. Success/error HTML pages are supplied by the caller.
- Rust: hyper 1.x server on tokio. Go: net/http.

Tests:
- helpers.ts starts a loopback node:http server; rewrite as a native loopback server helper.
- oauth.test covers discovery, registration, PKCE, refresh, concurrent 401s, step-up, URL binding, issuer mismatch, the configured metadata URL, the iss check and the callback pages.

units.title: Codemode package: source options parsing, TypeScript declaration rendering, QuickJS-WASM sandbox host/worker and prelude
units.notes:
This is the largest hidden porting cost. quickjs-wasi's JS glue (node_modules/quickjs-wasi/dist/index.js ~3100 lines, plus wasi-shim.js) must be reimplemented natively against node_modules/quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm (v3.6.2). Vendor the .wasm into both repos, using include_bytes! in Rust and go:embed in Go.

WASM exports used:
- Setup and limits: _initialize, qjs_init, qjs_set_memory_limit, qjs_set_max_stack_size (MAX_STACK_SIZE=512*1024), qjs_set_interrupt_handler.
- Eval and calls: qjs_eval(code,len,filename,flags), qjs_call, qjs_new_host_function(namePtr,nameLen,id).
- Values: qjs_new_string, qjs_new_number, qjs_get_undefined/true/false/global, qjs_get_prop_value, qjs_set_prop_string, qjs_dup_value, qjs_free_value.
- Exceptions: qjs_is_exception, qjs_get_exception, qjs_throw, qjs_new_error.
- Jobs: qjs_is_job_pending, qjs_execute_pending_job.
- Strings: qjs_get_string_len (length-aware WTF-8) + qjs_free_cstring. Type checks: qjs_is_undefined, qjs_is_string.
- Memory: wasm_malloc, wasm_free.

env imports:
- host_call(namePtr,nameLen,thisPtr,argc,argvPtr): returns a dup'd value, or 0 after qjs_throw.
- host_interrupt: polls the atomic abort flag.
- host_promise_rejection: frees values.
- host_module_normalize/load: unused, return an error.
- host_get_timezone_offset.

wasi_snapshot_preview1 shim:
- clock_time_get returns Date.now()*1e6 for both clocks.
- fd_write discards output but reports full length.
- fd_fdstat_get reports a char device for fds 1/2. fd_close/fd_seek return NOSYS(52).
- random_get, args/environ empty, proc_exit.
- Values cross the boundary as WTF-8. Lone surrogates cannot live in a Rust String or valid Go UTF-8, so decode lossily at the boundary or keep the WTF-8 bytes.

Host/worker (runtime/host.ts, worker.ts):
- The Node worker plus SharedArrayBuffer becomes a dedicated OS thread (Rust) or goroutine (Go) owning the wasm Store, fed by a channel carrying the protocol.ts message kinds (start/result/abort; bridge kinds call/global/output/done).
- Interrupt: an AtomicBool polled by host_interrupt. Backstops: wasmtime epoch_interruption, wazero WithCloseOnContextDone. Cap linear memory with wasmtime StoreLimits / wazero WithMemoryLimitPages.
- Embed PRELUDE_SOURCE verbatim and eval it with filename "codemode-prelude.js". Call it with a JSON string of the globals.
- Wrap the script exactly as `(async (tools, console) => {${code}\n})` with filename "codemode.js".
- drain(): loop executePendingJobs, then call api.stalled(). Settle tool results via api.settle.
- Result error kinds: script, timeout, aborted, sandbox. DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000.
- Prelude store limits: MAX_STORE_VALUE_CHARS 262144, MAX_STORE_TOTAL_CHARS 1048576. These are UTF-16 lengths computed inside the VM, so no native concern.
- RESERVED_GLOBALS and the global-name validation error strings must match.
- The "Worker exited with code" message is Node-specific; map it to a sandbox error with similar text.

wasm.ts:
- loadQuickJSWasm caches compiled modules per path. Native: compile the embedded bytes once (wasmtime Module / wazero CompiledModule plus compilation cache). Keep an optional override path for parity with config getQuickJSWasmPath.

declarations.ts:
- Emits TypeScript text for the model; it must be byte-identical.
- MCP_TYPESCRIPT_PREAMBLE verbatim. schemaToType sorts keys (JS default sort = UTF-16 code unit order) and resolves local $ref with MAX_REF_EXPANSIONS 32. DEFAULT_INPUT_SCHEMA_MAX_CHARS 16000 is measured in UTF-16 units.
- Also renderToolSignature/renderToolSample/renderToolOutputType/mcpStructuredContentSchema.

source.ts:
- parseCodemodeSource reads an optional first line `// @options: {...}` with keys max_output_tokens and timeout_ms (positive integers <= 2147483647).
- CodemodeSourceError messages embed V8 JSON.parse messages that cannot be reproduced; adapt the test assertions to the native message where they compare it.
- Keep CODEMODE_SOURCE_GRAMMAR (Lark) verbatim.

identifier.ts:
- toCodemodeIdentifier works per code point: ASCII [A-Za-z_$] first, [A-Za-z0-9_$] rest, otherwise '_'. "" becomes "_".

sandbox.test.ts adjustments:
- Skip the cases "accepts a worker path string" and "reports a missing worker file as a sandbox error" (Node worker file URL option; drop workerUrl from the native API).
- Replace the node:vm parse check "embedded sources parse as JavaScript" with a QuickJS compile-only eval.
- Adapt "reports a failing wasm module" to invalid wasm bytes.

units.title: Built-in codemode extension (tool, executor, renderer) and tool_search extension (BM25)
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/codemode-worker-config.test.ts -- tests config.ts resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier for Bun/bundled/unbundled JS worker entrypoints; native runs the embedded wasm in-process, no worker specifier
units.notes:
Extension registration (codemode/index.ts):
- createCodemodeExtension registers CODEMODE_TOOL_NAME="codemode" with defaultActive false. Mode comes from settings.codemode.mode; inlineBudget is read from settings.
- This is a native ExtensionFactory implementation of the ExtensionAPI trait/interface.

Tool definition (tool.ts):
- Schema `{code: string}` with description "Raw JavaScript source.".
- isCodemodeTool and isToolSearchTool compare schema object identity. Natively, compare a tool marker or kind id, never the name, because other extensions' tools named codemode/tool_search must not match.
- Description: DESCRIPTION_INTRO + describeGlobals + a catalog.
  - Budget DEFAULT_CODEMODE_INLINE_BUDGET=3000 tokens at CHARS_PER_TOKEN 4.
  - selectCatalog fills round-robin, cheapest first, and says what is missing.
  - Namespaces are sorted with localeCompare.
  - Deferred tools and namespace instructions are left out.
- prepareCodemodeLoadout implements modes on/only. constrainedSampling = {grammar openai_lark: CODEMODE_SOURCE_GRAMMAR}. exposure "model-only".

Execution (execute.ts):
- Nested calls go through ctx.executeTool with ids `${toolCallId}/...`, so hooks and permissions apply. Calls run in parallel.
- Memory limit 256MiB. Timeout defaults to Infinity unless timeout_ms is given.
- Store: CODEMODE_STORE_ENTRY_TYPE "codemode-store" custom entries. readCodemodeStore folds them from the root along the current branch and ignores malformed data. Append nothing for failed scripts or scripts without writes.
- Output budget: DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 10000 (x4 chars, UTF-16 lengths), head/tail split. The full text spills to os.tmpdir()/pi-codemode-<16 hex>.txt.
- Result header: "Script completed|failed\nWall time X.X seconds\nOutput:\n" (toFixed(1)).
- Discovery globals searchTools/describeTool/describeNamespace use tool-search Bm25Ranker.
- models globals:
  - getModelsOfType, getAvailableOfType, getModelOfType, classify, generateImages, with a concurrency limiter of 4.
  - Classifier and images contexts are validated. Headers are stripped from model info, and script-supplied auth fields are ignored.
- Usage of nested results is summed via usage-totals.

Renderer (renderer.ts):
- SCRIPT_HEADER regex; CODE_PREVIEW_LINES 10, CALL_PREVIEW_COUNT 8, OUTPUT_PREVIEW_LINES 5; icons ✓ ✗ ⊘ ….
- formatCost: toFixed(2) at >=0.01, else toPrecision(2). Port JS toPrecision exactly.
- Collapsed output is limited by wrapped visual lines.

Lazy loading:
- execute.lazy.ts (dynamic import) becomes a direct call.
- codemode/worker.ts is the bundle-only worker entry; drop it natively (it only re-exports pi-codemode/worker).

tool-search (tool.ts):
- STOP_WORDS set, naive stem (plural folding), tokenize (camelCase/snake_case split, lowercase).
- createToolSearchDocument concatenates name, description, namespace and schemaText.
- Bm25Ranker k1=1.2, b=0.75 with a stable sort; ties keep document order.
- TOOL_SEARCH_DESCRIPTION verbatim. searchAndLoad calls setActiveTools.
- Errors "query must not be empty" and "limit must be a positive integer".

Tests:
- The suite tests need test/suite/harness.ts + faux provider (agent-session area).
- codemode-renderer uses initTheme and node:util stripVTControlCharacters; use an ANSI-strip helper.

units.title: Built-in llama.cpp extension: router client, Hugging Face search, provider, /llama command and TUI
units.notes:
LlamaClient (client.ts):
- 15s per-request timeout combined with the caller signal (AbortSignal.any). Natively, use a child cancellation token / context.WithTimeout.
- Endpoints:
  - GET /models
  - GET /props?model=
  - POST /models/load, /models/unload
  - POST /models (download)
  - GET /models/sse: progress events, parsed by normalizing CRLF and splitting on "\n\n"
- Wait polls: unloadAndWait 100ms, loadAndWait 250ms, downloadAndWait 500ms.
- formatBytes. normalizeLlamaServerUrl derives management and inference (/v1) URLs with WHATWG URL semantics.

HuggingFaceClient (huggingface.ts):
- findHuggingFaceToken order: HF_TOKEN, HF_TOKEN_PATH, $HF_HOME/token, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/huggingface/token, ~/.cache/huggingface/token.
- search/details parse GGUF quantizations with QUANTIZATION_PATTERN and SHARD_SUFFIX_PATTERN, then sort with Q4_K_M first and localeCompare.
- 429 errors use retry-after or the ratelimit header `t=`.
- Reports gated/access requirements.

Provider (provider.ts):
- LLAMA_PROVIDER_ID "llama.cpp", DEFAULT_LLAMA_SERVER_URL http://127.0.0.1:8080.
- apiKey auth (login/check/resolve) storing URL plus an optional key. Credential env LLAMA_BASE_URL; LLAMA_API_KEY defaults to "local".
- Stays dormant until configured.
- Chat models: api openai-completions with compat flags. Qwen-style thinking is enabled when /props chat_template contains enable_thinking.
- Classifier models use the llama-cpp-classify api.
- refreshModels publishes and persists the store entry, restoring cached context for unloaded autoload presets. Unloaded presets are exposed only when router autoload is enabled.

Command and TUI:
- index.ts registers the `/llama` command (TUI only): load, unload and download flows, restoring the previous state on failure.
- ui.ts: LlamaView and HuggingFaceSearch with a 500ms debounce and fuzzyFilter. runWithProgress races completion against cancel. Key handling must come from keybindings (no hardcoded keys).

Tests:
- llama-extension.test.ts uses node:http mock servers plus createExtensionRuntime/loadExtensionFromFactory. Port with a native loopback server and the native extension loader for built-in factories.

units.title: MCP extension runtime: mcp.json config, server connections, OAuth credential store and refresh lock, tool/resource adapters, server log
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-conformance/run.ts -- official MCP conformance suite fetched via npx (@modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.11), needs network, run by a separate CI job, not a unit test; optionally port client.ts as a native binary and reuse run.ts/baseline.json

packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-conformance/client.ts -- conformance client launched by run.ts through node --import source-resolver; native equivalent would be a small binary over McpServerConnection + signInMcpServer
packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-conformance/baseline.json -- data for the conformance runner; keep as-is if the native conformance client is added
packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-conformance/README.md -- documentation for the conformance runner
units.notes:
Config (config.ts):
- loadMcpConfig reads <agentDir>/mcp.json and, for trusted projects, <cwd>/.pi/mcp.json. Validation lives in core/mcp-servers.ts.
- Errors: names that differ only in -/_ clash (mcpNamespace); `auth` is accepted only in the global file; autoEnableCodemode must be boolean, with project precedence.
- getMcpToolExposure resolves exact toolExposure names first, then patterns in order.
- update/add/removeMcpServerConfig rewrite JSON keeping the detected indent (/^([ \t]+)\S/m) and a trailing "\n", preserving other keys and their order.

Log (log.ts):
- formatMcpLogMessage: `${new Date().toISOString()} [server] level logger: text\n` with continuation lines indented 4.
- McpServerLog appends synchronously and rotates to .1 above 5MiB.

Credentials (oauth.ts):
- McpOAuthCredentialStore keeps mcp-auth.json via the auth-storage backend withLock (byte-compatible JSON).
- Key `${mcpNamespace(name)}|${serverUrl}`. Legacy URL-only keys migrate to the first server that loads them; signOut removes them too.
- Refresh lock: proper-lockfile on `mcp-auth-refresh-<sha256(key) hex[:16]>` in the agent dir, stale 20s, 250 retries every 100ms. Hand-port proper-lockfile's mkdir `<path>.lock` plus mtime-touch protocol so TS and native processes interoperate.
- createMcpAuthProvider: 30s expiry skew, 15s per refresh request.
- signInMcpServer: callback settings (port/url/scope/clientName), callback server raced with promptForRedirectUrl, McpSignInCancelledError. HTML pages come from ai utils/oauth-page.

Connection state machine (runtime.ts, McpServerConnection):
- States: connecting, connected, disconnected, needs-auth, failed, closed.
- Default timeout 60s. HTTP connect retries [250,1000] ms on transient errors. Resource reads are retried after transient HTTP errors, tool calls are not.
- McpSessionExpiredError: new session, retry once (shared among concurrent calls).
- Roots = [pathToFileURL(cwd)]. Records notifications/message into the log; tools/list_changed and resources/list_changed trigger a re-list. Servers without the tools capability are not listed.
- Exposes challenge, oauthUrl (HTTP without an Authorization header), oauthSettings(), reconnect(), signOut() and close().
- providerToken: auth.provider uses a model-registry API key and asks for the provider login on rejection.
- createDefaultTransport: expandHome (~) on command, args and cwd; resolve-config-value for headers, env and clientSecret (${NAME}, !command), lazily.
- Sends VERSION in clientInfo.
- runtime.lazy.ts (dynamic import) becomes a direct call.

Tool mapping (tools.ts):
- createMcpToolName: `mcp__<server>__<tool>` sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_], max 64 chars, with an 8-hex sha256 suffix on collision via a callback.
- createMcpResultSchema. Model-facing text is cut in the middle above MCP_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES 20KiB (truncateMiddle at UTF-8/char boundaries) while scripts get the full CallToolResult.
- Binary content spills to tmp `pi-mcp-<hex><ext>` with mode 0600. Resource links point to read_mcp_resource.
- `_meta` is stripped into structuredContent. Progress is forwarded as onUpdate.

Resources (resources.ts):
- Tools list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates and read_mcp_resource with Codex-compatible schemas.
- isMcpAppResource filtering. Servers sorted with localeCompare.

Tests:
- mcp-oauth-refresh runs several stores against a node:http OAuth+MCP server (suite/mcp-oauth-server.ts, the shared helper also used by agent-session-mcp-oauth). Port the helper as a native loopback server.

units.title: MCP extension wiring (session hooks, mcp_servers prompt section, /mcp command and manager UI), pi mcp CLI, built-in extension list
units.notes:
Built-in list (extensions/index.ts):
- builtInExtensions order: llama.cpp (builtin), codemode, tool-search and mcp (replaceable, builtin).
- main.ts prepends them to extension factories. Natively this is a Vec<Box<dyn Extension>> / []Extension.

session_start (index.ts):
- Loads config and starts background connections after one event-loop turn (setImmediate) so the first render happens.
- A `generation` counter drops stale async work after shutdown or restart.
- Servers registered by extensions via pi.getMcpServers() are overridden by mcp.json entries with the same namespace; overridden notices are kept.

ensureDiscoveryActive:
- Activates codemode (exposure codemode, unless autoEnableCodemode=false) or tool_search (exposure deferred), but only the built-in tools, identified by identity predicates.
- Warns once with exact text when neither is reachable.

registerTools:
- Names are assigned stably through toolOwners (`server\0tool`). Every tool whose sanitized name collides gets the hash suffix, independent of order.
- Tools cannot be unregistered: dropped tools are re-registered with exposure "hidden". The native ExtensionAPI must allow re-registering by name to replace a definition.
- syncResourceTools registers the resource tools with the widest exposure (direct > codemode > deferred), else hidden, and deactivates them when they leave direct.

mcp_servers prompt section (renderServersSection, MCP_SERVERS_SECTION="mcp_servers"):
- Lists enabled servers with codemode/deferred tools, sorted with localeCompare. Line format `- <namespace> (codemode|tool_search): <summary>`.
- Size limits: MAX_SERVERS_SECTION_CHARS 4096, MAX_SERVER_DESCRIPTION_CHARS 250, truncation with "…" in UTF-16 lengths. When server lines alone do not fit, the last servers are omitted and counted in a closing line.
- The intro text depends on which reach kinds are used. The output must be byte-identical.

Other hooks:
- before_agent_start waits once per session for servers with direct tools, up to startupWaitMs (default 10000), then notifies "MCP servers are still connecting…".
- tool_call waits (abortable by ctx.signal) for the servers a codemode script names. The rule is regex /\b(searchTools|describeNamespace|describeTool|ALL_TOOLS)\b/ or code.includes(namespace). tool_search and resource tools wait for all pending servers.
- turn_start reconnects needs-auth servers whose stored tokens changed (detects `pi mcp login` run in another process).
- mcp_servers_change adds/removes registered servers; a re-register with a new config replaces the server.
- session_shutdown closes all connections.
- reportProblems emits a single warning "MCP servers need attention:\n  ...\nRun /mcp to fix.".

/mcp command:
- Argument completions for login/logout/reconnect plus a server name.
- Handler: in TUI mode, showMcpManager; otherwise formatStatus text. The usage string is MCP_USAGE.
- pickServer: preferred/eligible logic, ctx.ui.select when ambiguous.
- The login notice uses an OSC 8 hyperlink with "Cmd+click to open" on darwin and "Ctrl+click to open" elsewhere.
- The manager menus (serversMenu sorted by attentionRank then localeCompare; serverMenu items; Tools and Exposure menus) have exact labels and descriptions. Settings changes are saved through updateMcpServerConfig, or apply only to the session for extension-scoped servers.

ui.ts (McpManagerView):
- Menus rebuild on change via subscribe; there are status and redirect-URL input screens.
- The hint is Cmd+click on darwin, Ctrl+click elsewhere. Keys come from keybindings.

`pi mcp` CLI (cli.ts runMcpCommand, used by main.ts):
- HELP text is verbatim and uses chalk.bold/dim (needs chalk-equivalent color detection). `--help` or `-h` anywhere in args prints help, even after `--`.
- parseOptions: `-l` aliases `--local`; known kinds flag/value/list. For add, maxPositionals=2 so a command's own flags pass through. "--" ends options. Unknown option -> `Unknown option X.\n<hint>`.
- add: url XOR command. HTTP-only vs stdio-only option checks. `--bearer-token-env-var` becomes header Authorization `Bearer ${NAME}`. Config key order is url/headers/oauth or command/args/env/cwd, then exposure, description. Validated by validateMcpServerConfig. Global or project (-l) file. Messages Added/Replaced, an untrusted-project note and a check hint.
- remove: hints at the other scope.
- list: connects all enabled servers concurrently (output stays in config order). Text or `--json` (JSON.stringify(...,null,2) with ServerReport key order name, scope, source, enabled, exposure, transport, state, tools, toolExposure?, resources?, resourceTemplates?, error?; top level servers, errors, note?). Exit 1 if anything failed.
- login: connects first; if needs-auth, runs signInMcpServer, showing the URL and opening the browser. With a TTY and no openUrl override it reads a pasted redirect from stdin (readline on stderr) with an abort on timeout; --timeout seconds default 300 uses JS Number() semantics. logout removes credentials.
- --oauth-callback-port uses Number() too, so port a JS ToNumber helper.
- ProjectTrustStore decides project trust. cli.lazy.ts becomes a direct call.

Tests:
- mcp-extension.test covers config, tools, connections and the servers section.
  - It uses in-memory transport pairs and a node:http server.
  - The win32-skipped `~` expansion test writes a Node server.mjs and runs it with process.execPath; replace it with the native fixture binary.
- mcp-command.test reuses packages/mcp/test/fixtures/stdio-server.mjs; switch it to the native fixture.
- Suite tests need harness.ts, createTestUiContext and utilities.ts from the agent-session/test-infra area, plus faux provider fauxToolCall/fauxAssistantMessage.
- agent-session-mcp-oauth probes a free port with node:net and uses suite/mcp-oauth-server.ts (owned by unit coding-agent-ext-mcp-runtime).

hazards: JSON key order and formatting: JSON.stringify output (mcp.json edits, mcp-auth.json, pi mcp list --json, structuredContent rendering, codemode-store entries, globals JSON passed to the prelude) must keep insertion order and JS number formatting; use serde_json preserve_order / ordered maps and a JS-compatible number formatter

UTF-16 length semantics: truncation and limits measured with String.length/slice (mcp_servers section 4096/250 chars, codemode output budget chars, describe/declaration caps like DEFAULT_INPUT_SCHEMA_MAX_CHARS 16000) must count UTF-16 code units, not bytes or Unicode scalars

localeCompare (ICU collation) is used for sorting codemode namespaces, MCP servers in the prompt section and /mcp menu, resource servers, llama models and HF quantizations; native byte-order sort differs for mixed case/punctuation; use a collator (icu4x/x/text/collate) or document the deviation
Array.prototype.sort stability: BM25 ties and catalog selection rely on stable sort (Rust sort_by is stable; Go must use sort.SliceStable)
V8 JSON.parse error messages are embedded in CodemodeSourceError text; native parsers produce different text, so the source.test.ts assertions on those messages need adaptation

WTF-8 strings from QuickJS may contain lone surrogates; Rust String/Go valid-UTF-8 cannot hold them, so convert lossily (U+FFFD) or carry bytes; behavior only differs for scripts emitting lone surrogates

WHATWG URL semantics (origin, pathname with trailing slash, href serialization, IPv6 bracket handling) drive OAuth discovery URLs, issuer comparison, credential store keys (`namespace|url`) and llama URL normalization; Go net/url differs (e.g. empty path vs '/'), so credential keys can silently stop matching TS-written mcp-auth.json
URLSearchParams form encoding (space as '+', specific percent-encode set) and Headers lowercasing must match for OAuth token/registration requests and tests

fetch error model: TS treats TypeError (network failure) and error codes starting with E or UND_ERR as transient for retry and as 'miss' in discovery; native ports need an explicit network-error classification

Process management: process groups, SIGTERM after a 500ms grace then SIGKILL after grace+2000ms, win32 `taskkill /T /F`, and an exit hook killing live server groups; orphaned MCP servers are the failure mode if this is skipped

Cross-process interop: the mcp-auth.json lock (core auth-storage withLock) and the proper-lockfile refresh lock `mcp-auth-refresh-<sha256[:16]>` (stale 20s) must use the exact same lock-dir protocol so TS pi and native pi running concurrently do not double-refresh or corrupt tokens
mcp.json editing must preserve detected indentation (/^([ \t]+)\S/m), other keys and order, and end with a trailing newline, byte-compatible with TS output

Temp files: pi-codemode-<16hex>.txt and pi-mcp-<hex><ext> written in os.tmpdir() with mode 0600 for MCP binaries; mcp.log rotation to mcp.log.1 above 5MiB with synchronous appends and ISO-8601 UTC millisecond timestamps (toISOString format)

Timers and cancellation: AbortSignal.timeout/any compositions (15s llama, 15s refresh, 1s DELETE, 30s/60s request timeouts renewed on progress, 10s startup wait, 5min callback) need explicit child cancellation tokens/contexts; Infinity/<=0 disables timeouts

Microtask/ordering assumptions: the in-memory transport delivers via queueMicrotask after send resolves, and the client handles incoming requests fire-and-forget; native channels must not deliver synchronously inside send or tests relying on ordering can deadlock or reorder

Codemode interrupt must stop both running JS and the pending-job drain loop; rely on host_interrupt polling plus a hard backstop (wasmtime epoch interruption / wazero context close) so runaway scripts and timeouts produce the 'timeout'/'aborted' kinds, not a hung thread
Codemode memory: qjs_set_memory_limit (256MiB from coding-agent) must fail allocations inside the script as a script error; also cap wasm linear memory growth so the host does not OOM
Tool identity: isCodemodeTool/isToolSearchTool compare schema object identity so other extensions' tools of the same name are never activated; native code needs a built-in marker, not name comparison

Tools cannot be unregistered: the MCP extension re-registers dropped/disabled tools with exposure 'hidden'; the native ExtensionAPI must support re-registration replacing a definition by name and the exposure values codemode/deferred/direct/hidden/model-only
Platform text: /mcp login hint and manager say 'Cmd+click' on darwin vs 'Ctrl+click' elsewhere; OSC 8 hyperlinks via tui hyperlink()
JS Number() parsing semantics for `pi mcp` --timeout and --oauth-callback-port ('' -> 0, hex, exponent, whitespace) must be reproduced for identical CLI behavior and error messages
Proxy support: TS fetch goes through undici's global EnvHttpProxyAgent (HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY); native HTTP clients for MCP, OAuth, llama and Hugging Face must use the shared proxy-aware client
The streamable HTTP SSE parser limits are measured in UTF-8 bytes and must handle CRLF split across chunks, BOM, comments, NUL in id, and non-digit retry exactly as tested

Model-facing strings must be byte-identical to TS: codemode description and globals text, TOOL_SEARCH_DESCRIPTION, MCP_TYPESCRIPT_PREAMBLE, rendered declarations, mcp_servers section, MCP placeholders, result headers; changes alter prompts and break tests and prompt-cache parity
js_runtime_dependent: Codemode script execution: model-written JavaScript runs inside QuickJS (quickjs.wasm) with the embedded PRELUDE_SOURCE JS defining the script API. Native handling: keep the same wasm and prelude verbatim and run them with wasmtime (Rust) or wazero (Go). Reimplement quickjs-wasi's JS glue natively: env host imports, wasi shim, WTF-8 marshalling, handle refcounts, host function trampoline, pending-job draining.

Node worker_threads isolation of the VM, with a SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics interrupt flag. Native: a dedicated OS thread or goroutine owning the wasm store, channel messages mirroring runtime/protocol.ts, an AtomicBool polled by host_interrupt, and epoch or context cancellation as a backstop.

CodemodeSandbox `workerUrl` option and config.ts getCodemodeWorkerSpecifier/resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier (JS worker entry resolution for source, bundle and Bun binaries). Native: drop them; getQuickJSWasmPath becomes embedded wasm bytes, with an optional override path.
packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/worker.ts (bundle-only worker entry). Native: delete.
Lazy dynamic imports codemode/execute.lazy.ts, mcp/runtime.lazy.ts, mcp/cli.lazy.ts and pi-ai's llama-cpp-classify.lazy. Native: direct calls; use OnceCell/sync.Once only if startup cost matters.

Built-in extensions are ExtensionFactory closures using pi.on(...) event handlers, registerTool, registerCommand and registerProvider. Native: implement the native Extension trait or interface for llama.cpp, codemode, tool-search and mcp, preserving builtInExtensions order and the replaceable/builtin flags. User TS extensions are not loaded, so pi.registerMcpServer and getMcpServers only receive servers from native extensions.

MCP test fixtures are Node scripts: packages/mcp/test/fixtures/*.mjs, the inline server.mjs in mcp-extension.test.ts, and stdio-server.mjs reused by mcp-command.test.ts. Native: rewrite them as test helper binaries (Rust CARGO_BIN_EXE / Go TestMain re-exec) with identical JSON-RPC replies.
sandbox.test.ts uses node:vm to check that the embedded prelude parses. Native: replace with a QuickJS compile-only eval.

MCP conformance runner: run.ts uses npx to fetch @modelcontextprotocol/conformance and runs client.ts via node --import source-resolver. Native: optional. Build a small native conformance client binary over McpServerConnection + signInMcpServer, and keep using the npx suite and baseline.json from CI.

reports.summary:
Scope: the session core of packages/coding-agent/src/core, 17,082 source lines in 40 files. It covers AgentSession and its runtime/SDK bootstrap, session JSONL persistence, settings, compaction, the model layer (config, composer, runtime, registry, resolver), credential stores, cache warming/stats, nested tool calls and small helpers.

Layering, bottom to top:
1. Persistence and config stores. These have no dependency on AgentSession.
   - SessionManager writes append-only tree-shaped JSONL sessions. Header version 3; entries carry an 8-hex id/parentId; v1->v3 migrations. It builds the LLM projection (compaction-aware, context_edit replacement) and lists sessions concurrently.
   - SettingsManager merges global agentDir/settings.json with project cwd/.pi/settings.json. It has migrations, a lock-protected modified-field-only write path and a serialized write queue.
   - AuthStorage (auth.json) and FileModelsStore (models-store.json) share FileAuthStorageBackend. That backend uses proper-lockfile: sync lock with busy-wait retry, async lock with 30 s stale and jittered backoff. Both stores keep a process-global read-state cache keyed by file revision (dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs).
   - resolve-config-value implements the $VAR / ${VAR} / $$ / $! template language and cached `!command` shell execution used by auth.json keys and models.json headers.
2. Model layer.
   - model-config loads and validates models.json with a typebox schema and exact error text.
   - provider-composer stacks four layers: built-in provider, then models.json (baseUrl/compat/custom models), then extension provider config, then OAuth modifyModels, then modelOverrides. It also composes API-key/OAuth auth and dispatches streaming to the extension, base provider or global API registry.
   - remote-catalog-provider overlays the pi.dev catalog (ETag/Last-Modified, 4 h freshness) on built-in providers.
   - virtual-models defines router-backed `pi-virtual` catalog entries.
   - ModelRuntime wraps pi-ai createModels together with RuntimeCredentials, ModelConfig, the models store, built-in/radius/extension/native providers and virtual models. It exposes snapshots (available/configured/auth), sequence-guarded availability refreshes, per-provider credential queues and routed streamSimple. PI_OFFLINE disables the network.
   - ModelRegistry is the synchronous extension-facing facade over it.
   - model-resolver handles CLI/scope pattern parsing (minimatch nocase, thinking-level suffixes, alias vs dated ids, ambiguity errors) and initial model selection; it calls process.exit on CLI error.
3. Compaction (compaction/**). Token estimation (chars/4 in UTF-16 units, 4800 per image), cut-point selection with split-turn handling, file-operation tracking, exact summarization prompts, and LLM summarization via completeSimple wrapped in retryAssistantCall. branch-summarization does the same for /tree navigation. messages.ts converts custom/bashExecution/summary messages into LLM messages.
4. AgentSession (4,348 lines, split into three units). It wires pi-agent-core Agent hooks:
   - beforeToolCall/afterToolCall;
   - prepareRequest (virtual-model routing, threshold compaction);
   - finishTurn and before_settle boundaries;
   - prepareNextTurnWithContext (system-prompt section diffs, tool loadout);
   - transformContext.
   It also owns event emission, persistence of every message, the tool registry (direct, model-only, codemode, deferred, hidden exposure), prompting with skill/template expansion, steer/follow-up queues, model and thinking management, manual/auto compaction with overflow recovery, auto-retry, bash recording, tree navigation with branch summaries, stats and export.
5. Bootstrap. sdk.createAgentSession restores model/thinking, builds request options (attribution headers, idle timeout, before_provider_headers), starts the CacheWarmer and sets the default stream function. agent-session-services builds the shared services: ModelRuntime, SettingsManager, ResourceLoader and pending provider registrations. AgentSessionRuntime handles session switch/new/fork/import, with teardown order abort -> session_shutdown -> invalidate -> dispose.

Key flows to preserve byte-for-byte:
- Session file creation is lazy: the file is created with `wx` only once an assistant message exists, then appended line by line.
- JSON key order per entry type, and verbatim round-trip of provider message bodies. This needs ordered JSON.
- settings/auth/models-store files are written with JSON.stringify(x, null, 2).
- All exact prompt and summary prefix strings, system-prompt section tags (`<name>...</name>`) and diff patches.
- Session dir naming `--<cwd sanitized>--` and file names `<iso with : and . replaced>_<uuidv7>.jsonl`.

Extensions are native. Every place that calls ExtensionRunner (events, boundaries, providers, virtual routers, tools, cache_warming_decision, inline test extension factories) becomes a native Rust trait / Go interface. The suite harness must accept native test extensions instead of inline JS factories.

Suggested port order: credential stores and session-manager first, then settings, provider composition, model runtime, compaction, session support, the three AgentSession units (ported together before the suite tests run), and bootstrap last.

Tests owned by other areas (not listed here):
- CLI: auth-check, credential-print, initial-message, max-thinking, session-id-readonly, session-file-invalid, startup-session-name, 7269.
- migrations: config-value-migration, 5661.
- Interactive/TUI: session-share, export-jsonl-share, model-catalog-refresh, custom-message, model/session/settings selectors and the regressions importing interactive-mode, rpc-mode or components (3217, 4167, 5080, 5433, 5724, 5868, 5943, 6949, 6999, 7027, 7153, 7209, 7443, 7731, 7829, 8611, 9068, startup-session-rebind).
- tools: 3302, 3303, 5208, 5303, 6104, 6596, tool-system-prompt-contributions, block-images.
- extensions loader / resource-loader: 2781, 6260, 7193, 8237, 8261, 8423, 9540, extension-factory-cache.
- themes: 2791.
- JSON mode: 7290, 7911, 7925.
- package-manager: 7187.
- built-in extensions: suite/agent-session-codemode, -mcp, -mcp-oauth, -tool-orchestration and suite/mcp-oauth-server.ts. These depend on this area's suite harness.

units.title: Session JSONL persistence, tree, projection, listing; LLM message conversion; branch export
units.notes:
Byte-compatible on-disk format.
- CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION=3. Header {type:"session",version,id,timestamp,cwd,parentSession?}.
- Entry types: message, thinking_level_change, model_change, usage, compaction, branch_summary, custom, custom_message, context_edit, label, session_info.
- Key order differs per entry type: custom puts {type,customType,data,id,parentId,timestamp}; most others start with {type,id,parentId,timestamp}. Mirror the TS object-literal order exactly.
- JSON.stringify drops undefined fields.
- Messages must round-trip verbatim, including unknown provider fields. Use serde_json preserve_order or a Value-backed message in Rust, and json.RawMessage or an ordered map in Go.
- Number output must follow the JS Number.prototype.toString algorithm.

Ids and file naming.
- Entry id = randomUUID().slice(0,8), checked for collisions against byId; falls back to a full UUID.
- Session id = uuidv7 from the pi-ai port.
- Dir name: `--${cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/,'').replace(/[/\\:]/g,'-')}--` under agentDir/sessions.
- File name: `${iso.replace(/[:.]/g,'-')}_${id}.jsonl`.

Persistence.
- Lazy flush: nothing is written until the first assistant message (#10000).
- First flush opens with the `wx` flag and writes all entries; later entries use appendFileSync.
- Fork/import writes the header with flag wx.
- loadEntriesFromFile reads 1 MiB chunks through a StringDecoder (invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD), skips malformed lines, validates the header, and appends '\n' when the last line was unterminated.
- readSessionHeader scans at most 1 MiB in 4096-byte chunks.
- Migrations: v1->v2 adds the id tree and maps firstKeptEntryIndex->firstKeptEntryId; v2->v3 renames role hookMessage->custom.

Listing.
- Concurrency limits 10 (cwd) and 64 (all); progress published every 10/100 files.
- File names sorted descending with localeCompare.
- Follows symlinked dirs but ignores links to files (#7497).

Projection (buildSessionProjection/buildSessionContext).
- The newest compaction on the branch wins; the kept range starts at firstKeptEntryId and has system messages filtered out.
- context_edit replaces an entry, or omits it when the replacement is null.
- branch_summary and custom_message become messages; labels and the session_info name are tracked.

messages.ts.
- COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX/SUFFIX and BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREFIX/SUFFIX are exact strings.
- bashExecutionToText format must match.
- convertToLlm maps custom->user, and bashExecution->user unless excludeFromContext.
- Timestamps use new Date(iso).getTime().

session-export re-parents branch entries linearly. Default output name: session-<iso with : and . replaced>.jsonl, resolved against process.cwd().

session-info-modified-timestamp calls initTheme only incidentally; drop that call in the port.

units.title: Settings load/merge/migrate/write with file locking; settings diagnostics; install telemetry flag
units.notes:
Files.
- Global: agentDir/settings.json. Project: cwd/.pi/settings.json (CONFIG_DIR_NAME).
- Settings keys are written in camelCase exactly as in the TS interface.
- Deep merge of project over global. defaultTools merges +name/-name modifiers specially.

Migrations on load:
- queueMode -> steeringMode
- websockets -> transport
- skills object -> array
- retry.maxDelayMs -> retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs
- A UTF-8 BOM is stripped (#8337).

Writes.
- Read the current file under lock, apply only the modified fields (nested-key tracking) onto the on-disk JSON, then JSON.stringify(...,null,2). This preserves unknown keys and the existing key order.
- Writes are serialized through a promise-chain write queue (flush awaits it).
- Lock: proper-lockfile lockSync(path,{realpath:false}) with 10 attempts and a 20 ms synchronous busy-wait. Share the lock helper with coding-agent-credential-stores.
- Project writes require a trusted project.
- Load/parse errors are recorded and drained (drainErrors) for diagnostics.
- The inMemory variant serializes its initial settings through the same migration.

Defaults.
- compaction: reserveTokens 16384, keepRecentTokens 20000. Per-model compaction overrides are keyed provider/modelId and validated as safe non-negative integers.
- retry: 3 attempts, base 2000 ms; provider maxRetryDelayMs defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_RETRY_DELAY_MS (60000).
- cacheWarming is global-only.
- httpIdleTimeoutMs is parsed by http-dispatcher.

Environment variables:
- VISUAL/EDITOR (fallback notepad on win32, otherwise nano)
- PI_CLEAR_ON_SHRINK
- PI_HARDWARE_CURSOR
- PI_TELEMETRY overrides enableInstallTelemetry; truthy values are 1/true/yes, case-insensitive.

The pi-tui imports are type-only (TuiMode, ScrollViewScrollbar, TerminalCapabilities, WheelScrollLines); port them as small enums.

settings-diagnostics only needs the AgentSessionRuntimeDiagnostic type. Define it in a shared types module to avoid a dependency cycle.

Test 3616 needs the DefaultResourceLoader port; 8337 also covers frontmatter BOM handling from utils.

units.title: auth.json AuthStorage + lock backends, config value resolution, runtime credential overlay, models-store.json, auth guidance strings
units.notes:
FileAuthStorageBackend.
- Creates the parent dir with mode 0700 and the file "{}" with mode 0600. The mode applies on creation only.
- Sync lock: lockSync with realpath:false, 10 attempts, 20 ms busy-wait.
- Async lock: lock({retries:0, stale:30000, onCompromised}).
  - On ELOCKED, back off min(10*2^n, 1000) * (1+random) ms, capped at the remaining time of a 30 s deadline. The sleep is abortable.
  - A compromised lock throws.
- proper-lockfile compatibility, so TS pi and the port can share ~/.pi/agent:
  - The lock is a directory `<file>.lock` created with mkdir.
  - Its mtime is refreshed every stale/2.
  - A lock is stale when its mtime is older than stale (default 10 s for the sync lock).
- Writes use JSON.stringify(data,null,2).

AuthStorage.
- A process-global read state is shared per auth path (sharedAuthFileReadState) and validated by getFileRevision = `${dev}:${ino}:${size}:${mtimeNs}:${ctimeNs}` from a bigint stat. Use MetadataExt in Rust and syscall.Stat_t in Go; Windows needs a fallback.
- Concurrent reloads are coalesced with reader counting; the reload is aborted when the reader count drops to 0.
- Without a signal, a failed read falls back to the last snapshot.
- read() resolves api_key values through resolveConfigValue(key, credential.env).
- ReadOnlyAuthStorage validates with exact messages ("Invalid auth.json: expected an object", "Invalid auth.json credential for provider \"x\"").
- InMemoryAuthStorageBackend serializes operations through a promise chain.

resolve-config-value.
- Values starting with '!' are commands. Otherwise they are templates: $NAME or ${NAME} (NAME matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), $$ -> $, $! -> !. An unterminated ${ is a literal $.
- Env lookup is `env[name] || process.env[name] || undefined`: an empty value counts as missing.
- Commands run like execSync(cmd): /bin/sh -c on Unix, 10 s timeout, stdout trimmed, stderr ignored, an empty result becomes undefined.
- On win32, run through getShellConfig (args or stdin transport) and fall back to the default shell on ENOENT.
- Results are cached per process for the cached variant.
- Error messages from resolveConfigValueOrThrow/resolveHeadersOrThrow must match exactly (tests assert them).

FileModelsStore reuses FileAuthStorageBackend on agentDir/models-store.json with the same shared read-state pattern. Reads and writes structuredClone entries.

RuntimeCredentials overlays non-persistent API keys over a CredentialStore.

auth-guidance strings join getDocsPath() with providers.md and models.md.

units.title: models.json schema/config, provider layer composition, remote pi.dev catalog overlay, virtual models, provider attribution headers
units.notes:
model-config.
- models.json is read with comments stripped (stripJsonComments) and BOM removed, then validated against the typebox schema.
- Error format: `Invalid models.json schema:\n  - <path>: <msg>\n\nFile: <path>`. The port must reproduce typebox's instance paths and messages for the tested cases.

provider-composer: getAllModels applies these layers in order:
1. Built-in provider models.
2. applyModelsJson: baseUrl and compat on all models (radius keeps its own baseUrl); custom models upserted by chat id, with defaults from findModelDefaults; defaults contextWindow 128000 and maxTokens 16384.
3. applyExtension: replace the model list, or override baseUrl only.
4. OAuth modifyModels (chat models only).
5. modelOverrides (chat models only; topmost layer).
- mergeCompat deep-merges openRouterRouting, vercelGatewayRouting, chatTemplateKwargs and chatTemplateArgs.
- All thrown error strings are asserted by model-registry tests.
- composeApiKeyAuth covers: inherited auth, configured key (env-name presence check, command values treated as configured), the default login prompt "Enter API key", headers resolved with env context, and authHeader adding `Authorization: Bearer`.
- adaptOAuth maps the legacy OAuthLoginCallbacks onto the new interaction API.
- Streaming dispatch order: extension streamSimple when model.api matches; else the base provider if it supports the api; else the global compat API registry (getApiProvider).
- Image and classifier dispatch also fall back to error results.
- configuredRequestAuthStatus sources: models_json_command, environment (with env names as the label), fallback (extension apiKey), models_json_key.

virtual-models.
- VIRTUAL_MODEL_API="pi-virtual"; the state entry customType is "pi.virtual-model-state".
- createVirtualModel maps unsupported levels to null in the thinkingLevelMap.
- withVirtualModels hides physical chat models that share an id with a virtual model; a missing provider gets a keyless provider.
- Unrouted stream error: `Virtual model p/id must be routed before streaming`.
- getBranchSelection semantics must match the tests.

remote-catalog-provider.
- Request: GET `${base}/api/models/providers/${encodeURIComponent(id)}?types=chat,image,classifier` with accept, User-Agent and if-none-match. The If-None-Match header is sent only when the stored model list is non-empty.
- 4 s per-attempt timeout via fetchWithRetry; 4 h freshness window.
- 304: only checkedAt moves. 404/501: lastModified 0, no etag. Other non-OK: persist checkedAt, then throw.
- Last-Modified is parsed like Date.parse of an RFC 1123 date; NaN becomes 0.
- The overlay applies only when lastModified > the bundled generatedAt.
- Models merge keyed by `${type}\u0000${id}`.

provider-attribution.
- openrouter: provider match or substring "openrouter.ai" in baseUrl. nvidia and cloudflare: matched by WHATWG URL hostname.
- These headers are gated by isInstallTelemetryEnabled.
- opencode session headers x-opencode-session and x-opencode-client.
- Merge order: session headers, then attribution headers, then the given sources.

Extension-provided callbacks (streamSimple, refreshModels, oauth.*, images, classifiers, route) become native trait objects.

units.title: ModelRuntime (pi-ai Models wrapper with auth, catalogs, virtual routing) and ModelRegistry facade; radius constants
units.notes:
ModelRuntime.create({credentials, modelsPath (null disables), modelsStore, allowModelNetwork}).
- Wraps pi-ai createModels with RuntimeCredentials, ModelConfig and FileModelsStore (or the in-memory store).

units.notes:
Token estimation.
- estimateTokens = ceil(chars/4), where chars is the JS string .length (UTF-16 code units). Each image counts as 4800 chars. Do not use byte or char counts.
- estimateContextTokens uses the last assistant usage plus trailing estimates.
- shouldCompact: tokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens.

Cut points (findCutPoint / prepareCompaction).
- Valid cut points are user/assistant/custom message entries, never tool results.
- Split turns produce a turn-prefix summary, merged with `\n\n---\n\n**Turn Context (split turn):**\n\n`.
- Follows the recovery-omission suffix rule.
- Works with a previous compaction (iterative UPDATE prompt).

Prompts and serialization.
- File operations are tracked from read/write/edit tool calls and rendered as <read-files>/<modified-files> blocks.
- Prompt constants must be byte-identical: SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT, SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT, UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT, TURN_PREFIX_*, BRANCH_SUMMARY_*.
- serializeConversation format and truncation (UTF-16 slice) must match; nested tool call records are serialized too.

LLM call.
- completeSummarization calls completeSimple with cacheRetention "none" and sessionId ?? uuidv7(), wrapped in retryAssistantCall with the retry settings and callbacks.
- maxTokens = min(floor(0.8*reserve), model.maxTokens); the turn prefix uses 0.5; branch summaries use min(4096, ...).
- Reasoning/thinking levels are passed through (compaction-summary-reasoning test).

usage-totals: combineUsage keeps the optional cacheWrite1h/reasoning fields only when either side has them. getUsageCostBreakdown sorts by cost descending.

compaction.test.ts contains a 'LLM summarization' describe gated on ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN. Skip that block only; port the rest.

units.title: Cache warmer and cache-miss stats, nested tool calls, system prompt builder, event bus, defaults, timings, diagnostics types, experimental flag
units.notes:
CacheWarmer.
- Replays the last request with maxTokens 1 and maxRetries 0 before the cache TTL expires.
- delay = max(1, floor(min(0.9*ttl, ttl-10s))). TTL comes from model.promptCache[short|long]; PI_CACHE_RETENTION is read via getProviderEnvValue.
- Refresh deadline = nextWarmAt + floor((ttl-delay)/2). Age limits: 60 min while streaming, 30 min idle.
- Economics: warm if continuationProbability*missCost - warmCost >= $0.05, with continuation probability 1 while streaming and 0.15 idle.
- Anthropic budget thinking without forceAdaptiveThinking is not replayable.
- The decide hook maps to the extension cache_warming_decision event; failures fall back to pi's decision.
- Appends a usage entry with kind cache_warm.
- Exact status/usage strings: toFixed(3), and toFixed(6) followed by the regex /(\.\d{3}\d*?)0+$/.
- Timers are unref'd. Port with tokio::time / time.AfterFunc plus cancellation.

cache-stats.
- Noise floor 1024 tokens; resets on compaction and branch_summary; cache_warm usage entries seed the baseline.
- Results are a Map keyed by AssistantMessage object identity. Key by entry id or index in the port.

nested-tool-calls.
- Limits: maxCalls 256, args 8 KiB per call and 32 KiB total, measured as UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify(args). Error text is sliced to 500 UTF-16 units.
- Nested ids are `${callerId}/${n}`.
- Exclusive calls are serialized through queueTail, and a holder's own nested calls do not wait on it.
- Durations are round(performance.now() delta).
- Usage is summed with combineUsage.

system-prompt.
- Sections are ordered: preamble, tools, rules, docs, addendum, project_context, skills, cwd, plus custom sections.
- Section names must match /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/. Each is wrapped as `<name>\n...\n</name>`.
- diffSystemPromptSections returns a patch with null for removed sections.
- Docs/readme/example paths come from config helpers. Preamble text must be exact.

event-bus.
- Fire-and-forget emit.
- Async handlers' errors are logged as `Event handler error (<channel>):`.
- on() returns an unsubscribe function; clear() removes all handlers.

defaults: DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL=medium and the THINKING_LEVEL_OPTIONS order.

timings: PI_TIMING=1 is read once at startup; output format goes to stderr.

experimental: PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1.

units.title: AgentSession part 1: types, constructor, auth resolution, agent hooks, request projection, boundaries, agent event handling and persistence
units.notes:
Why agent-session.ts is split. The file is 4348 lines, over the 3500 limit, so it is split at its own section banners:
- L1-1385: setup, hooks and the event core
- L1386-2666: state, tools, prompting, queues, model and thinking
- L2667-4348: compaction, extensions, retry, bash, tree, stats, export
All three parts implement one struct (Rust: impl blocks spread over several files of the agent_session module; Go: methods spread over files of the same package). Port them together before running the suite tests.

This part contains:
- Exported types: AgentSessionEvent union (agent events with parentToolCallId plus queue_update, compaction_start/end, auto_retry_*, summarization_retry_*, entry_appended, session_info_changed, thinking_level_changed, agent_settled, bash_execution_update), AgentSessionConfig, PromptOptions, SessionStats, ExtensionBindings.
- parseSkillBlock regex `^<skill name="([^"]+)" location="([^"]+)">\n([\s\S]*?)\n</skill>(?:\n\n([\s\S]+))?$`.
- Required request auth (formatNoApiKeyFoundMessage).
- _installAgentToolHooks: beforeToolCall/afterToolCall dispatch tool_call/tool_result to extensions, normalize tool-result images and record nested calls.
- _installAgentRequestProjection: prepareRequest performs virtual-model routing and threshold compaction before the request.
- Boundary hooks: finishTurn for turn_end and agent_before_settle drafts, previews and commit.
- _installAgentNextTurnRefresh.
- _handleAgentEvent: persists message_end into the session; _replaceMessageInPlace mutates the same object that agent state holds; custom messages are deferred to turn end (#8537); the agent_end willRetry flag.
- subscribe, dispose.

Porting hazards:
- The pi-agent-core port must expose the same hook points (beforeToolCall, afterToolCall, prepareRequest, finishTurn, prepareNextTurnWithContext, transformContext) and runToolCall.
- Identity maps (_entryIdsByMessage, _boundaryDispatchedMessages, WeakMap/WeakSet over message objects) need stable message ids or Arc pointers.
- Listener callbacks are synchronous, while extension handlers are awaited sequentially. Event order is asserted heavily by the suite tests.

Test harnesses.
- suite/harness.ts builds an AgentSession on the faux provider: registerFauxProvider, SettingsManager.inMemory, AuthStorage.inMemory, an in-memory ModelRuntime, and optional models.json.
- Its `extensionFactories` must become native test extensions implementing the extension trait.
- utilities.ts helpers (createTestResourceLoader, createTestExtensionsResult, userMsg/assistantMsg, buildTestTree) are shared by many units.
- test-harness.ts is the legacy faux stream harness; port it only together with its own test.

units.notes:
Compaction.
- _runDefaultCompaction calls compact() with the summarization auth/route, retry settings and summarization_retry callbacks.
- Manual compact() aborts the current run first.
- _checkCompaction has three cases: overflow with retry (removes the failed assistant message, compacts, retries once), overflow without retry, and threshold.
- _runAutoCompaction emits session_before_compact, which a hook may cancel or answer with a custom summary. It emits compaction_start/end with a reason and willRetry. The cancellation semantics are tested by #9340/#9777.

Extensions and reload.
- bindExtensions/_bindExtensionCore installs the ExtensionRunner actions (sendMessage, setActiveTools, setSessionName with newlines filtered (#5996), registerProvider, and so on) as native trait callbacks.
- _refreshToolRegistry builds the tool registry from built-in tool definitions (createAllToolDefinitions) plus extension tools, applying allowlist/excludelist (#5109) and synthetic source info.
- _buildRuntime creates the extension ModelRegistry facade.
- reload() calls resetApiProviders, reloads resources and re-emits session_start.

Auto-retry.
- _prepareRetry uses isRetryableAssistantError and retryDelayMs(baseDelay, attempt) with a cap from the provider maxRetryDelayMs. The abortable sleep emits auto_retry_start/end with exact messages; the explicit provider retry message is tested by #6019.

Bash.
- executeBash/recordBashResult: results are deferred while streaming and flushed before the next prompt; bash_execution_update events are emitted; abortBash aborts all running commands.

Tree navigation.
- navigateTree can summarize the abandoned branch (session_before_tree may return a custom summary with usage) and emits session_tree. The ambient auth path is tested by #6324.

Stats and export.
- getSessionStats sums tokens/cost over branch entries including summaries and tool usage.
- getContextUsage estimates usage.
- exportToHtml falls back to the active theme when the configured theme is missing (#5596).
- exportToJsonl and summarizeForBugReport.

hazards: UTF-16 semantics. String .length and .slice are used for token estimation (chars/4), error truncation (500 chars), conversation truncation and compaction. Count UTF-16 code units, not bytes or Unicode scalar values.

localeCompare ordering is used for session file names, session info and model id sorting. Use ICU collation (icu_collator / golang.org/x/text/collate), or confirm that ASCII-only inputs make plain ordering equivalent.
Date handling. toISOString format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ; Date.parse of ISO and RFC 1123 Last-Modified values; NaN mapped to 0 or null; file-name timestamp replacement /[:.]/g -> '-'.

proper-lockfile interop. TS pi and the native port may run concurrently on the same ~/.pi/agent, so lock-directory naming, stale thresholds (10 s default, 30 s async auth), mtime refresh and compromise detection must stay compatible. The sync lock uses a 20 ms CPU busy-wait retry (10 attempts).

Process-global caches. sharedAuthFileReadState and sharedModelsFileReadState (read state per path, validated by file revision dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs), the resolve-config-value command cache, setDefaultStreamFn, the compat API registry reset on reload (resetApiProviders), and cleanupSessionResources per session id. Windows needs a getFileRevision fallback (file index plus times).

Event semantics. AgentSession listeners are called synchronously, _handleAgentEvent is async and awaited by the agent, and extension handlers run sequentially. Suite tests assert exact event order: message_end persistence before tool_call handlers (#1717), agent_end willRetry, agent_settled after retries, queue_update.

Object identity. WeakMap/WeakSet/Map keyed by message objects (_entryIdsByMessage, _boundaryDispatchedMessages, cache-stats misses, NestedCallRecorder startedAt). _replaceMessageInPlace mutates the shared message object so agent state and session stay consistent. Use shared ownership (Arc<Mutex>) or stable ids.

Lazy session persistence (#10000). No file is created until an assistant message exists, then the file is opened with the wx flag. Forks and imports must not overwrite existing files (wx / COPYFILE_EXCL with -N suffix).

Timers. CacheWarmer setTimeout is unref'd (must not keep the process alive). Retry sleeps are abortable. Wall-clock (Date.now) and performance.now are mixed; tests use vi.useFakeTimers, so ports need an injectable clock.
process.exit(1) inside findInitialModel and console.error output (chalk) from library code; the port must preserve the CLI-visible behavior without exiting from library code paths used by tests.

Shell execution of `!command` config values: execSync uses /bin/sh -c on Unix (with the inherited environment) and the configured shell on win32. Results are cached per process (except the uncached header path) and time out after 10 s.

PI_OFFLINE, PI_TELEMETRY, PI_TIMING (read once at module load), PI_EXPERIMENTAL, PI_RADIUS_GATEWAY, PI_CACHE_RETENTION, VISUAL/EDITOR, PI_CLEAR_ON_SHRINK and PI_HARDWARE_CURSOR all change behavior. Tests stub env vars, so make env access injectable.

Exact user-visible strings are asserted by tests: models.json schema errors, provider composition errors, config resolution errors, auth.json validation errors, retry/compaction messages, cache-warming status lines, the system prompt text and summarization prompts.

Replace with a native ExtensionProvider trait whose implementations are compiled in. Pure-data registrations (models, baseUrl, headers, apiKey) also stay available from models.json.

Rust:

- `ExtensionContext` as a cheap clone holding an Arc to runner state.

Go:
- `type Extension interface{ Name() string; Register(*ExtensionAPI) error }`.
- Typed `On<Event>` registration methods.
- `ToolDefinition` interface.

Keep the event type strings verbatim; they appear in error reports (`event` field).
