units.title: ExtensionRunner event dispatch, contexts, tool wrapper, extensions barrel
units.notes:
The runner owns ordered extensions, the bound runtime and contexts. Behaviors to port verbatim:

Event dispatch:
- snapshotEventHandlers copies the handler list per emit, so handlers registered during an emit do not run in that emit.
- emit(): errors are caught per handler and sent to onError listeners as {extensionPath, event, error, stack}. session_before_* stops at the first `cancel: true`.
- emitToolCall has no catch, so errors propagate to the agent loop. The first `block` short-circuits.
- emitUserBash fails closed. isUserBashEventResult requires exactly one of `operations` (with an exec fn) or `result` (output string, exitCode, cancelled, truncated, optional fullOutputPath); otherwise it throws.
- emitContext: structuredClone the messages, run the `context` handlers, then `context_with_system` with the system message restored via getCurrentSystemMessage. The leading-system-message check must use stable identity (index or id), not pointer equality.
- emitInput: chain transform results; stop on handled.
- emitBeforeAgentStart: chained systemPrompt; forceSystemPrompt; the systemPrompt getter renders via buildSystemPrompt/normalizeBuildSystemPromptOptions.
- emitMessageEnd: a replacement must keep the role.
- emitToolResult: replacing content without structuredContent deletes structuredContent.
- emitCacheWarmingDecision: the last override wins.
- emitProjectTrust: the first yes/no wins; undecided falls through.
- emitBeforeProviderRequest/Headers mutate in place.
- emitBoundary (turn_end, agent_before_settle): recreate the context after each handler; an invalid result yields empty entries.
- withUIPrompt: depth counter; ui_prompt_start/end are queued after the current task. Use a deferred task queue in Rust/Go and order them before the next await.

Registration and lookup:
- getShortcuts: RESERVED_KEYBINDINGS_FOR_EXTENSION_CONFLICTS and buildBuiltinKeybindings, keys lowercased. Diagnostics text is verbatim, e.g. "Extension shortcut '${key}' from ${path} conflicts with built-in shortcut. Skipping." Without a UI, warnings go to stderr.
- resolveRegisteredCommands: duplicates are renamed `name:N`.
- getAllRegisteredTools: first wins.

Binding and lifecycle:
- bindCore flushes queued provider and virtual-model registrations, reporting errors with event register_provider / register_virtual_model. It also installs the McpServerRegistry change listener, which emits mcp_servers_change and reportUnhandledMcpServers (event register_mcp_server).
- invalidate() marks contexts stale with the long stale message.
- createToolContext.executeTool fallback returns an isError result with the text "Nested tool calls are not available in this context" and toolCall id `${toolCallId}/0`.
- noOpUIContext defaults.

  - registerMcpServer validate, owner and namespace clash checks, deep clone.
- Commit/discard: registrations stage in pending state and apply on commit; a factory failure discards them and marks the extension failed (regression 8423).
- registerVirtualModel wraps the route with a fresh context.
- loadExtensionFromFactory, loadExtensions, loadExtensionsCached. The cache keyed by cwd and generation becomes a native factory-instance cache; the extension-factory-cache test should assert factory invocation counts.
- Discovery: resolveExtensionEntries (package.json pi.extensions, then index.ts, then index.js), discoverExtensionsInDir (direct files *.ts/*.js plus one subdir level), discoverAndLoadExtensions order: project .pi/extensions, agentDir/extensions, then configured paths.
- Non-builtin, non-inline file paths produce an error entry formatted "Failed to load extension: <path>: ...". Use one fixed message for JS/TS extensions being unsupported, and keep the error list order.

resource-loader.ts:
- HOST_PROVIDED_EXTENSION_PACKAGES warnings.
- mergeExtensionWarnings dedupes by path.
- omitReplacedExtensions: built-ins flagged replaceable are dropped when another extension registers the same tool:/command:/flag: name. The warning mentions `pi config`; text verbatim.
- loadContextFileFromDir candidates in order: AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, AGENTS.MD, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.MD.
- findShadowedContextFile handles nested worktree, bare repo and submodule layouts via findGitPaths.
- loadProjectContextFiles: global first, then ancestors root to cwd.
- reload(): resolveProjectTrust pre-pass via loadProjectTrustExtensions; CLI metadata {source:cli, scope:temporary, origin:top-level}.
- Conflict diagnostics: `Tool "x" conflicts with P` and `Flag "--x" conflicts with P`.
- dedupePrompts and dedupeThemes produce collision diagnostics (winnerPath, loserPath, `<builtin>`). mapSkillPath maps a dir to SKILL.md. mergePaths uses canonicalizePath.
- SYSTEM.md and APPEND_SYSTEM.md: project copies only when trusted.
- loadThemes uses getTerminalColorMode(detectCapabilities(() => false)) and loadThemeFromPath.
- Inline factories are named `<inline:N>` or `<inline:name>` (regression 6260).

pi-manifest.ts: readPiManifest returns null on parse failure or when `pi` is not an object, and keeps only string-array fields extensions/skills/prompts/themes (regression 7187).

Tests that write JS extension files: convert to native factory registrations. Drop cases that only exercise jiti resolution (pi-ai subpaths, OAuth barrel, node_modules resolution, syntax errors, missing default export) and replace them with one 'JS extension path yields unsupported error' case.

units.title: Agent Skills discovery/validation and prompt template loading/expansion
units.notes:
skills.ts:
- Name regex ^[a-z0-9-]+$, max 64 chars, no leading/trailing or double hyphens per the spec checks. Description required, max 1024.
- A SKILL.md at a directory root makes the dir a skill and stops recursion. .gitignore/.ignore/.fdignore are honored through the node-ignore matcher with path prefixing.
- Symlinked dirs and files are followed via stat. Hidden dirs and node_modules are skipped.
- Collision diagnostics keep the first loaded skill. disable-model-invocation frontmatter is respected.
- formatSkillsForPrompt XML output (escaping of & < > " ') must match byte for byte.

prompt-templates.ts:
- parseCommandArgs uses JS /\s/, i.e. Unicode whitespace including NBSP and U+FEFF, so do not use ASCII-only checks.
- substituteArgs regex /\$\{(\d+|ARGUMENTS|@):-([^}]*)\}|\$\{@:(\d+)(?::(\d+))?\}|\$(ARGUMENTS|@|\d+)/g:
  - single pass, no recursive substitution;
  - `${N:-d}` falls back when empty;
  - slice start 0 is treated as 1;
  - parseInt on huge digit strings must not panic (use saturating parse).
- Description falls back to the first non-blank body line, truncated to 60 UTF-16 code units plus "...". Rust/Go must count UTF-16 units, not bytes or chars, for parity.
- Template name is the basename minus `.md`. Directories are scanned non-recursively; broken symlinks are skipped.
- Source info: under agentDir/prompts it is user scope, under cwd/.pi/prompts project scope, otherwise local with a baseDir.
- expandPromptTemplate regex ^\/([^\s]+)(?:\s+([\s\S]*))?$ .

units.title: Package manager: npm/git/local sources, resource resolution, filters, install/update
units.notes:
A single 2760-line file. It is under the 3500-line split threshold, so it stays one unit. Natural internal seam: free functions L1-L811 (env, patterns, collectors, filters) vs the DefaultPackageManager class L812-end.

Port the command execution (runCommand, runCommandCapture, runCommandSync, spawn) behind an injectable CommandRunner trait/interface. package-manager.test.ts stubs these private methods, and the tests should assert the same argv arrays.

Resolution and precedence:
- resourcePrecedenceRank: builtin 5, package 4, project local 0 / auto 1, user local 2 / auto 3.
- resolve(): project packages first, dedupe by identity, then local entries, then auto-discovery (extensions/skills/prompts/themes plus ancestor .agents/skills up to the git root), then builtins with `-builtin:x` overrides.
- Filter patterns: plain, `!` exclude, `+` force-include, `-` force-exclude.
- matchesAnyPattern tries minimatch (default options, so dotfiles are not matched by *) against the relative path, basename and absolute posix path. For SKILL.md it also tries the parent variants.
- expandPackageGlob: fs.globSync(cwd=root), drop entries with dot segments, sort.

Sources and versions:
- parseSource: `npm:` prefix; npm spec regex ^(@?[^@]+(?:\/[^@]+)?)(?:@(.+))?$; local path detection; git URL parsing via utils/git.ts (ssh, https, shorthand).
- semver gt/maxSatisfying/rcompare/satisfies/valid/validRange use npm semantics.
- getLatestNpmVersion runs `npm view <spec> version --json`. NETWORK_TIMEOUT_MS is 10000. Update concurrency is 4.
- getPackageManagerName: detect npm, pnpm or bun from the npmCommand setting, including `--` separators and wrapper commands. Error "Ambiguous npmCommand package managers".
- Install flags:
  - npm: `--prefix <dir> --legacy-peer-deps`;
  - pnpm: config flags;
  - bun: `--cwd --omit=peer`.

On-disk layout (byte-compatible):
- Roots: agentDir/npm, agentDir/git/<host>/<path>, and tmp/extensions/<prefix>/<sha256 of `${prefix}-${suffix}${ref ? @ref : ''}`, first 8 hex chars>.
- package.json `{"name":"pi-extensions","private":true}`, pretty-printed with a 2-space indent and no trailing newline.
- .gitignore `*\n!.gitignore\n`; markPathIgnoredByCloudSync.
- Git update marker `.<name>.pi-update-incomplete`. Update sequence: fetch, reset --hard, clean -fdx, then repair missing deps.
- ls-remote runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
- resolveManagedPath refuses paths outside the root: "Refusing to use path outside package install root".
- The project scope asserts trust: "Project is not trusted; refusing to access project package storage".

Process and environment:
- spawn stdio is inherit, or [ignore, stderr, stderr] when stdout is taken over (output-guard).
- runCommandCapture error format: `${cmd} ${args} failed with code N: stderr||stdout`, or `timed out after Nms`. It resolves trimmed stdout.
- getEnv falls back to /proc/self/environ on Linux. PI_OFFLINE skips network.
- Legacy global roots: `npm root -g`, `bun pm bin -g`, `pnpm list -g --depth 0 --json`.

git-update.test.ts uses a real local git binary (no network); keep it as an integration test gated on git availability.

units.title: Project trust store/resolution, MCP server config registry, bug report and crash log
units.notes:
trust-manager.ts:
- agentDir/trust.json: an object of path to boolean, keys sorted, JSON.stringify with indent 2 plus a trailing newline. Lookup uses the nearest ancestor.
- Locking mirrors proper-lockfile lockSync(dir, {realpath:false, lockfilePath:'trust.json.lock'}): mkdir of the lock directory, stale detection by mtime, 10 attempts with a 20ms busy wait. Interop with a concurrently running TS pi requires the same lock-dir protocol.
- getProjectTrustOptions labels, verbatim: "Trust", "Trust parent folder (P)", "Trust (this session only)", "Do not trust", "Do not trust (this session only)".
- hasTrustRequiringProjectResources checks .pi/settings.json, mcp.json, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, SYSTEM.md, APPEND_SYSTEM.md, and ancestor .agents/skills excluding ~/.agents/skills.

project-trust.ts:
- resolveProjectTrusted order: override, no resources (true), extension project_trust event (remember means store.set), store, defaultProjectTrust always/never/ask, no UI (false), UI select.
- Prompt text, verbatim: `Trust project folder?\n${cwd}\n\nThis allows ${APP_NAME} to load ${CONFIG_DIR_NAME} settings and resources, install missing project packages, and execute project extensions.`

mcp-servers.ts:
- Pure validation with exact error strings, the codemode-deferred to codemode exposure alias, and mcpNamespace (`mcp__` + name with - replaced by _).
- getMcpToolExposure: `*` glob patterns; an exact match wins.
- isLoopbackRedirectUri. URL.canParse maps to WHATWG-ish parsing (Rust `url` crate; in Go net/url is looser, so add extra checks).
- McpServerRegistry has a single change listener. There are no direct tests here; it is covered by the built-in mcp extension tests in another area.

bug-report.ts:
- SENSITIVE_KEY (case-insensitive) is applied after a camelCase-to-snake split. redactUrl handles nested schemes; redactJsonValue redacts recursively.
- Metadata: schemaVersion 1, uuidv7 id, environment (os.release/os.version, runtime string).
- Archive files: report.json, diagnostics.json, session.jsonl, summary.md. Zip name `pi-bug-report-${id}.zip`.
- Summary via completeSummarization using 60% of the context window and maxTokens at least 4096.
- In bug-report.test.ts, port only the redaction describe blocks. The reportBug UI flow belongs to the interactive area.

bug-report-upload.ts: multipart POST to `${getRadiusGatewayUrl()}/v1/bug-reports`.

crash-log.ts:
- agentDir/crashes.json keeps at most 5 records within 7 days, with a `notified` flag.
- Stack attribution maps stack frame paths to extension sourceInfo, case-insensitive on Windows, using regexes with the /u flag. Native panics produce different backtraces, so keep the attribution function for test parity and feed it native frame paths.

units.title: App keybindings manager, git footer data provider, HTTP dispatcher config
units.notes:
keybindings.ts:
- KEYBINDINGS = TUI_KEYBINDINGS plus app.* ids with defaults and descriptions.
- Platform-dependent defaults (win32, WSL detection, darwin tree keys) must be computed the same way.
- KEYBINDING_NAME_MIGRATIONS: migrateKeybindingsConfig renames legacy keys; orderKeybindingsConfig orders keys by definition order.
- agentDir/keybindings.json is loaded with BOM stripping.
- KeybindingsManager extends the TUI manager. Use composition in Rust/Go.
- keybindings-migration.test.ts calls runMigrations from migrations.ts (another area); port it once migrations exist.

footer-data-provider.ts:
- findGitPaths resolves .git as a dir, or as a file with `gitdir:` (worktrees, submodules, commondir), plus reftable detection.
- Branch read from HEAD. When HEAD is `.invalid` (reftable), run `git symbolic-ref`.
- Watch the HEAD directory with fs.watch (notify/fsnotify). Paths under WSL /mnt use watchFile polling instead.
- 500ms debounce; retry timer FS_WATCH_RETRY_DELAY_MS on watcher error. The watcher must never crash the process.
- Extension status map and available provider count.
- The tests mock child_process and fs.watch, so inject a watcher factory and a git command runner.

http-dispatcher.ts:
- parseHttpIdleTimeoutMs / formatHttpIdleTimeoutMs and HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_CHOICES (30 sec, 1 min, 2 min, 5 min, disabled; default 300000).
- applyHttpProxySettings writes HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars.
- configureHttpDispatcher installs undici EnvHttpProxyAgent {allowH2:false, proxyTunnel:true, bodyTimeout=headersTimeout=idle, autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout:2000}.
- Native: a process-wide shared HTTP client builder. Rust reqwest: http1_only, read_timeout, proxy from env with NO_PROXY. Go: http.Transport with a fresh httpproxy.FromEnvironment config (not the cached ProxyFromEnvironment), ForceAttemptHTTP2=false, ResponseHeaderTimeout, and a per-read idle deadline on the body.
- http-dispatcher.test.ts starts local HTTP/CONNECT proxy servers. Port it with a local TCP proxy in the test.

hazards: Ordering: JS Map/object insertion order drives the order of extensions, handlers, tools, commands, flags, skills, prompts, themes and diagnostics. Use IndexMap (Rust) or ordered slices (Go), never HashMap iteration.
Description truncation (prompt templates at 60, skills limits at 64/1024) counts UTF-16 code units in JS. Count the same way to match validation results.
structuredClone in emitContext/registerMcpServer and identity checks (sameMessages by reference) need explicit deep clones and index/id-based identity natively.
Microtask ordering: ui_prompt_start/end are emitted with queueMicrotask; the runner's withUIPrompt depth counter must produce the same event order relative to awaits.
Error propagation differences: emitToolCall rethrows, emitUserBash fails closed on an invalid result, and all other events catch and report. Getting these wrong changes security behavior.
Stale context: every ExtensionContext getter after invalidate() must return the exact stale error. Long-lived closures in Rust (Arc) and Go (pointers) must check a generation counter.

Process env mutation: applyHttpProxySettings and PI_OFFLINE set env vars. Rust 2024 std::env::set_var is unsafe; Go http.ProxyFromEnvironment caches env on first use, so use httpproxy.FromEnvironment per configure.
The Linux /proc/self/environ fallback in package-manager getEnv must be replicated (it exists for env vars hidden from process.env).
proper-lockfile interop: a TS and a native pi running concurrently must agree on the lock dir protocol (trust.json.lock directory, mtime-based staleness, 10 retries with a 20ms busy wait).
Platform-specific keybinding defaults (win32, WSL, darwin) and Windows case-insensitive path comparisons in crash-log attribution and canonicalizePath.
WSL /mnt paths need polling instead of inotify. fs.watch errors must be swallowed and retried, never crash (see regression 2791 in the theme area).
Package-manager tests stub private methods (runCommand, runCommandCapture, spawn). Without an injectable runner the tests cannot be ported, and real npm/git calls would run.
The npm semver range semantics differ from Cargo semver and Masterminds (prerelease inclusion, x-ranges, || unions).
minimatch default options (no dot matching, no matchBase) and node-ignore negation/dir-only semantics must match exactly, or resource filtering silently changes.
The source-info.ts <-> package-manager.ts type import cycle (PathMetadata) must be broken by moving PathMetadata into source_info.

Built-in replacement: replaceable built-ins (mcp, codemode, llama, tool-search) are omitted when a user extension registers the same tool/command/flag. With no user JS extensions natively this rarely triggers, but keep the logic for native inline extensions and the warning text.
js_runtime_dependent: Loading user TS/JS extensions from .pi/extensions, agentDir/extensions, settings paths and package pi.extensions via jiti. Native handling: still discover and list these paths, but load nothing. Emit a per-path load error ('Failed to load extension: <path>: ...not supported') so diagnostics and `pi config` listings stay stable.
Virtual modules and import aliases (virtual-modules.ts, jiti-loader.ts, jiti-static-loader.ts) that expose @earendil-works/* packages to extensions. Native handling: drop entirely.

Extension module cache keyed by cwd and generation (loadExtensionsCached/clearExtensionCache). Native handling: cache native factory instances keyed by the same inputs; adapt extension-factory-cache.test to count factory invocations.
Node SEA/bundled-binary detection for the jiti mode (isBunBinary, isBundledNode). Native handling: drop; the 8237 and 9540 regressions are skipped.

ExtensionAPI.registerProvider with JS streamSimple and OAuth callback functions. Native handling: providers are trait objects/interfaces from the ai package and are only registrable by native built-in or inline extensions.
InlineExtension factories passed through the SDK. Native handling: a Rust closure/trait object or Go func registered via SDK options, keeping `<inline:N>`/`<inline:name>` naming.

Built-in extensions (mcp, codemode, llama, tool-search) supplied as `builtin:<name>` factories. Native handling: a static registry of native Extension implementations. Codemode runs quickjs-wasi WASM via wasmtime/wazero (owned by another area).

Tests that write JS extension source to temp dirs (extensions-runner, extensions-discovery, extensions-input-event, regression suites). Native handling: rewrite as native factories; drop the jiti-resolution-only cases.

HOST_PROVIDED_EXTENSION_PACKAGES warnings about extensions depending on host packages. Native handling: keep the manifest/package.json inspection and warning text for parity, though only JS packages trigger it.

npm/pnpm/bun installation of extension packages. Native handling: still run the external package manager, since packages also ship skills, prompts and themes; their JS extension entries yield unsupported errors.

Bug report runtime string (node/<version>) and crash-log JS stack-trace attribution. Native handling: report rust/<ver> or go/<ver>, and feed native backtrace frame paths into the same attribution function.
undici global dispatcher installation (setGlobalDispatcher). Native handling: configure the shared HTTP client used by the ai package.

reports.summary:
Area ca-core-tools-utils is the coding-agent's tool layer and the utility code underneath it. It includes:
- The built-in tools in core/tools: read, write, edit, ls, find, grep, bash and powershell, plus their TUI renderers.
- Shared tool infrastructure: truncation, output accumulation, path resolution, the per-file mutation queue, and the adapters between ToolDefinition and AgentTool.
- User-shell execution (core/bash-executor.ts, core/exec.ts) and stdout protection (core/output-guard.ts).
- HTML session export (core/export-html), including its browser template and the vendored marked 18.0.5 and highlight.js 11.9.0.
- config.ts: app identity, the ~/.pi/agent layout, asset directories, and install-method/self-update detection.
- utils/: paths, child processes, shell discovery, ANSI stripping, frontmatter, images, clipboard, terminal syntax highlighting, the fd/rg downloader, version check, git URL parsing, changelog parsing, zip writing, and the Windows self-update quarantine.

Layering, bottom-up. Mirror this as Rust modules and Go packages.
1. Foundation: config.ts and the small utils (paths, child-process, text, ansi, abort/sleep, frontmatter, wsl, fs-watch, open-browser). Nothing here depends on tools.
2. Tool primitives:
   - shell.ts: shell discovery, PATH injection of ~/.pi/agent/bin, control-character sanitizing, process-tree kill.
   - truncate.ts, output-accumulator.ts, path-utils.ts, file-mutation-queue.ts, exec.ts, output-guard.ts.
   - tool-definition-wrapper.ts.
3. Leaf services:
   - images and clipboard: MIME sniffing, EXIF orientation, resize/convert, clipboard backends.
   - network and release utils: fetchWithRetry, the fd/rg installer, version check, git URL parsing, changelog, zip, Windows self-update.
4. Tools. Each create*ToolDefinition(cwd, {operations}) returns a ToolDefinition with name, label, description, promptSnippet, promptGuidelines, parameters (TypeBox JSON schema), outputSchema (bash), constrainedSampling, prepareArguments, execute, and renderCall/renderResult. The Read/Write/Edit/Ls/Find/Grep/Bash operations interfaces can be swapped for remote backends such as SSH. index.ts holds the ToolName set and the factories (coding set: read, bash, edit, write; read-only set: read, grep, find, ls).
5. Renderers and syntax highlighting. These are interactive presentation code and depend on theme.ts, pi-tui components, keybinding hints and the diff component.
6. export-html. Depends on session-manager, theme, and the renderers of ToolDefinitions.

Key flows:
- **Tool call.** The agent calls AgentTool.execute, which wrapToolDefinition forwards to ToolDefinition.execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx).
  - Paths resolve through resolveToCwd: Unicode spaces become plain spaces, a leading '@' is stripped, '~' and file:// URLs are expanded, and MSYS drive paths are converted.
  - Mutating tools (edit, write) are serialized per realpath by withFileMutationQueue. They check abort after each await but hold the lock until in-flight I/O settles.
- **bash.**
  - getShellConfig picks the shell. The command runs in a detached process group with an env built by getShellEnv plus the PI_* session variables.
  - Output chunks are sanitized (stripAnsi, control characters, CR) into an OutputAccumulator. It keeps a rolling tail and spills to a temp file named pi-bash-<hex>.log once output passes 50KB or 2000 lines.
  - onUpdate snapshots are throttled to 100ms. waitForChildProcess resolves on exit plus a 100ms idle grace that restarts on every chunk (#5303).
  - The result text is tail-truncated and carries notices. A non-zero exit, timeout or abort throws an Error whose message includes the output. structuredContent uses snake_case for codemode.
  - bash-executor.ts runs the same pipeline for user '!' commands. Its BashResult is persisted inside session entries.
- **edit.**
  - prepareArguments normalizes legacy input shapes.
  - The file is read, its BOM split off, and line endings normalized to LF.
  - Matching tries an exact match first, then a fuzzy match (NFKC, trailing whitespace, smart quotes, dashes, Unicode spaces).
  - Edits are checked for uniqueness and overlap, then applied while keeping untouched lines as they were. Line endings and the BOM are restored and the file is written.
  - Details are the numbered display diff, the jsdiff unified patch and firstChangedLine, all stored in session JSONL.
- **read.**
  - Missing paths are retried with macOS filename variants: U+202F before AM/PM, NFD, and U+2019 for straight quotes.
  - Images are detected by magic bytes and resized (2000px, 4.5MB base64, a JPEG quality ladder) with a coordinate-scale hint.
  - Text is read with a 1-based offset and limit, then head-truncated with exact notices.
- **find/grep/ls.**
  - fd and rg are spawned directly. They are downloaded to ~/.pi/agent/bin on demand unless PI_OFFLINE is set.
  - fd adds --full-path and a '**/' prefix for patterns containing '/'. grep parses rg --json and kills rg once the match limit is reached.
  - ls sorts with localeCompare and caps output at 500 entries or 50KB.
- **export.**
  - SessionData {header, entries, leafId, systemPrompt, tools, renderedTools} is turned into JSON, base64-encoded, and substituted into template.html. The themed CSS variables, template.js and the vendored libraries go in the same way.
  - Custom (non-template) tools are pre-rendered through their TUI renderers, then converted from ANSI to HTML.

Port strategy:
- **Break the import cycles.**
  - extensions/types.ts imports tool types (BashOperations, EditToolDetails, BashResult, ExecOptions), and the tools import ToolDefinition from it. tools/renderers and tools also reference each other.
  - Declare ToolDefinition, ToolRenderContext, a minimal ExtensionToolContext, and the tool Details/Operations types in a leaf module (Rust) or package (Go). Extensions re-export them.
  - In Go, keep the tools and their renderers in one package, or put the Details types in a leaf package.
- **Keep byte-for-byte output.**
  - Hand-port jsdiff's diffLines, createTwoFilesPatch and applyPatch. The diff and patch strings are persisted and asserted in tests.
  - Build the TypeBox schemas as ordered JSON. They are sent to providers and embedded in exports.
  - Keep every model- or user-visible string verbatim.
  - Write JS-compatible helpers for Number.toFixed (ties round up), Number toString, String.trim (which also strips U+FEFF), UTF-16 length/slice (truncateLine), and ICU localeCompare.
- **Replace JS-runtime pieces natively.**
  - photon WASM becomes the Rust image crate / Go image + x/image.
  - worker_threads become threads/goroutines.
  - hljs becomes syntect (Rust) / chroma (Go), with token scopes mapped to hljs scope names so renderHighlightedHtml and the theme mappings keep working.
  - The pi-tui native clipboard addon becomes arboard (Rust) / golang.design/x/clipboard (Go).
  - Bun/Node runtime and asset detection becomes embedded assets plus a PI_PACKAGE_DIR override.
  - process.stdout monkey-patching becomes a global stdout sink.
  - The quickjs wasm path becomes embedded wasm bytes.
- **Tests.** Port tools.test.ts, the util tests and the tool regression suites as unit tests. Use dependency injection for spawn, fetch, clipboard, platform and env in place of vi.mock and the process.platform overrides.

Lowest layer; must not import tools or extensions.

config.ts, identity:
- Reads package.json (name, version, piConfig.name/configDir) at module load. Turn these into compile-time constants generated from packages/coding-agent/package.json (Rust build.rs; Go go:embed or -ldflags -X). Still honor piConfig from PI_PACKAGE_DIR/package.json for rebranded builds.
- APP_NAME is 'pi'. APP_TITLE is 'π' unless piConfig.name is set. CONFIG_DIR_NAME is '.pi'.
- Env var names derive from APP_NAME.toUpperCase(): PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR.
- getAgentDir: the env override goes through normalizePath; otherwise join(homedir, '.pi', 'agent').
- These names must match exactly: models.json, auth.json, settings.json, themes, tools, bin, prompts, sessions, and `${APP_NAME}-debug.log`.
- getShareViewerUrl = (PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL || 'https://pi.dev/session/') + '#' + gistId. An empty env value counts as unset.

config.ts, runtime and asset detection:
- isBunBinary (import.meta.url contains $bunfs, ~BUN or %7EBUN), isBunRuntime, isBundledNode, the src-vs-dist probing in getThemesDir/getExportTemplateDir/getInteractiveAssetsDir, and getPackageDir have no meaning in a native binary.
- Embed the assets (Rust include_dir!/rust-embed; Go embed.FS) and keep PI_PACKAGE_DIR as an on-disk override.
- getReadmePath, getDocsPath, getExamplesPath and getChangelogPath are shown to the model and read with tools, so they must exist on disk. Extract them to a versioned directory or ship them next to the binary; coordinate with the system-prompt area.
- findNodePackageDir stays a pure upward fs walk: skip a dist/package.json when the parent also has one. Tested.
- getQuickJSWasmPath and setEmbeddedQuickJSWasmPath become embedded wasm bytes. resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier and getCodemodeWorkerSpecifier are removed.

config.ts, install method and self-update:
- config.test.ts fakes process.execPath and PI_PACKAGE_DIR and puts fake pnpm/yarn/bun scripts (.cmd on win32) on PATH. Port detectInstallMethod, getSelfUpdateCommand, getSelfUpdateUnavailableInstruction and getUpdateInstruction as functions that take execPath, packageDir and env.
- They shell out to `pnpm root -g`, `yarn global dir` and `bun pm bin -g`.
- The writability check uses access(W_OK): Rust rustix::fs::access, Go unix.Access.
- Display quoting wraps any arg matching /\s/ in double quotes. A renamed package gets an uninstall step joined with ' && '.
- A standalone native binary should take the 'bun-binary' branch (download instruction).

child-process.ts:
- spawnProcess and spawnProcessSync use cross-spawn on win32 only: PATHEXT lookup, and .cmd/.bat run through cmd.exe with metacharacter escaping.
- Rust: which + Command. Since 1.77 std refuses unsafe batch args, so escape explicitly or call cmd /d /s /c.
- Go: exec.LookPath plus explicit cmd /d /s /c for shims.
- waitForChildProcess (#5303):
  - Resolves on close, or after exit once both pipes reach EOF, or after a 100ms idle grace restarted on every chunk that arrives after exit.
  - Returns null for a signal exit. A spawn 'error' rejects. Streams are destroyed when it resolves.
  - Rust: pipe-reader tasks send chunk events over a channel; use select! with a resettable sleep.
  - Go: do not rely on cmd.Wait. It blocks until the pipe copiers finish when a grandchild holds the pipe. Use your own readers with time.Timer.Reset, or Cmd.WaitDelay.

paths.ts:
- normalizePath order:
  1. optional trim
  2. Unicode spaces [U+00A0, U+2000-200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000] become a space
  3. strip a leading '@'
  4. on win32, /c/x, /mnt/c/x and /cygdrive/c/x become C:\x
  5. tilde: only '~', '~/', and '~\' on win32
  6. file:// through fileURLToPath, which throws on invalid URLs. Rust url::Url::to_file_path; Go needs a hand port.
- resolvePath must match Node path.resolve: lexical . and .. handling, no trailing slash, no symlink resolution. Rust needs a hand-written lexical normalizer (std::path::absolute keeps '..'). Go filepath.Abs+Clean matches on Unix.
- getCwdRelativePath follows path.relative semantics (Rust pathdiff; Go filepath.Rel).
- getFileRevision formats dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs. It is only compared in memory (auth-storage, models-store), so any stable fingerprint works.
- markPathIgnoredByCloudSync spawns xattr (darwin) or setfattr (linux).

ansi.ts:
- The pattern comes from ansi-regex. OSC uses a lazy [\s\S]*? up to BEL, ESC-backslash or U+009C; CSI accepts ESC or U+009B. Rust regex and RE2 both support lazy quantifiers.
- Rust \d is Unicode: use [0-9].
- Keep the fast path that skips when there is no ESC or U+009B.

json.ts:
- stripJsonComments uses alternation regexes with replacement callbacks. Rust: Regex::replace_all with a closure. Go: a FindAllStringSubmatchIndex loop, because ReplaceAllStringFunc gives no access to groups.

frontmatter.ts:
- Converts CRLF and CR to LF and strips the BOM.
- The YAML is the block between a leading '---' and the first '\n---'. The body is everything 4 characters after that, then JS-trimmed. JS trim also strips U+FEFF; Rust str::trim and Go strings.TrimSpace do not, so write a JS-compatible trim.
- A null YAML document becomes {}. Parse YAML 1.2 so 'yes'/'no' stay strings.

Small helpers:
- getPiUserAgent returns `pi/${version} (${platform}; ${runtime}; ${arch})` using Node names (darwin/linux/win32, x64/arm64). Map the Rust/Go OS and arch names to these, and choose a runtime token such as rust/<ver> or go/<ver>. Check pi-user-agent.test.ts.
- sleep rejects with Error('Aborted').
- raceWithAbortSignal rejects with signal.reason or an AbortError 'The operation was aborted'. Model it with CancellationToken (Rust) or context.Context (Go) and typed errors.
- isWSL: WSL_DISTRO_NAME or WSLENV, or /proc/version matching /microsoft|wsl/i.
- fs-watch: errors must reach onError and never crash. Rust notify; Go fsnotify. FS_WATCH_RETRY_DELAY_MS is 5000.
- openBrowser never uses a shell: open, `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, or xdg-open, detached, with errors ignored.
- deprecation.ts has no importers; ask before dropping it.

units.title: Shell resolution, truncation, output accumulator, path utils, mutation queue, exec, output guard, ToolDefinition wrapper
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/resolve-config-value.test.ts -- belongs to the config-value/settings area (it only spies on utils/shell)
packages/coding-agent/test/rpc-prompt-response-semantics.test.ts -- belongs to the RPC area (it vi.mocks output-guard)
packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-extension.test.ts -- belongs to the MCP area. It is the only test of truncateMiddle, so add native truncateMiddle unit tests here
units.notes:
truncate.ts:
- Byte counts are UTF-8 (Buffer.byteLength): str.len() in Rust, len() in Go. Lines are split on '\n', and a trailing newline drops the last empty element.
- TruncationResult fields are stored in session JSONL details. Keep the camelCase names: truncated, truncatedBy ('lines', 'bytes' or null), totalLines, totalBytes, outputLines, outputBytes, lastLinePartial, firstLineExceedsLimit, maxLines, maxBytes. truncatedBy must serialize as null, not be omitted.
- truncateTail can take the end of an oversized last line, starting at a UTF-8 boundary.
- truncateLine counts UTF-16 code units (line.length, slice). Count with encode_utf16 (Rust) or the unicode/utf16 package (Go). If the cut splits a surrogate pair, JS keeps a lone surrogate that Rust/Go strings cannot hold: cut before the pair and document the divergence. The suffix is '... [truncated]'.
- truncateMiddle cuts at UTF-8 boundaries and counts removed characters in code points (Array.from). The marker is '…N chars truncated…' with U+2026.
- formatSize uses toFixed(1), which rounds exact ties up: 1280 B gives '1.3KB'. Rust {:.1} and Go strconv 'f',1 round ties to even and give '1.2KB'. Write a JS-compatible toFixed and test 1280 and 3328 bytes.

output-accumulator.ts:
- Uses a streaming TextDecoder: stateful UTF-8 that emits U+FFFD for invalid bytes and keeps split sequences across chunks. Rust: encoding_rs::Decoder or Utf8Error::error_len handling. Go: buffer bytes until utf8.FullRune.
- Keeps a rolling tail of 2x maxBytes.
- The temp file is `${prefix}-${randomBytes(8).hex}.log` in os.tmpdir(), created lazily once a limit is exceeded, with earlier chunks written first. Rust std::env::temp_dir and Go os.TempDir both honor TMPDIR.
- readFullOutput returns head and tail halves joined by '\n\n[... N bytes omitted ...]\n\n', cut at UTF-8 boundaries.
- Node write streams are async but ordered: use a buffered writer and flush it before exposing the path.

exec.ts:
- Spawns without a shell. On abort or timeout it sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5s; proc.killed only means a signal was sent.
- stdout/stderr are decoded per chunk with Buffer.toString, so multibyte characters can split. Decoding the joined buffer once is fine.
- code ?? 0: a signal-killed process reports 0 with killed=true. A spawn error resolves with code 1.
- Uses waitForChildProcess.

output-guard.ts:
- Monkey-patching process.stdout.write has no native equivalent. Add a process-wide output sink: Rust static Mutex<Box<dyn Write>>; Go a mutex-guarded io.Writer variable.
- takeOverStdout sends ordinary stdout writes to stderr. writeRawStdout keeps the real stdout for JSON/RPC protocol bytes.
- Raw writes are serialized. ENOBUFS, EAGAIN and EWOULDBLOCK retry every 10ms (Rust ErrorKind::WouldBlock; Go syscall.EAGAIN). Any other error exits with code 1.
- flushRawStdout waits for the queue to drain.
- Audit dependencies that print to stdout directly.

shell.ts:
- getShellConfig order:
  1. custom path; must exist, else 'Custom shell path not found: X'
  2. win32: %ProgramFiles% and %ProgramFiles(x86)% Git\bin\bash.exe, then `where bash.exe` (first existing line), then the multi-line 'No bash shell found' error, verbatim
  3. Unix: /bin/bash, then `which bash`, then sh
- Legacy WSL bash (C:\Windows\System32 or Sysnative\bash.exe, case-insensitive) gets args ['-s'] and stdin transport.
- getPowerShellConfig: win32 only. Prefers pwsh.exe over powershell.exe, with args -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command.
- getShellEnv prepends ~/.pi/agent/bin using whatever case the PATH key has (Windows env is case-insensitive).
- sanitizeBinaryOutput removes [\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F\uFFF9-\uFFFB].
- killProcessTree on Unix: kill(-pid, SIGKILL), falling back to kill(pid). This needs the child spawned in its own group: Rust CommandExt::process_group(0); Go SysProcAttr Setpgid.
- killProcessTree on win32: spawn %SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe /F /T /PID, ignoring spawn errors (#6596; port the test with an injectable spawner).
- Tracked detached PIDs are killed on shutdown signals; the main area owns the signal handlers.

path-utils.ts:
- resolveReadPath tries, in order: the exact path; ' AM.'/' PM.' with U+202F (case-insensitive); NFD; U+2019 for straight quotes; then NFD with the curly quote. Rust: unicode-normalization. Go: x/text/unicode/norm.

file-mutation-queue.ts:
- Keyed by realpath. Falls back to path.resolve on ENOENT or ENOTDIR and rethrows other errors. Symlink aliases share one queue.
- Registration is itself serialized, which keeps the order FIFO.
- Rust: a global map of Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>> (FIFO-fair), removing the entry after the last release. Go: a per-key FIFO built from chained channels, because sync.Mutex is not FIFO.
- The lock stays held until fn settles.

tool-definition-wrapper.ts:
- Provides wrapToolDefinition(s) and createToolDefinitionFromAgentTool, with lazy ctxFactory.
- Define the ToolDefinition trait/interface in a leaf module that does not import extensions. Go forbids the extensions/types.ts <-> tools import cycle.

units.title: Image sniffing, EXIF, resize/convert pipeline and clipboard backends
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard-image-native-errors.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive-mode area (drives InteractiveMode)
packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard-paste-file-paths.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive-mode area (drives InteractiveMode)
units.notes:
mime.ts:
- Sniffs magic bytes from the start of the buffer or file: JPEG FF D8 FF, the PNG signature, GIF87a/89a, RIFF....WEBP, and BMP 'BM'.
- APNG (an acTL chunk) is not a supported PNG. Keep the rules exact.

photon.ts:
- Lazily loads photon-node WASM and patches fs.readFileSync for Bun binaries. Drop it entirely and use native codecs.
- Rust: the image crate with png, jpeg, gif, webp and bmp, and imageops Lanczos3 or fast_image_resize. photon-rs gives identical algorithms.
- Go: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, x/image/webp, x/image/bmp, plus disintegration/imaging Lanczos.

exif-orientation.ts:
- Hand-parses JPEG APP1 Exif and WebP EXIF chunks: TIFF byte order, IFD0 tag 0x0112. Orientations 2-8 map to flips and rotations.
- Port the byte parser directly and keep the silent fallback on malformed data.

image-resize-core.ts:
- Defaults: maxWidth and maxHeight 2000, maxBytes 4.5MB measured as base64 length (4*ceil(n/3)), jpegQuality 80.
- Tries the original first. Then, at each size, tries PNG and JPEG with deduplicated quality steps [q, 85, 70, 55, 40], then scales by 0.75 and repeats. Returns a failure when nothing fits.
- Encoded bytes will differ from photon. Tests should assert dimensions, MIME type and limits, not bytes.

image-resize.ts and image-resize-worker.ts:
- Resizing runs in a worker_threads Worker with an in-process fallback. Replace both with spawn_blocking (Rust) or a goroutine (Go).
- formatDimensionNote produces '[Image: original WxH, displayed at wxh. Multiply coordinates by S to map to original image.]'. S uses toFixed(2), with the same tie-rounding hazard as formatSize.

image-process.ts and tool-result-images.ts:
- image-process converts GIF, WebP and BMP to PNG (image-convert), then resizes with the model's ModelImageResizeOptions.
- tool-result-images rewrites ImageContent blocks and appends a text block of hints joined with '\n'.

clipboard-command.ts:
- An async spawn with a timeout and buffered stdout. Rust: tokio::process with timeout. Go: exec.CommandContext.

clipboard.ts:
- copyToClipboard writes directly first (the native addon, then platform commands), then OSC 52.
- Platform commands, kept in source order: pbcopy (darwin); Windows clipboard through PowerShell reading a temp file, with wslpath -w under WSL; termux-clipboard-set when TERMUX_VERSION is set; wl-copy when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set; xclip -selection clipboard; xsel --clipboard --input.
- OSC 52 is ESC]52;c;<base64>BEL, skipped when the encoded text exceeds 100000 characters. It is preferred under WT_SESSION and emitted for remote or headless sessions.
- The error messages ('Clipboard unavailable: ...') are verbatim.
- The OSC 52 write goes to process.stdout and must go through the output-guard sink.
- readClipboardText uses termux-clipboard-get, `wl-paste --no-newline --type text`, xclip -out or xsel --output. readClipboardFilePaths reads file paths from the clipboard.

clipboard-image.ts:
- Tries the native addon first.
- Wayland: `wl-paste --list-types`, pick a supported image type, then `wl-paste --type T --no-newline`.
- X11: `xclip -selection clipboard -t TARGETS -o`, then the preferred type.
- WSL: a powershell.exe script saves the image to a temp PNG, located through wslpath.
- BMP is converted to PNG.
- isWaylandSession checks env. extensionForImageMimeType maps MIME types to file extensions.

Testing and native clipboard:
- The tests vi.mock child_process, the pi-tui native clipboard, process.platform and env. Define a ClipboardBackend trait/interface (command runner, native clipboard, platform, env, temp fs) and inject it.
- Native clipboard: Rust arboard (with wayland-data-control). Go golang.design/x/clipboard (cgo); without it, use the command fallbacks only.

units.title: fetchWithRetry, fd/rg tools-manager, version check, git URL parsing, changelog, zip writer, Windows self-update
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/bug-report.test.ts -- belongs to the bug-report area, which uses zip.ts indirectly
units.notes:
management-http.ts, fetchWithRetry:
- maxRetries defaults to 2 (non-finite also means 2).
- Retries on status 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 (unless retryOnStatus=false), cancelling the discarded body. Also retries transport errors.
- Caller abort and the overall timeoutMs are terminal. attemptTimeoutMs aborts only the current attempt.
- An AbortError is not retried unless an attempt timeout caused it.
- Rust: reqwest with a per-request timeout plus a tokio::time::timeout for the overall budget, and a CancellationToken.
- Go: net/http with nested context.WithTimeout.
- Inject an HTTP client trait/interface; the tests stub the global fetch. Should honor the same proxy env as the http-dispatcher area.

tools-manager.ts:
- TOOLS_DIR = getBinDir() is evaluated at module load. Compute it lazily but read the env the same way.
- getToolPath checks ~/.pi/agent/bin/<bin>(.exe) first. Otherwise it probes `<name> --version` on PATH (fd also tries fdfind) and returns the bare command name.
- getLatestVersion requests https://github.com/<repo>/releases/latest with redirect 'manual' and parses the tag from Location: resolve relative Locations, discard the body, and keep the error messages verbatim. Rust: reqwest redirect::Policy::none(). Go: CheckRedirect returning http.ErrUseLastResponse.
- Asset names use darwin/linux/win32 and x86_64/aarch64 (musl on Linux, msvc zip on Windows). fd is pinned to 10.3.0 on darwin x64. Timeouts: 10s network, 120s download.
- Extraction uses tar or unzip, and on Windows System32 tar.exe then PowerShell Expand-Archive. Native extraction is equivalent and removes the external tools: Rust flate2+tar / zip; Go archive/tar, compress/gzip, archive/zip. Then chmod 755 and rename into the bin dir.
- PI_OFFLINE ('1', 'true' or 'yes', case-insensitive) disables downloads. Android prints a Termux `pkg install` hint. Status goes through a callback, never the console. The error cause chain is surfaced (tested).

version-check.ts:
- Fetches https://pi.dev/api/latest-version with the pi user agent.
- PI_OFFLINE and PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK short-circuit.
- Uses semver valid() and compare(). If either version is invalid, any trimmed difference counts as newer.
- formatVersionCheckError appends error codes collected from error.cause and AggregateError, or the cause message. Native errors need an equivalent cause chain; adapt test expectations to native error codes.

git.ts, parseGitUrl:
- Built on hosted-git-info.fromUrl plus custom handling: git+ssh://, scp-like git@host:path, https URLs, an optional #ref or @ref, and github: shortcuts.
- The GitSource objects are persisted in settings.json package sources, so their shape must be identical. Hand-port the needed hosted-git-info patterns; git-ssh-url.test.ts is the spec.

changelog.ts:
- Parses '## [x.y.z]' sections. compareVersions is numeric. getNewEntries filters by lastVersion. getChangelogPath is re-exported from config.
- normalizeChangelogLinks rewrites inline markdown links:
  - LEGACY_REPO_RE has a lookahead (?=\/|$), which Rust regex and Go RE2 lack. Capture the boundary group and re-emit it, or check it by hand.
  - It also uses path.posix.normalize and encodeURI (no stdlib equivalent; hand-port the JS reserved set).
  - Links are rewritten to blob/tree at tag v<version>.

zip.ts:
- A minimal ZIP writer: local headers, central directory and EOCD, with deflateRawSync and crc32.
- DOS date and time come from local time. Rust: flate2 DeflateEncoder, crc32fast, and chrono::Local (the time crate's local offset is unreliable on multithreaded Unix). Go: compress/flate, hash/crc32, time.Local.
- Compressed bytes may differ.

windows-self-update.ts:
- Before an npm self-update on win32, renames loaded .node addons (from process.report.getReport().sharedObjects under the install dir) aside so npm can replace locked files.
- A native binary loads no .node addons. Replace this with renaming the running .exe for standalone self-update, or make it a no-op.

units.title: edit-diff engine and the edit, write, read, ls tools
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/image-resize-callers.test.ts#L46-55 -- covers processFileArguments in the CLI file-processor area
packages/coding-agent/test/image-resize-callers.test.ts#L86-95 -- covers deferred attachment resizing in the CLI/agent-session area
units.notes:
edit-diff.ts, text handling:
- Detects CRLF vs LF from the first line ending, normalizes to LF, and restores the original endings afterward. The BOM is split with splitBom and put back.
- normalizeForFuzzyMatch applies NFKC, strips trailing whitespace per line, and folds smart single/double quotes, Unicode dashes and Unicode spaces to ASCII.
- JS uses UTF-16 indices. Use byte offsets on the normalized string consistently. NFKC changes lengths, which is why applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines maps by line: only lines touched by a replacement take normalized text; all other lines keep their original bytes.
- Validation errors (empty oldText, not found, multiple occurrences, overlap, no change) are seen by the model and asserted in tests: copy them verbatim.

edit-diff.ts, diff and patch:
- generateDiffString runs jsdiff diffLines. Lines are prefixed '+', '-' or ' ' with padded line numbers. Context is 4 lines, with '...' marking gaps. It also returns firstChangedLine.
- The patch is createTwoFilesPatch(path, path, old, new, ..., {context: 4}) with the Index/=== header removed.
- Both strings are stored in EditToolDetails (session JSONL) and tests apply the patch with applyPatch.
- Hand-port jsdiff 8.0.4: the base Myers diff with the line tokenizer, which keeps newlines in tokens; structuredPatch hunk assembly; formatPatch including '\ No newline at end of file'; and applyPatch.
- Rust similar and Go difflib choose different hunks on ambiguous diffs.
- computeEditsDiff is also called by renderers/edit.ts for previews.

edit.ts:
- Schema {path, edits: [{oldText, newText}]}, constrainedSampling strict 'prefer', renderShell 'self'.
- prepareArguments accepts edits as a JSON string, as a single object, or as legacy top-level oldText/newText. Keep the precedence.
- Errors: 'Edit tool input is invalid. edits must contain at least one replacement.' and `Could not edit file: ${path}. ${msg}.`. Success text: `Successfully replaced ${n} block(s) in ${path}.`.
- Reads decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement (Rust from_utf8_lossy; Go strings.ToValidUTF8).
- After each await, check abort and throw 'Operation aborted', but keep the queue lock until the in-flight I/O settles. The deferred-promise tests rely on this.

write.ts:
- mkdir -p, then write UTF-8. Success text is `Successfully wrote to ${path}` using the user-supplied path.

read.ts:
- Resolves with resolveReadPathAsync. Images are detected by magic bytes and run through processImage with the model's resize options; when resizing is unsafe the result is text-only.
- Text is split on '\n'. offset is 1-based. Then truncateHead.
- Notices are verbatim: '[Showing lines a-b of N. Use offset=M to continue.]', the '(50.0KB limit)' variant, '[K more lines in file. Use offset=M to continue.]', and '[Line N is X, exceeds 50.0KB limit. Use bash: sed -n 'Np' path | head -c 51200]'.
- Offset errors are verbatim: `Offset ${offset} is beyond end of file (${n} lines total)`.

ls.ts:
- Sorts with a.toLowerCase().localeCompare(b.toLowerCase()), which is ICU root collation: Rust feruca or icu_collator; Go golang.org/x/text/collate (language.Und). A plain codepoint sort differs for accented names and punctuation.
- Directories get a '/' suffix via stat, which follows symlinks; stat failures skip the entry. Dotfiles are included.
- Default limit 500. Notices: `${limit} entries limit reached. Use limit=${2*limit} for more` and '50.0KB limit reached'. An empty directory gives '(empty directory)'.
- Errors: `Path not found`, `Not a directory`, and `Cannot read directory: ${e.message}`. The last embeds Node's errno text, which native code cannot reproduce; map errno to Node-style messages or relax the tests.

Operations interfaces:
- ReadOperations, EditOperations, WriteOperations and LsOperations become async traits/interfaces for remote backends.
- Details structs (EditToolDetails, ReadToolDetails, LsToolDetails) go in the leaf tool-types module, so renderers and extensions can import them without cycles.

units.title: bash and powershell tools, bash-executor, find and grep tools, tools index
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-bash-persistence.test.ts -- belongs to the agent-session area (exercises bash-executor through AgentSession)
packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/9068-user-bash-fail-closed.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive/RPC area
packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/8611-thinking-toggle-pending-bash-output.test.ts -- belongs to the interactive components area
units.notes:
bash.ts, schema and timeouts:
- Schema {command, timeout?: number in seconds}.
- The description embeds DEFAULT_MAX_LINES and '50KB'.
- outputSchema {output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds} uses snake_case and is consumed by codemode. Serialize wall_time_seconds exactly as JS would: serde_json prints 2.0 where JS prints 2.
- A non-finite or non-positive timeout fails with 'Invalid timeout: must be a finite number of seconds'. Above 2147483647 ms it fails with 'Invalid timeout: maximum is 2147483.647 seconds'.
- The JS Number-to-string formatting of the seconds also appears in 'Command timed out after N seconds'.

bash.ts, local operations:
- Checks the cwd first: `Working directory does not exist: ${cwd}\nCannot execute ${shellName} commands.`.
- Spawns shell, args and command; legacy WSL bash gets the command on stdin and ignores stdin errors.
- Non-win32 children are detached into their own process group, and the PID is tracked for shutdown.
- stdout and stderr are delivered in arrival order through one onData.
- Abort or timeout kills the process tree and rejects with 'aborted' or `timeout:${secs}`.
- Exit code = code ?? (signal ? 128 + signo : 1). Rust ExitStatusExt::signal; Go WaitStatus.Signal(). Use the libc signal numbers, which match Node's os.constants.signals.

bash.ts, environment:
- Removes PI_SESSION_ID, PI_SESSION_FILE, PI_PROVIDER, PI_MODEL and PI_REASONING_LEVEL from the env, then sets them from ctx when exposeSessionEnvironment is true (the default). promptGuidelines are only included when it is on.
- spawnHook may rewrite {command, cwd, env}. commandPrefix is prepended with '\n'.

bash.ts, execute:
- Output goes into an OutputAccumulator. onUpdate is called once with empty content, then throttled to BASH_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS (100, from renderers/bash.ts): leading edge plus a trailing timer.
- Output arriving after completion is dropped (#5208).
- Errors are thrown as appendStatus(output, 'Command aborted' / 'Command timed out after N seconds' / 'Command exited with code N' / 'Command terminated without an exit code'), so the model sees the output.
- structuredContent.output is capped at 1 MiB with truncateMiddle.
- Windows: there are no process groups, so use taskkill /T. bash-close-hang-windows covers daemonized descendants (cfg(windows) only).

powershell.ts:
- Reuses createShellToolDefinition with getPowerShellConfig, which only exists on win32.

find.ts:
- Default limit 1000. A custom FindOperations.glob path gets ignore ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**'].
- Otherwise it calls ensureTool('fd'). Failure: 'fd is not available and could not be downloaded'.
- fd args: --glob --color=never --hidden.
- Adds --no-require-git unless a .git exists in any ancestor (#5960), then --max-results.
- A pattern containing '/' adds --full-path and gets a '**/' prefix unless it starts with '/' or '**/' or is '**'. On win32, '/' becomes [/\\].
- The command ends with '--', pattern, searchPath. fd's exact glob and .gitignore semantics are what you want (#3302, #3303), so always spawn fd; do not reimplement globbing.
- relativizeFindResultPath handles root and drive-root search paths (#6104).
- Messages: 'No files found matching pattern'; `${limit} results limit reached. Use limit=${2*limit} for more, or refine pattern`; `Failed to run fd: ${err.message}`.

grep.ts:
- Default limit 100 (minimum 1). Calls ensureTool('rg').
- Runs `rg --json --line-number --color=never --hidden` with optional --ignore-case, --fixed-strings and --glob.
- Parses JSON-lines 'match' events. path.text can instead be base64 path.bytes for non-UTF-8 names.
- Kills rg once the limit is reached (matchLimitReached).
- Context lines are read from the file itself.
- Output lines are 'path:N: text' for matches and 'path-N- text' for context. truncateLine applies at 500 UTF-16 units (linesTruncated), then truncateHead.
- rg exit 1 means 'No matches found'.
- Messages: `${limit} matches limit reached. Use limit=${2*limit} for more, or refine pattern`; 'ripgrep (rg) is not available and could not be downloaded'.

bash-executor.ts (user '!' commands):
- Streaming decode, then stripAnsi, sanitizeBinaryOutput, and removal of '\r'.
- The rolling buffer is measured in UTF-16 text.length (2x50KB), while totalBytes counts raw bytes. The temp file pi-bash-<hex>.log opens once raw bytes exceed 50KB or the final output is truncated.
- cancelled means exitCode is undefined.
- BashResult {output, exitCode, cancelled, truncated, fullOutputPath} is persisted in bashExecution session entries. Keep the field names and omit undefined fields; Go omitempty would also drop exitCode 0, so use pointers.

Renderers and the import graph:
- Renderers are spread into ToolDefinitions (...writeRenderers). withBuiltInRenderers (renderers/index.ts) adds them to definitions created without renderers.
- They import theme.ts, keybinding-hints.ts, visual-truncate.ts and diff.ts. None of those import core/tools, so this dependency direction is legal in Go: tools -> renderers -> theme/components.
- Renderers also import the tools' Details types and ToolName, while the tools import their renderers. Put renderers in the same Go package as the tools, or move the Details types to a leaf package. Rust modules within one crate can be mutually dependent.

Renderer state and display:
- BASH_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS (100) is exported here and used by bash.ts.
- BashRenderState keeps an elapsed-time interval timer; EditRenderState holds a precomputed diff preview from computeEditsDiff. Drive both from the TUI's invalidate/tick mechanism rather than raw OS timers.
- render-utils:
  - shortenPath replaces a $HOME prefix with '~'. It uses startsWith without a separator check, so preserve that.
  - linkPath emits an OSC 8 hyperlink with pathToFileURL. Rust url::Url::from_file_path; Go needs a hand-written file URL with WHATWG percent-encoding.
  - replaceTabs turns a tab into 3 spaces. normalizeDisplayText drops '\r'.
  - getTextOutput applies stripAnsi + sanitizeBinaryOutput and shows images through imageFallback when they are disabled or unsupported.
  - invalidArgText and renderToolPath are small display helpers.
- Renderer output is never persisted, but should look the same.

syntax-highlight.ts:
- highlight.js 10.7.3 core with 21 eager languages: bash, c, cpp, csharp, dart, go, groovy, java, javascript, json, kotlin, lua, nix, perl, php, python, ruby, rust, scala, swift, typescript. loadAllHighlightLanguages dynamically imports the rest.
- highlight(code, {language, theme}) passes hljs HTML through renderHighlightedHtml, which walks nested <span class='hljs-X'>.
  - Formatter lookup: the full scope, then prefixes cut at '.' and '-'.
  - Unmapped or unscoped spans inherit the parent formatter.
  - Entities are decoded by html.ts.
- supportsLanguage checks the hljs registry and aliases.
- Native port: syntect + two-face (Rust) or chroma/v2 (Go) produces tokens. Map their scopes or token types to hljs scope names (keyword, built_in, type, literal, number, string, comment, title, title.class, title.function, params, attr, meta, variable, ...) so the theme.ts mappings and the cli-highlight default-scope test keep working.
- Keep renderHighlightedHtml as a pure function; its tests feed literal HTML. Language names and aliases from getLanguageFromPath (theme.ts) must resolve to native grammars.

html.ts:
- decodeHtmlEntityAt handles named amp, lt, gt, quot and apos, plus &#N; and &#xN;. The semicolon must be within 16 characters.
- Number.parseInt is lenient ('&#12ab;' parses as 12). Mirror that.
- String.fromCodePoint on a surrogate code point yields a lone surrogate. Rust char::from_u32 and Go return invalid there: emit U+FFFD.

units.notes:
Size: - src_lines counts the TypeScript plus template.html. template.css (1076), template.js (1918), highlight.min.js (1212, hljs 11.9.0) and marked.min.js (78, marked 18.0.5) are browser code embedded verbatim (Rust include_str!; Go //go:embed). Keep their license headers. - The xss and skill-block tests read template.js as text and port as string assertions on the embedded asset. Entry points and errors: - exportSessionToHtml(sm, agentState?, opts|outputPath) backs AgentSession /export. exportFromFile(inputPath, opts) backs the CLI --export. - Errors, verbatim: 'Cannot export in-memory session to HTML', 'Nothing to export yet - start a conversation first', `File not found: ${resolved}`. - The default output is `${APP_NAME}-session-${basename(file, '.jsonl')}.html`, relative to the process cwd. An explicit outputPath only goes through normalizePath (tilde etc.), not resolve. SessionData and serialization: - SessionData is {header, entries, leafId, systemPrompt?, tools?: [{name, description, parameters}], renderedTools?}, JSON-stringified, UTF-8, then base64-encoded. - Serialize entries from the raw stored JSON so key order and numbers survive: Rust serde_json with preserve_order or RawValue; Go json.RawMessage. Use SetEscapeHTML(false) in Go for parity. Omit undefined fields. - tools[].parameters must keep TypeBox key order. Template substitution: - String.replace with a string pattern replaces the first occurrence only and treats $$, $&, $` and $' in the replacement as special. Today's assets contain none of these sequences, so replacen(..., 1) (Rust) or strings.Replace(..., 1) (Go) is equivalent. Add a test that the embedded assets stay free of them. - Order: 1. In template.css: {{THEME_VARS}} (lines joined with '\n '), {{BODY_BG}}, {{CONTAINER_BG}}, {{INFO_BG}}. 2. In template.html: {{CSS}}, {{JS}}, {{SESSION_DATA}}, {{MARKED_JS}}, {{HIGHLIGHT_JS}}. Theme colors: - Each entry of getResolvedThemeColors becomes `--key: value;`. Then come --exportPageBg, --exportCardBg and --exportInfoBg, taken from getThemeExportColors or derived from userMessageBg (default '#343541'). - parseColor accepts #RRGGBB or rgb(r,g,b). - Luminance uses the 0.03928, 12.92 and 2.4 constants; above 0.5 counts as light. - adjustBrightness factors: light 0.96; dark 0.7 and 0.85. It uses Math.round; Rust f64::round and Go math.Round match for non-negative values. - infoBg offsets: light +10/+5/-20, dark +20/+15/+0. - Fallbacks: rgb(24, 24, 30), rgb(30, 30, 36) and rgb(60, 55, 40), with exact spacing. Custom tool pre-rendering: - TEMPLATE_RENDERED_TOOLS (bash, read, write, edit, ls) are drawn by template.js. Every other tool call or result goes through tool-renderer.ts. - It calls the ToolDefinition's renderCall and renderResult with a ToolRenderContext (collapsed and expanded), renders the pi-tui Component at width 100, trims TUI spacer lines, and converts with ansiLinesToHtml. Renderer errors yield undefined. - Only native and built-in extension tools get pre-rendered; user TS extensions are not loaded. ansi-to-html.ts: - SGR codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, 30-37, 90-97, 40-47, 100-107, 38/48;5;n and 38/48;2;r;g;b, 39 and 49. - 256-color cube components are 0 or 55+40n; grayscale is 8+10n; the 16-color table uses fixed hex values. - escapeHtml produces & < > " '. - Each line becomes
...
with no whitespace between lines (whitespace test). Asset location: - Embedded assets, with PI_PACKAGE_DIR/export-html (or src/core/export-html) as an on-disk override for development.
