external_deps.rust_suggestion: include_str!/include_bytes! or rust-embed, while keeping the config.ts-equivalent path helpers for reported paths
external_deps.go_suggestion: embed.FS (//go:embed)

hazards: Exact-tie rounding in JS toFixed(2) is half-up: 0.125 gives '0.13', and interactive-mode-compaction expects '~$0.13'. Rust format!("{:.2}") and Go strconv.FormatFloat give '0.12'. A shared JS-compatible toFixed helper is required.

JS Math.round rounds .5 toward +infinity (-0.5 gives -0). Rust f64::round and Go math.Round round away from zero. The system-theme OKHSL/OKLab math, hex conversion and contrast bisection must use floor(x+0.5) and the same operation order to reproduce colors exactly.
Theme validation error text must reproduce typebox wording and ordering: 'Missing required color tokens:' sorted, then 'Other errors:' with `  - <path or />: <message>`.

Global mutable singletons (current theme, terminal colors and scheme, registered themes, onThemeChange listeners) are read from many threads in Rust. Use ArcSwap/RwLock. In Go use atomic.Pointer and guard the listener list.

The InteractiveMode tests depend on calling class methods with fake `this` objects (Reflect.get(prototype).call). Native ports must design injectable seams (session, runtime host, ui, settings, clipboard, command runner, process control, clock) up front, or most tests cannot be ported.
Go import cycles: components import external-editor, model-search and model-catalog-refresh, while interactive imports components. Place those three (and theme) in packages below components.

Signal and exit semantics:
- SIGTERM/SIGHUP listeners are prepended and stay registered until cleanup completes.
- No SIGHUP or SIGTSTP on Windows.
- Exit codes: 0 for quit and signal; 129 for dead-terminal EIO/EPIPE/ENOTCONN; crashes go to the crash log.
- The shutdown order differs between the signal path and the interactive path (#5080, #5724).
Ctrl+Z suspend must ignore SIGINT while stopped and restore exactly once on SIGCONT. kill(0, SIGTSTP) targets the process group. Restore the terminal (ui.stop/start) around it.

External editor: the command is split on single spaces (no shell parsing) except shell:true on win32. Use async spawn to avoid the Windows console input race. Strip the BOM and exactly one trailing newline.

Locale-dependent formatting: Date/Number toLocaleString in /session and the crash notice, and localeCompare sorting for themes and resources. Choose deterministic en-US output and ICU-like collation, and document the choice.

Built-in theme files are embedded natively but getAvailableThemesWithPaths, getThemeByName and resource listing expose paths. Keep config.ts-equivalent getThemesDir layouts (source checkout, installed package, standalone binary) or define virtual paths consistently.
Environment variables: PI_OFFLINE (blocks uploads and telemetry), TMUX (tmux check), COLORFGBG (theme detection), VISUAL/EDITOR, FORCE_COLOR/NO_COLOR/TERM (chalk level).
The external tools gh and tmux and the tools-manager downloads for fd/rg must be mockable. session-share tests mock child_process; native tests need a CommandRunner fake.

The renderer can be swapped at runtime (regular vs fullscreen). Every stored reference to the TUI must go through a handle that dispatches to the current renderer (#7731). Theme controller and extension UI bindings must be rebound after a swap.

Extension UI factories (widgets, header, footer, custom overlays, custom editor, autocomplete wrappers, terminal input listeners, markdown transformers) become native trait objects. Without user TS extensions, the only producers are the native built-ins (mcp, codemode, llama, tool-search). Keep the trait surface complete so built-ins and future native extensions work.
js_runtime_dependent: Global theme Proxy over globalThis[Symbol.for('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent:theme')] plus the legacy @mariozechner key, used to share one theme across duplicate JS module copies. Natively, a single process-global accessor (Rust ArcSwap/RwLock static, Go atomic.Pointer); the legacy key is dropped.

createInteractiveTuiReference uses a JS Proxy that re-binds captured methods to the current renderer. Natively, a handle type whose methods resolve the current renderer at call time. Monkeypatching tui.render (first #7731 case) has no native equivalent; skip that case.

setCustomEditorComponent copies actionHandlers/onSubmit/onChange by duck typing because extension modules loaded by jiti have distinct class identities. Natively, an EditorComponent trait with optional handler-transfer methods.
instanceof / isViewportTUI / isWorkingStatusEditor / isExpandable runtime type checks. Natively, enum matching or trait downcasts (Rust Any, Go type assertions).

Tests that call InteractiveMode.prototype methods with partial fake `this` objects (Reflect.get(...).call(fakeThis)). Natively, construct a real InteractiveMode over faux runtime/harness fakes, VirtualTerminal and injected seams.

Tests that vi.mock modules (node:child_process in session-share, utils/clipboard in interactive-tui) or spy on process.on/once/kill, setInterval and process.platform (suspend, signals). Natively, dependency-injected CommandRunner, Clipboard, ProcessControl and Platform seams.
The 2791 regression inspects process._getActiveHandles and emits 'error' on a Node FSWatcher. Natively, a unit test asserts that the watcher error path closes the watcher and does not panic.

fixtures/fake-external-editor.mjs is a Node script used as $EDITOR in tests. Natively, a small test helper binary (Rust: a cargo test bin or build-script-compiled helper; Go: a TestMain re-exec or go run helper) or a POSIX sh script with a Windows .cmd equivalent.
setInterval(noop, 2**30) keepalive during SIGTSTP exists only to keep the Node event loop alive. Native ports drop it and block on the SIGCONT handler instead.

reports.summary:
Scope: packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components. It holds 48 TS files (11,658 lines) with every interactive-mode widget, all built on pi-tui.

**Component contract.** Every component implements pi-tui Component:
- render(width) returns string[] of ANSI-styled lines no wider than width.
- invalidate() clears caches.
- handleInput(data) is optional and receives raw terminal byte strings.
- handleMouse(event) is optional.
- Focusable components forward `focused` to their inner Input/Editor so the IME cursor lands in the right place.

Composition uses pi-tui Container, Box, Text, TruncatedText, Spacer, Markdown, MouseRegion, SelectList, SettingsList, Input, Editor, Loader, CancellableLoader and Image.

**Singletons.** Two process-wide singletons drive almost everything:
- the `theme` proxy (modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts): fg/bg/bold/italic/inverse plus the markdown, select-list, editor and settings-list themes;
- the keybindings manager: getKeybindings().matches(data, "tui.select.up" / "app.*").

Native ports should keep both as globals (Rust OnceLock/RwLock, Go package var plus mutex). Components read them at render time, and theme changes call invalidate().

**Layers (unit plan)**

1. **Foundation (A).** No dependencies on other units in this area. It holds:
   - DynamicBorder, keybinding hint formatting (darwin shows alt as "option"), ThemedText, CountdownTimer, visual truncation, markdown-transform chaining and the pi logo.
   - The StatusIndicator family (Working/Retry/Compaction/BranchSummary/Idle), which are loaders that can render inside the editor top border.
   - CustomEditor, an Editor subclass that dispatches app keybindings and embeds the working status in its border.
   - BorderedLoader, renderDiff (intra-line highlights via jsdiff diffWords) and the mermaid markdown transformer (grok-mermaid).

   Core tool renderers, the codemode/llama/mcp extension UIs and the experimental TUIs import A, so A must land before them.
2. **Transcript (B).**
   - AssistantMessage: coalesced thinking runs, click-to-expand per run, stop-reason/error lines, OSC 133 markers only when there are no tool calls.
   - UserMessage: Markdown with user background and OSC 133 A/B/C markers.
   - CustomMessage and CustomEntry: extension renderers with error fallbacks.
   - Collapsible branch, compaction and skill summaries.
   - BashExecution: streaming output, tail truncation at 2000 lines / 50KB, 20-line preview.
   - ToolExecution: a renderer shell with fallback JSON rendering, inline images with kitty PNG conversion, and self-rendering tools.
   - The Earendil announcement image.
3. **Dialogs (C).**
   - Extension UI: selector, input and editor with countdown timeouts; the editor can open an external VISUAL/EDITOR.
   - Radius login menu with a shimmer animation.
   - LoginDialog: OSC 8 auth link, device code, promise-returning prompts, abort on cancel.
   - Auth provider selector, trust selector, first-time setup (theme, then analytics), theme/show-images/thinking selectors, and the fork user-message selector.
4. **Model and settings (D).**
   - ModelSelector: all/scoped scope, fuzzy search, async catalog refresh with a 15s timeout.
   - ScopedModelsSelector: enable, reorder, unsaved state.
   - SettingsSelector with about 40 SettingsList items. Submenus come from settings-submenu: SelectSubmenu with optional search, and SteppedSubmenu for multi-step flows such as per-model thinking overrides and automatic light/dark theme pairs.
   - Footer: cwd/branch/session-name line, token/cost/context stats with a cached aggregation, model and thinking on the right, extension statuses.
5. **Session selector (E1).** The search parser handles `re:` regex, quoted phrases and fuzzy tokens. The picker has current/all scope, async loaders with progress and abort, threaded/recent/relevance sort, a named-only filter, rename, and delete through the `trash` CLI with an unlink fallback.
6. **Tree selector (E2).** The /tree navigator flattens the session entry tree:
   - active branch first, with gutters and connectors;
   - filter modes, search, folding and labels;
   - horizontal scrolling;
   - one-line summaries per tool.
7. **Config selector (F).** `pi config` resource groups (packages, extensions, skills, prompts, themes) across global and project scope. Toggles rewrite settings through SettingsManager setters using +/-/! patterns.
8. **Easter eggs and barrel (G).**
   - Armin: XBM bitmap with 7 random reveal effects.
   - Armin3d: fullscreen alt-screen overlay. It parses the captured screen ANSI into cells, ray-casts a 3D logo into braille, and adds a sliding puzzle and starfield.
   - Daxnuts pixel reveal.
   - The index.ts barrel re-exports every component for src/index.ts. Port it last.

**Key flows**
- **Rendering.** InteractiveMode adds components to its chat container. They cache by width and rebuild on invalidate. Tests assert visible text and, in places, exact ANSI and OSC sequences, so SGR output from theme.fg/bg must match byte-for-byte.
- **Input.** handleInput resolves bindings through the keybindings manager and calls onSelect/onCancel/onSubmit callbacks supplied by the caller. Dialogs that return values (LoginDialog prompts, extension input/editor) resolve promises. Natively these become oneshot channels (Rust) or channels/callbacks (Go).
- **Async and timers.** CountdownTimer, Loader spinners, shimmer and easter-egg animation timers call tui.requestRender(). Async work re-checks disposal and staleness before mutating state:
  - ModelSelector refresh, with AbortController and a 15s timeout;
  - session loading, with progress and abort on scope switch;
  - kitty PNG conversion, which re-checks that the image is still current.

  Ports need a render-request channel into the TUI loop rather than mutating state from background tasks.
- **Extension surface.** Extensions supply MessageRenderer, EntryRenderer, ToolDefinition renderCall/renderResult/renderShell, MarkdownTransformer and WorkingIndicatorOptions. Under the user decisions these become native Rust traits / Go interfaces, implemented by core tool renderers and the built-in extensions (mcp, codemode, llama, tool-search).

**Build order:** A, then B (needs core/tools/render-utils and truncate), then C, D, E1, E2 and F in any order, then G last because of the barrel.

**Reverse importers outside the area:** core/tools/renderers/*, extensions/{codemode,llama,mcp}, cli/{config-selector,session-picker,startup-ui}.ts, experimental/{client-tui,client-tui-chat,durable/tui,vacation/tui}.ts, interactive-mode.ts and src/index.ts.

units.title: Interactive components foundation: borders, key hints, status indicators, custom editor, diff, mermaid
units.notes:
This unit must stay free of dependencies on other component units and on core/tools renderers. Core tool renderers, the codemode/llama/mcp extension UIs and the experimental TUIs import dynamic-border, keybinding-hints, visual-truncate and diff.

**keybinding-hints**
- On process.platform darwin, 'alt' is shown as 'option' (capitalized form 'Option').
- Bindings joined with '/'.
- keyHint = dim key + muted description.

**countdown-timer**
- remaining = ceil(ms/1000).
- onTick fires immediately, then every 1000ms with requestRender.
- onExpire fires at 0.
- dispose clears the interval.

**visual-truncate**
- Renders through a temporary pi-tui Text and keeps the last N visual lines.
- VisualLinePreview caches per width.

**markdown-transform**
- Chains transformers in order, swallows exceptions and ignores non-string returns.
- Native transformer signature: Result<String> or (string, error).

**status-indicator**
- Subclasses of Loader carrying a kind.
- Retry wraps CountdownTimer.
- Compaction labels differ for manual / threshold / overflow.
- renderInBorder / renderSpinnerInBorder are consumed by CustomEditor.
- IdleStatus renders 2 blank lines to keep the vertical layout stable.

**custom-editor**
Extends pi-tui Editor, so the native Editor needs overridable hooks (a handler trait or composition). Key dispatch order is exact and tested:
1. onExtensionShortcut
2. pasteImage
3. interrupt (skipped while autocomplete is showing)
4. exit (only when the text is empty)
5. history bindings (take precedence)
6. actionHandlers map

The top border embeds the status with ' ↑ N more ' overflow math.

**diff.ts**
- Line regex /^([+-\s])(\s*\d*)\s(.*)$/.
- Tabs become 3 spaces.
- Intra-line word diff (jsdiff diffWords, highlighted with theme.inverse) applies only when exactly one removed line pairs with one added line.
- Leading whitespace is stripped from the first change.

**mermaid.ts**
Flow:
- Marked().lexer finds top-level code tokens with lang mermaid.
- Each token.raw is replaced by grok-mermaid render() rows. Each row becomes an inline code span whose backtick fence is longer than the longest backtick run in the row; empty rows use nbsp; rows are joined with two spaces + newline.
- Warnings render only when not streaming.
- Span classes (border/text/edge/edgeLabel/title) map to theme colors.

The transformer is skipped when:
- mode is off;
- messageType is thinking;
- the message is streaming and mode != 'streaming'.

**pi-logo**
- Exact RGB constants: CORAL 228,138,122; BLUE 79,142,179; YELLOW 234,182,93.
- Half-block glyphs.
- supportsPiLogo = !isAppleTerminalSession().

units.title: Transcript components: assistant/user/custom messages, summaries, bash execution, tool execution
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/tool-renderer-examples.test.ts -- loads TS example extensions from examples/extensions through the JS extension loader; user TS extensions are not loaded in native ports
packages/coding-agent/test/streaming-render-debug.ts -- manual debug script, not a test
units.notes:
**assistant-message**
- Consecutive thinking blocks coalesce into one run. Each run has its own click-toggled visibility override on top of the global hideThinking setting.
- Spacing rules between text, thinking and tool calls are tested.
- Stop reasons:
  - 'length' shows 'Response was truncated before completion.'
  - aborted (only when there are no tool calls) shows errorMessage, or 'Operation aborted' when the message is 'Request was aborted'.
  - error shows 'Error: <msg>'.
- OSC 133 prompt markers (ESC]133;A BEL / B / C) are emitted only when the message has no tool calls.

**user-message**
- Markdown with userMessageBg; options preserveOrderedListMarkers and preserveBackslashEscapes; transform type 'user'.
- OSC 133 A goes on the first line; B+C are prefixed onto the last line.

**custom-message / custom-entry**
- Call extension MessageRenderer/EntryRenderer with {expanded, outputPad}.
- On a renderer error, fall back to a Box showing '[customType] renderer failed: msg' (entry) or a label + markdown (message).
- Natively the renderer is a trait/interface registered by built-in extensions. Custom types from extensions that are not loaded always use the fallback path.

**Collapsible summaries** (branch/compaction/skill)
- MouseRegion left-click toggles expanded.
- Compaction prints tokensBefore.toLocaleString(): en-US grouping with commas.

**bash-execution**
- stripAnsi + CRLF normalization.
- truncateTail with DEFAULT_MAX_LINES 2000 and DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES 50KB. The byte limit counts UTF-8 bytes.
- 20-line preview through a width-cached visual-truncate component.
- Status strings: '(exit N)', '(cancelled)', 'Output truncated. Full output: <path>'.

**tool-execution**
- Defines the ToolRenderers contract: renderShell 'default' vs 'self', renderCall, renderResult with ToolRenderContext state.
- Box backgrounds: toolPendingBg / toolErrorBg / toolSuccessBg.
- Fallback rendering: formatToolCallWithArgs, JSON.stringify(args, null, 2), FALLBACK_PREVIEW_LINES 10.
- Images:
  - For kitty-capable terminals, non-PNG images are converted with convertToPng.
  - The async result is ignored if the component changed meanwhile (race guard).
- Self-rendered shells offset mouse events by selfRenderHeight; hideComponent supported.
- For JSON parity:
  - Rust: serde_json with preserve_order + 2-space PrettyFormatter.
  - Go: an ordered encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false).

**earendil-announcement**
- Reads src/modes/interactive/assets/clankolas.png (an asset owned by the interactive-mode area) through getBundledInteractiveAssetPath.
- Base64 cached once; Image maxWidthCells 56.

**Tests**
- tool-execution-component.test.ts and edit-tool-no-full-redraw.test.ts need the core/tools bash/read/write/edit tools and renderers; port them after the core tools units.
- tool-execution-component.test.ts mocks utils/image-convert (vi.mock). Natively, inject the converter.

units.title: Dialog components: extension UI, login dialogs, auth/trust/theme/thinking selectors, first-time setup
units.notes:
**extension-selector / extension-input**
- Optional CountdownTimer timeout that auto-cancels.
- j/k navigation in addition to the bindings.
- A plain newline byte counts as confirm.
- app.tools.expand toggles details.

**extension-editor**
- Wraps pi-tui Editor.
- External editor is resolved from VISUAL, then EDITOR, then notepad on win32 / nano elsewhere.
- Calls tui.stop(), spawns the editor, then tui.start() and requestRender(true).
- Port the stop/start semantics with the native TUI, restoring raw mode.

**radius-login-selector**
- RadiusLoginMenuComponent extends ExtensionSelectorComponent.
- Shimmer colors #4d9abf #83ccd2 #f1be57 #f09082; 4 chars per color; 10 chars/s; 50ms frame timer with unref.
- Colors are smoothstep-interpolated with mixColors 'srgb'.
- The selected line is located by comparing rendered Text output.
- Also exports createLoginMenuSelector.

**login-dialog**
Methods:
- showAuth: calls openBrowser and renders OSC 8 hyperlinks (ESC]8;;url BEL).
- showDeviceCode.
- showManualInput / showPrompt: return Promise<string>. After submit, the input is replaced by a '> value' Text.
- showDetails, showInfo, showWaiting, showProgress.

On cancel: abort the AbortSignal, reject with 'Login cancelled', and call onComplete(false, ...). Native mapping: oneshot channel plus a cancellation token.

**oauth-selector**
- AuthSelectorProvider type.
- formatAuthSelectorProviderType returns 'API key' / 'account' / 'subscription'.
- formatAuthSelectorProviderStatus adds an 'env: ' prefix when the source looks like an env var (uppercase-identifier regex).
- maxVisible 8; fuzzyFilter search.

**trust-selector**
- Options come from getProjectTrustOptions(cwd).
- Decisions inherited from a parent show 'inherited from'.

**first-time-setup**
- Two steps: theme (system/dark/light), then analytics.
- Fixed analytics text with APP_NAME.

**thinking-selector**
- LEVEL_DESCRIPTIONS.
- Search Input with fuzzyFilter. The SelectList is rebuilt by replacing container children[index]; the native Container must support indexed replacement.
- app.thinking.save binding.

**user-message-selector**
- Wrap-around navigation; maxVisible 10.
- With no messages it auto-cancels through setTimeout(100). Keep it deferred, not synchronous.

**theme-selector**
- onSelectionChange live preview.

**Tests**
- The first case in oauth-selector.test.ts calls InteractiveMode.prototype.getLoginProviderOptions; port that case with the interactive-mode unit.
- The 5433 regression covers LoginDialog prompt input.

units.title: Model selector, scoped models selector, settings selector/submenus, footer
units.notes:
**model-selector**
- Scope all/scoped, toggled with tab.
- Sort order: current model first, then the default, then provider localeCompare.
- A query starting with 'default' pins the default model.
- Fuzzy search via model-search. Changing the filter resets the selection (regression 7209).
- refreshModels:
  - refreshModelCatalogs with a 15s timeout and an AbortController.
  - On failure: 'Could not refresh N model catalogs (a, b); showing cached models.'
  - dispose() aborts the refresh.
  - Async results are applied only while the component is still alive.
- Models.json hot reload covered by regression 6999.

**scoped-models-selector**
- enabledIds null means all models are enabled.
- Helpers: toggle, enableAll, clearAll, move, normalizeEnabled.
- Order is preserved (regression 3217).
- Hardcoded matchesKey: ctrl+c clears the search, or cancels when it is empty; escape cancels. Keep this behavior for parity.
- Footer shows an '(unsaved)' marker.

**settings-submenu**
- SelectSubmenu: optional searchable Input, list layout min 12 / max 32, hint text.
- SteppedSubmenu: multi-step flow with context and loop; Esc goes back one step.

**settings-selector**
- SettingsConfig/SettingsCallbacks.
- WarningSettingsSubmenu.
- ThemeSubmenu: single theme or automatic 'light/dark' pair (AUTOMATIC_THEME_VALUE '/').
- Per-model thinking SteppedSubmenu with CLEAR_OVERRIDE_VALUE '__clear__'.
- Items are inserted in splice order. show-images and image-width appear only when getCapabilities().images is set.
- Wheel scroll choices dedupe [1,2,3,5,10,current] and sort them; HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_CHOICES.
- provider localeCompare.

**footer**
- formatTokens: <1000 raw; <10k toFixed(1)+'k'; <1M round+'k'; <10M toFixed(1)+'M'; otherwise round+'M'.
- JS toFixed rounds exact binary ties up: 1250 gives '1.3k'. Rust format! and Go FormatFloat round half-to-even and would give '1.2k', so implement a JS-compatible toFixed.
- Stats parts: ↑ ↓ R W CH% $cost.toFixed(3) '(sub)' ctx%/window '(auto)', plus an xp marker when experimental.
- Session stats cache keyed by session/sessionId/leafId/entryCount/limitsModel.
- Right side: model, thinking level and routed model; adds '(provider)' when width allows.
- formatCwdForFooter: home shortening from HOME/USERPROFILE plus path.relative/sep.
- Extension statuses sorted by localeCompare.
- The status-source regex accepts uppercase identifiers separated by ', '.
- formatTokens is also imported by the experimental TUIs.

units.title: Session selector (resume picker) and session search
units.notes:
**session-selector-search**
parseSearchQuery:
- 're:' prefix compiles a user regex with flag 'i'. It needs an ECMAScript-compatible engine: Rust regress or fancy-regex, Go dlclark/regexp2 in ECMAScript mode. An invalid regex yields an error/no-match state.
- Otherwise tokens, with quoted phrases. Unbalanced quotes fall back to whitespace splitting.

matchSession scoring:
- regex: match index * 0.1;
- phrase: index * 0.1;
- tokens: fuzzyMatch score.

filterAndSortSessions:
- 'recent' keeps input order;
- 'relevance' sorts by score, then modified time descending.

Also hasSessionName.

**session-selector**
- Header shows scope (current/all), sort mode, named filter, loading progress (SessionListProgress), delete confirmation and auto-hiding status messages (setTimeout).
- buildSessionTree:
  - links sessions through the canonical parentSessionPath;
  - sorts by latest subtree activity;
  - draws tree connectors in threaded mode.
- formatSessionDate buckets: now / Nm / Nh / Nd / Nw / Nmo / Ny.
- Delete:
  - spawnSync('trash', [maybe '--', path]); '--' is passed when the path starts with '-';
  - if the file still exists, fall back to fs.unlink.
  - Tests use symlinked tmp dirs and compare canonical paths.
- Rename mode uses an inline Input.
- loadScope: an AbortController per load; switching scope cancels the in-flight load.
- Home shortening via os.homedir.
- Also used by cli/session-picker.ts.

units.title: Session tree selector (/tree navigator)
units.notes:
**flattenTree**
- Iterative (explicit stack, no recursion), so deep sessions cannot overflow.
- Children on the active branch are ordered first.
- Indent, gutter and connector rules (├─ └─ │) are tested exactly.
- With multiple roots, a virtual root is used.

**Filters and search**
- Filter modes: default / no-tools / user-only / labeled-only / all.
- Search tokens match against entry text.

**Folding and layout**
- Folding with ⊞/⊟ markers.
- recalculateVisualStructure runs after filter or fold changes.
- Horizontal viewport scrolling with a gutter of 2, using sliceByColumn and wrapTextWithAnsi.

**formatToolCall**
- One-line summaries per tool name: read/write/edit/bash/grep/find/ls.
- Tool paths are shortened with HOME or USERPROFILE.
- Unknown tools render JSON.stringify(args).slice(0, 40) + '...' when longer. That slice counts UTF-16 code units; emulate it for parity (ASCII tests).
- Compaction entries show Math.round(tokensBefore/1000)+'k'.

**Labels and timestamps**
- formatLabelTimestamp uses local time: today shows only HH:MM, otherwise a date.
- New labels get new Date().toISOString(), i.e. a millisecond 'Z' ISO string.
- LabelInput is an inline component.

**Help and key handling**
- TreeHelp compacts key names with word-boundary regex replacements (pageUp to pgup, arrows to glyphs).
- Search input is handled manually: control characters are filtered and printable text is appended.
- Navigation runs through keybindings.
- InteractiveMode wiring is tested separately in interactive-mode-tree-navigation.test.ts (other area).

units.title: Config selector (pi config resource toggles)
units.notes:
**Resource groups**
- Built from package-manager ResolvedPaths and grouped by scope (global/project) and source.
- Groups sort by source localeCompare; items by displayName localeCompare.
- builtin: sources use BUILTIN_PATH_PREFIX.
- Paths are displayed through path.relative/dirname/basename and os.homedir shortening.

**Toggling**
- Writes settings through SettingsManager setters (setExtensionPaths/setProjectExtensionPaths, setPackages/setProjectPackages, plus the skills/prompts/themes equivalents).
- Pattern prefixes: '+' force-include, '-' exclude, '!' negate.
- Project override cycle: inherit -> load -> unload.
- Helpers: canonicalizePath, isLocalPath, resolvePath (utils/paths).
- The written settings JSON must stay byte-compatible with the TS output (settings-manager port).

**Keys**
- Hardcoded matchesKey for ctrl+c / escape alongside the keybindings; keep it for parity.
- Focusable search Input.

**Tests**
- package-command-paths.test.ts: only the ConfigSelector cases (about lines 498-590) belong here. The rest of the file tests the package-manager CLI and belongs to that area.

**Consumers**
- cli/config-selector.ts launches it.

units.title: Easter eggs (Armin, Armin 3D overlay, Daxnuts) and components barrel
units.notes:
Port this unit last: index.ts re-exports every component. In Rust it becomes pub use lines in components/mod.rs; in Go, exported identifiers of the components package (no barrel file). Only src/index.ts imports the barrel.

**armin.ts**
- XBM bitmap 31x36; exports ARMIN_WIDTH, ARMIN_HEIGHT and isArminPixel.
- One of 7 reveal effects is chosen with Math.random: typewriter, scanline, rain, fade, crt, glitch, dissolve. Non-deterministic, so any RNG works.
- Interval timers at 30/60fps; caption 'ARMIN SAYS HI'.

**armin-3d.lazy.ts**
- playArmin3d(tui):
  - returns false unless tui is a TuiAltScreen (fullscreen);
  - returns true if an overlay is already showing;
  - captures tui.getScreenLines(), then dynamically imports armin-3d.ts.
- Natively this is a direct call.

**armin-3d.ts**
- parseScreen: an SGR parser into cells.
  - Handles colon sub-parameters, 256-color and truecolor.
  - Skips OSC/APC/DCS/PM strings.
  - Splits graphemes with Intl.Segmenter (Rust unicode-segmentation, Go rivo/uniseg) and accounts for wide graphemes with visibleWidth.
- LogoRaster:
  - ray-casts cube faces with a depth buffer (Float32Array: use f32 storage to match quantization);
  - packs braille 2x4 dots;
  - halo blur on light backgrounds.
- Sliding-puzzle shuffle uses a deterministic hash built on Math.imul and uint32 arithmetic (Rust wrapping_mul on u32, Go uint32 multiply).
- Spin/linger easing and starfield flicker are timed with performance.now; FRAME_MS is 30fps with unref.
- The exit animation reverses; close on escape, app.clear or a mouse click.
- Module-level `playing` guard.
- tui.queryTerminalColors({timeoutMs: 100}) picks the light/dark halo.
- Math.round on positive values only; f64::round/math.Round are fine.
- Visual only, no tests: verify manually in fullscreen mode via /arminsayshi.

**daxnuts.ts**
- 32x32 hex pixel image rendered with ▄ half blocks (fg/bg truecolor).
- Scanline reveal over 25 ticks at 80ms.
- Centered by measuring width after stripping SGR.

external_deps.used_for: mermaid.ts: renders mermaid fenced blocks into terminal text art. render(src) returns {width, warnings, rows of styled spans with classes border/text/edge/edgeLabel/title/none} or null. The library is about 4.6k lines of TS under node_modules/grok-mermaid/src.
external_deps.rust_suggestion: Hand-port grok-mermaid into its own crate or module (e.g. pi-coding-agent::mermaid). No crate produces identical box-drawing output (mermaid-rs/merman target SVG). Port its tests/fixtures for byte parity.
external_deps.go_suggestion: Hand-port into an internal/grokmermaid package. No Go library matches the output (mermaid-go/d2 render SVG).

external_deps.used_for: diff.ts: diffWords for intra-line highlighting of a single removed+added line pair. The tokenizer uses Unicode-aware word regexes (u flag), with whitespace stitching and post-processing. Probably shared with core/tools/edit-diff.ts.
external_deps.rust_suggestion: Hand-port jsdiff's Diff base (Myers with jsdiff's path selection) plus the wordDiff tokenizer/postprocess into a small shared module. The similar crate tokenizes and orders changes differently, so only use it if outputs are proven equal.
external_deps.go_suggestion: Hand-port the jsdiff base and wordDiff into a shared internal/jsdiff package. sergi/go-diff (diff-match-patch) gives different chunking.

external_deps.used_for: mermaid.ts: new Marked().lexer(markdown) finds top-level code tokens (lang mermaid) and uses token.raw for exact source replacement.
external_deps.rust_suggestion: Reuse the marked-compatible lexer from the pi-tui Rust port (needed for Markdown anyway). pulldown-cmark offsets do not reproduce marked's token.raw boundaries (e.g. trailing newlines).
external_deps.go_suggestion: Reuse the pi-tui Go port's marked-compatible lexer. goldmark segments differ from marked raw text.

hazards: **Global singletons.** The theme proxy and getKeybindings() are read at render/input time by nearly every component. Ports need global, swappable instances (RwLock/atomic pointer) and must call invalidate on theme changes. Tests set the theme explicitly (initTheme) before asserting ANSI.

**Exact escape sequences are asserted.** Theme fg/bg/bold/inverse SGR (chalk-generated, truecolor vs 256-color by getColorMode), OSC 133 A/B/C zone markers on user/assistant messages, OSC 8 hyperlinks in login-dialog, and literal bold on/off (ESC[1m / ESC[22m) labels. Native output must be byte-identical.

**JS toFixed rounding.** Exact binary ties round up (1250 tokens -> '1.3k'; 0.25 -> '0.3'), while Rust format! and Go strconv round half-to-even. Footer formatTokens, context percent, cache-hit percent and cost toFixed(3) need a JS-compatible toFixed helper.

**Number and string locale behavior.** toLocaleString in compaction-summary-message assumes en-US comma grouping. localeCompare sorts provider names, extension statuses and config-selector sources/display names; ICU collation differs from byte ordering for case/accents. Use a locale-aware compare (Rust icu_collator / feruca, Go golang.org/x/text/collate) or document a byte-order deviation. Tests mostly use lowercase ASCII.

**User regex search.** Session search 're:' compiles user input with new RegExp(pattern, 'i'), so ECMAScript syntax (lookbehind, backrefs, named groups) must be accepted. Rust: regress (ECMAScript) or fancy-regex. Go: dlclark/regexp2 with ECMAScript option. Invalid patterns must not crash.

**UTF-16 vs UTF-8 string slicing.** JSON.stringify(args).slice(0, 40) in tree-selector and other .length/.slice truncations count UTF-16 code units. Native ports must emulate this or slice by chars without splitting a codepoint. Tests are ASCII.

**JSON.stringify(args, null, 2) parity** in tool-execution fallback rendering: insertion key order, 2-space indent, no HTML escaping, JS number formatting. Go encoding/json escapes <>& and sorts map keys unless an ordered type and SetEscapeHTML(false) are used. Rust serde_json needs preserve_order.
**Graphemes in armin-3d parseScreen.** Intl.Segmenter grapheme segmentation plus wide-character width handling; use unicode-segmentation (Rust) / rivo/uniseg (Go) and the pi-tui visibleWidth port.

**armin-3d numeric parity.** The deterministic shuffle hash uses Math.imul and >>> 0 (u32 wrapping semantics). Float32Array buffers quantize to f32. Animation timing uses performance.now. Math.round is round-half-up toward +inf (differs from Rust/Go round for negative halves).

**Timers and async.** CountdownTimer (1s), Loader spinners, the radius shimmer (50ms, unref), the armin/daxnuts/armin3d animation intervals, setTimeout(100) auto-cancel in user-message-selector, and status auto-hide timeouts in session-selector all call tui.requestRender. Native ports must route timer ticks through the TUI event loop and cancel timers on dispose, so no tick lands after the component is gone.

**Async staleness and abort.** ModelSelector refresh (AbortController, 15s timeout, abort on dispose), session-selector loadScope (abort on scope toggle, progress callbacks) and tool-execution kitty PNG conversion (ignore results for outdated images) all guard against stale results. Port them with cancellation tokens/contexts and generation counters.

**Promise-based dialogs.** LoginDialog showPrompt/showManualInput and extension input/editor return promises resolved by key handlers. Cancel aborts an AbortSignal and rejects with 'Login cancelled'. Map these to oneshot channels plus cancellation, keeping the resolve-then-onComplete ordering.

**Session deletion shells out.** spawnSync('trash', ['--'?, path]) is tried first (with '--' when the path starts with '-'). If the file still exists afterwards, fs.unlink runs. A missing trash binary must fall through silently. Tests use symlinked tmp dirs and canonical paths.

**Platform branches.** darwin shows 'alt' as 'option' and 'Cmd+click' instead of 'Ctrl+click'. External editor falls back to notepad on win32, otherwise nano, after VISUAL/EDITOR. HOME vs USERPROFILE for footer cwd and tree tool-path shortening; os.homedir in session/config selectors. path.relative/sep differ per OS.

**Local-time formatting.** Tree label timestamps (today shows only HH:MM) and session-selector relative dates (now/m/h/d/w/mo/y) use the local timezone and new Date(); label creation stores new Date().toISOString() with millisecond 'Z' format.

**Hardcoded matchesKey** checks for ctrl+c/escape in scoped-models-selector and config-selector bypass configurable keybindings. Preserve the behavior in the port (do not silently convert) and flag it for a later upstream fix.

**Mutable children.** Container children are replaced by index (thinking-selector, settings submenus rebuild SelectList in place). The native Container needs indexed replacement while focus stays on the right child.
**Truncation limits are bytes.** BashExecution uses truncateTail with DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES (50KB, UTF-8 bytes) and DEFAULT_MAX_LINES 2000; preserve the semantics from core/tools/truncate.ts.

**CustomEditor key dispatch order** (extension shortcut, paste image, interrupt unless autocomplete, exit only when empty, history bindings precedence, action handlers) is tested. The native Editor must expose a pre-dispatch hook so the subclass behavior can be composed.
**Third-party library parity.** grok-mermaid, jsdiff diffWords and marked token.raw must be hand-ported for byte-identical output. No off-the-shelf Rust/Go library matches.
js_runtime_dependent: **Extension-provided renderers** (MessageRenderer, EntryRenderer, ToolDefinition.renderCall/renderResult/renderShell, MarkdownTransformer, WorkingIndicatorOptions) are JS callbacks from loaded extensions. They become native Rust traits / Go interfaces implemented by core tools and the built-in extensions (mcp, codemode, llama, tool-search). User TS extensions are not loaded, so custom message/entry types from unknown extensions always take the CustomMessageComponent/CustomEntry fallback rendering.

**Extension UI dialogs** (ExtensionSelector/Input/Editor, radius login menu, LoginDialog prompts for extension OAuth) are driven by the ctx.ui API from extensions. Keep the components, invoked through the native extension UI trait/interface by built-in extensions and native auth providers.

**armin-3d.lazy.ts** uses a dynamic import('./armin-3d.ts') to defer loading. Natively it is a direct function call (optionally behind a Cargo feature / Go build tag); the fullscreen and overlay guards stay.
**mermaid.ts** depends on the grok-mermaid JS library at runtime. Port the library natively and drop the JS dependency.

**dynamic-border.ts module-cache comment.** The comment about extensions loaded through jiti getting a separate theme module instance (hence the explicit theme parameter) does not apply natively. Keep the optional color-function parameter for API parity.
**tool-renderer-examples.test.ts** executes TS example extensions through the extension loader. It is skipped because user TS extensions are not loaded natively.

reports.summary:
The ca-cli-modes area is the outer shell of the coding-agent package. It covers:
- process entry points
- argument parsing
- subcommands: auth, package management, experimental server/client, and the mcp hand-off
- startup UI: first-time setup, session picker, project-trust prompt, config selector
- the three non-interactive run modes: print text, JSON event stream, and RPC over JSONL
- the RpcClient used by embedders
- config and on-disk migrations
- the public SDK surface (index.ts)
- shipped docs, packaging metadata, and all examples

ENTRY POINTS
- cli.ts runs cli/setup.ts (proxy and undici dispatcher bootstrap), then calls main(argv).
- rpc-entry.ts is an alternate entry that forces `--mode rpc`.
- bun/cli.ts is the compiled-binary entry. It:
  - restores the sandbox env from /proc/self/environ when Bun starts with an empty env;
  - registers the Bun OAuth and Bedrock providers;
  - points codemode at an embedded quickjs.wasm.
- In Rust and Go all of these become one native `main`. Assets are embedded with include_bytes!/go:embed, so the Bun shims go away.
- index.ts becomes lib.rs / the Go package's exported surface (SDK re-exports, RpcClient, modes, components).

MAIN.TS ORDER
The order is load-bearing: it decides stdout cleanliness and exit codes.
1. `pi auth check|print-api-key|print-bearer-token`. Exit codes: 0 ready, 1 not_ready, 2 invalid.
2. Windows quarantine cleanup, then managed-install cleanup.
3. Settings, proxy, and dispatcher bootstrap.
4. Package commands: install, remove/uninstall, update, list, config.
5. `mcp` subcommand.
6. parseArgs.
7. --version, then --export.
8. takeOverStdout for json/rpc, so only protocol records reach stdout and everything else goes to stderr.
9. runMigrations.
10. First-time setup.
11. Session directory and session resolution:
    - flags: --session, --fork, --resume, --continue, --session-id;
    - lookup order: path, local exact id, local prefix, global exact id, global prefix;
    - a session from another project needs a readline [y/N] confirm.
12. Runtime creation: trust, settings, services, and model scope (15 s timeout).
13. --help and --list-models. These run after extensions load so extension flags appear in help.
14. Read piped stdin.
15. Build the initial message, including @file arguments via file-processor.
16. initTheme.
17. Deprecation warnings and diagnostics (fatal diagnostics exit 1).
18. No-model error.
19. Mode dispatch: interactive, print, json, or rpc.

CLI PARSING
args.ts is a hand-written parser. Its semantics do not map cleanly onto clap or cobra:
- unknown `--flags` are collected into unknownFlags so extension flags can use them;
- `--x=y` is supported;
- `--` ends option parsing (#7269);
- `@file` arguments are collected separately;
- `-p` has special rules for when it consumes the next argument;
- error texts are exact;
- help is colored with chalk, includes an env-var list, and pads extension flags with padEnd(30).

Port it as a hand-written parser and golden-test printHelp. The experimental CLI (cli/experimental) is a small command/option registry for `server` and `client`. The stable cli must never dispatch to it (#9132).

PRINT AND JSON MODES
- Text mode prints the last assistant text.
- JSON mode writes the session header first, then toJsonEvent for each session event:
  - `partial` is stripped from message_update, which becomes {type, usage, assistantMessageEvent};
  - toolcall_start is enriched with id and toolName.
- Writes respect stdout backpressure.
- Exit codes: 1 on error/aborted stop reasons (message to stderr), 143 on SIGTERM, 129 on SIGHUP.
- session_shutdown is always emitted through runtimeHost.dispose.

RPC MODE
- stdin carries LF-delimited JSON commands. There are about 36 command types in rpc-types.ts. A trailing CR is stripped; U+2028 and U+2029 are kept inside lines.
- stdout carries:
  - responses: {id, type:"response", command, success, data | error}; parse failures use command "parse";
  - streamed session events;
  - extension_ui_request records with randomUUID ids. Dialog methods wait for extension_ui_response; notify, setStatus, setWidget, setTitle and set_editor_text are fire-and-forget.
- Input lines are dispatched concurrently: handleInputLine is not awaited. This is required. Example: a prompt whose preflight runs an extension command that opens ui.select is still pending when the client sends extension_ui_response. A serial reader would deadlock here.
- The prompt response is sent only after preflight, and carries a disposition (started / handled / queued).
- get_commands order: extension commands, then prompt templates, then `skill:<name>`.
- Shutdown happens on stdin EOF or when an extension requests it.

RPCCLIENT
- Spawns `<pi> --mode rpc`.
- Request ids are `req_N`, with a 30 s timeout.
- On child exit, pending requests are rejected with "Agent process exited (code=X signal=Y)".
- stop() sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 1 s.
- promptAndWait and waitForIdle complete on agent_settled.

PACKAGE MANAGER CLI
- Sources: npm, git, and local. Scopes: project (-l) and global.
- Supports trust prompts (--approve/-a, --no-approve/-na), config toggles, and `update --self/--extensions/--models/--all`.
- Self-update goes through PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE using a managed release layout:
  - marker file managed-install.json with layout releases-v1;
  - proper-lockfile locks;
  - `npm ci --ignore-scripts`;
  - an atomic current-version switch.
- Native self-update must instead download and switch native release binaries in the same layout. npm and git resource packages still install through npm/git. TS extensions inside packages are discovered but never loaded.

MIGRATIONS
- oauth.json and settings.apiKeys move to auth.json (mode 0600).
- Flat session files move into encoded cwd directories `--<cwd with / \ : replaced by ->--`. scripts/migrate-sessions.sh is the bash+jq equivalent.
- commands/ becomes prompts/, and tools/ becomes bin/.
- Keybinding names are renamed.
- Deprecated hooks/ and tools/ directories produce warnings.

DOCS
docs/** ships with the package; the system prompt points to it as "Additional docs".
- The wire references are normative for byte compatibility and are kept verbatim: cli, environment-variables, json, rpc, rpc-commands, rpc-extension-ui, session-format, message-types.
- sdk, extensions, tui, custom-provider and parts of cli-integration need Rust/Go rewrites.
- documentation.test validates docs.json navigation and links.

EXAMPLES
Become native examples:
- examples/sdk 01-14. 06 changes from loading a .ts path to registering a native extension.
- rpc-client and rpc-extension-ui. These spawn the native binary.
- About 85 extension examples. Each becomes a native implementation of the Extension trait/interface, registered at compile time in an examples binary or crate.
- custom-provider-anthropic and custom-provider-gitlab-duo, reusing the native pi-ai providers.

JS-only:
- doom-overlay (Emscripten glue). A native version needs a WASI rebuild of doomgeneric run under wasmtime/wazero.
- gondolin (npm micro-VM library).
- sandbox (@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime). A native rewrite is possible via sandbox-exec/bubblewrap.
- with-deps (demonstrates jiti dependency resolution).
- plugins/pi-example-plugin (Chord TS facets).

UNIT SPLIT
- Four code units: cli-args-auth-migrations, cli-main-entry, package-manager-cli-startup-ui, modes-print-json-rpc.
- Two docs/packaging units.
- Seven example units.

units.title: CLI argument parser, help, auth/credential subcommands, list-models, @file processing, experimental CLI registry, migrations
units.notes:
args.ts:
- Port it as a hand-written parser. Do not use clap or cobra: error texts, the unknownFlags capture for extension flags, the `--x=y` form, `--` end of options (#7269), `@file` collection, and the `-p` rule (consumes the next arg unless it starts with @ or -) must all match.
- Thinking levels: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. `--tui-mode` accepts regular|fullscreen.
- printHelp must be byte-identical, including chalk SGR codes (bold = \x1b[1m..\x1b[22m) and the env-var list. Extension flags are padded with padEnd(30). Write a golden test for it.
- `--offline` sets PI_OFFLINE=1 and PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 (applied in main).

auth-command / auth-check / credential-print:
- `--min-expiry` regex is ^(\d+)(ms|s|m|h)$ (case-insensitive). Bearer extraction uses ^Bearer\s+(.+)$ (case-insensitive). Default bearer min expiry is 30 min.
- Other flags: --json, --credentials, --no-refresh. The JSON output key order must match TS.
- Exit codes 0/1/2 are set in main. credential-print.test also calls main(); port that part after cli-main-entry exists.

list-models: the table layout uses tui visibleWidth.

file-processor:
- Turns @file args into text blocks or image attachments.
- Respects blockImages and autoResize, and can defer resizing until prompt dispatch.
- block-images.test and image-resize-callers.test are shared with the core tools (read tool) unit. Port only their processFileArguments cases here.

Experimental CLI:
- A registry parser. cli.parse([]) returns errors ["Expected experimental command: server or client"].
- --server-id must be a lowercase UUIDv4 (isServerId in pi-protocol).
- --connect accepts unix:///path or radius://<uuid>. Check that the url crate / net/url parse the tested inputs the same way WHATWG URL does.

migrations.ts:
- oauth.json and settings.apiKeys move into auth.json (0600).
- Sessions are re-homed into `--${cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/,'').replace(/[/\\:]/g,'-')}--`.
- commands/ becomes prompts/, tools/ becomes bin/, keybinding ids are renamed, and deprecated hooks/ and tools/ produce warnings.
- Uppercase env-like values stay literal (#5661).
- migrate-sessions.sh ships as-is (bash+jq). It is an asset, not ported code.

units.title: main() orchestration, stable/rpc entry points, SDK public surface, Bun runtime shims
units.notes:
main.ts:
- Keep the startup order listed in the area summary exactly. Moving takeOverStdout, migrations, or help/list-models changes stdout cleanliness: in `--mode json --help --approve`, stdout must stay empty while npm chatter and Usage go to stderr (stdout-cleanliness.test).
- Use explicit exit paths. In Rust, std::process::exit does not flush stdout buffers, so flush first. In Go, os.Exit skips defers.
- The session-resolution conflict rules (--fork/--session/--resume/--continue/--session-id) and the readline [y/N] cross-project confirm must match docs/cli.md.
- An invalid session file prints `Error: Session file is not a valid pi session: <path>`, exits 1, prints no stack trace, and leaves the file untouched.
- --name is applied to the selected session before model validation (startup-session-name.test).
- `--session-id` is read-only semantics; see session-id-readonly.test, which calls createSessionManager from main.
- The model scope has a 15 s timeout. In RPC mode the model catalog is refreshed in the background.
- `-e <path.ts>`: user TS extensions are not loaded natively. Keep the flag in the parser and turn TS paths into a clear diagnostic.

cli.ts must not dispatch experimental commands (#9132). `pi server --server-id invalid --version` prints the version. The experimental entry itself lives outside this area; port only the stable-entry assertions of experimental-cli-entry.test here.

rpc-entry.ts: becomes a `--mode rpc` default in the same binary. Optionally ship a `pi-rpc` alias.

index.ts: maps to lib.rs (Rust) or the exported identifiers of the root Go package. Export the same logical surface: createAgentSession, SessionManager, SettingsManager, AuthStorage, ModelRegistry, tools, RpcClient, runPrintMode/runRpcMode, theme, components, and helpers.

bun/*:
- runtime-setup becomes embedded quickjs.wasm (include_bytes!/go:embed) plus static provider registration.
- quickjs-wasm.d.ts is dropped.
- restore-sandbox-env (parses "FOO=bar\0BAZ=qux\0" from /proc/self/environ only when the env is empty) is unnecessary for native binaries. Port it only as an optional Linux fallback, and keep restore-sandbox-env.test for its parser only.

Tests that spawn the CLI must use the built binary (CARGO_BIN_EXE_pi, or `go build` in TestMain).

units.title: pi install/remove/update/list/config, managed self-update, startup TUI (first-time setup, session picker, trust prompt, config selector)
units.notes:
package-manager-cli:
- Commands: install, remove/uninstall, update, list, config.
- Flags: -l, --approve/-a, --no-approve/-na, --force, --self/--extensions/--models/--all/--extension. Unknown-option errors use the same text as auth commands.
- npm is invoked through the npmCommand setting (argv array) with --ignore-scripts.

Self-update:
- Talks to PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE (default https://pi.dev/api/installer/releases).
- Marker managed-install.json is {kind:"pi-managed-install",schemaVersion:1,layout:"releases-v1"}.
- releases/<version> directories, an atomic rename of current-version, and proper-lockfile on the root and update targets.
- Natively, the release payload is a platform binary archive instead of an npm tree. Keep the marker, layout, and lock protocol (mkdir `<file>.lock`, mtime refreshed, stale after 10 s) so the installer script and concurrent TS installs interoperate.
- Windows npm quarantine and pending-delete logic is in utils/windows-self-update. Port it for Windows builds only.
- Packages containing TS extensions: install and list them, but natively surface their extensions as "not loadable (TS)". Skills, prompts, and themes still work.

startup-ui:
- Runs a mini TUI before the main runtime and queries the terminal background color for the theme.
- shouldRunFirstTimeSetup is true only when all hold: official distribution (not a fork; see first-time-setup-fork.test), PI_EXPERIMENTAL enabled, no ENV_AGENT_DIR override, and no settings.json.
- session-picker and config-selector wrap interactive components. Port them after the interactive-mode components exist.

cli/project-trust: prompts for trusting project-local resources. Shared by main and the package commands.

package-command-paths.test (1037 lines) uses fake npm .mjs scripts. Replace them with POSIX sh scripts, or with small Rust/Go helper binaries built for tests, and skip shell-specific cases on Windows.

units.title: Print/JSON event mode, RPC JSONL mode, RPC types and RpcClient
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/rpc.test.ts -- e2e: requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and spawns built dist/cli.js against a real provider
packages/coding-agent/test/rpc-example.ts -- manual interactive script driving a real provider, not a test
units.notes:
jsonl.ts:
- Split on LF only, using a streaming UTF-8 decoder so multi-byte characters survive chunk boundaries. Strip one trailing \r. Never split on U+2028/2029.
- serializeJsonLine = JSON.stringify(value) + "\n".
- Natively, use BufRead::read_until(b'\n') / bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n'), with the final unterminated line flushed on EOF.

JSON output must match JSON.stringify:
- Key insertion order: use structs, or serde_json with preserve_order.
- No escaping of U+2028/2029, '<', '>' or '&'. Go's encoding/json always escapes U+2028/2029, so use a custom encoder or encoding/json/v2 with HTML escaping off.
- JS number formatting: integers without .0, shortest round-trip floats. In Rust use ryu-js.
- Omit undefined fields instead of writing null.

json-event.toJsonEvent:
- message_update becomes {type, usage, assistantMessageEvent} with `partial` removed.
- toolcall_start gains id and toolName (#7925).
- Usage stays on message_update (#7911). Output stays linear, never buffered out of order (#7290).

print-mode:
- JSON mode writes the session header line first.
- Text mode prints the last assistant text. On stopReason error/aborted, print the message to stderr and exit 1.
- SIGTERM exits 143; SIGHUP exits 129 (non-Windows).
- runtimeHost.dispose emits session_shutdown exactly once.
- Respect stdout backpressure (writeRawStdout / waitForRawStdoutBackpressure).

rpc-mode:
- Calls takeOverStdout.
- Must handle input lines concurrently: spawn a task or goroutine per line. Reason: extension_ui_response must resolve pending dialogs while a prompt preflight is still awaiting them.
- Response shapes:
  - success: {id?, type:"response", command, success:true, data?}
  - failure: {id?, type:"response", command, success:false, error}
  - parse failures: command "parse" with text "Failed to parse command: <msg>". The <msg> suffix is V8-specific and cannot match natively; document it.
- An unknown command echoes its id (#5868).
- The prompt response is sent only after preflight, with a disposition.
- Extension UI requests use UUIDv4 ids.
- user_bash hooks fail closed (#9068). That test also has an interactive part owned by interactive-mode.
- Shutdown on stdin end, signal (143/129), or extension shutdown request. Skip the stdout flush on SIGTERM.

rpc-client:
- Spawns the native pi binary (not node).
- Ids are req_N; default timeout 30 s.
- Pending requests are rejected with `Agent process exited (code=43 signal=null)`. Go and Rust have to synthesize the `null` text.
- stop() sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 1 s.
- waitForIdle and promptAndWait resolve on agent_settled.
- Tests that use node child scripts should use `sh -c 'exit 43'` or a tiny test helper binary.

rpc-prompt-response-semantics.test mocks output-guard/jsonl/theme. Natively, inject the writer through a trait or interface.

units.title: Wire-format and integration reference docs (CLI, env vars, JSON, RPC, SDK, extensions)
units.notes:
This unit is prose (src_lines counts markdown lines).

Copy verbatim; these are the normative byte-compat spec. Native code must satisfy them, and Rust/Go RPC tests should cite them:
- cli.md
- environment-variables.md
- json.md
- rpc.md
- rpc-commands.md
- rpc-extension-ui.md

Rewrite for the native ports:
- sdk.md: TS createAgentSession examples become the Rust/Go SDK.
- extensions.md: the ExtensionAPI TS interface becomes the native trait/interface. State that TS extensions are not loaded and that extensions are compiled in.
- cli-integration.md: the node spawn snippets.

Keep the headings and anchors stable; docs.json and documentation.test validate the link targets.

units.title: User guides, docs navigation, images, package README and package metadata
units.notes:
This unit is prose and assets (src_lines counts markdown/json lines).

docs.json:
- Navigation groups: Get Started; Guides (Run Pi / Customize Pi / Build on Pi); Reference.
- Redirects: development to index, session to session-format, tree to sessions, process-integration to cli-integration.
- documentation.test checks the docs.json schema, link targets, and that there are no orphan pages. It parses with the marked lexer; use pulldown-cmark or goldmark natively.

Session and message reference: session-format.md and message-types.md describe the on-disk JSONL and must stay exact.

Rewrite for native:
- tui.md (TS Component API to native TUI API) and custom-provider.md (registerProvider in TS to native).
- README.md: native install (binary or installer script instead of npm/Node 22), and dev commands (cargo/go instead of npm run check, ./test.sh).

Docs and examples must be embedded or installed next to the binary and resolved through config.ts helpers (getDocsPath/getExamplesPath). The system prompt points at them.

package.json:
- Metadata only; its native equivalents are Cargo.toml and go.mod.
- Carry over the bin name `pi` and piConfig.configDir ".pi" (the config dir name) as constants.
- package-distribution.test asserts the npm export map. Rewrite it as a native packaging assertion: binary name, and rpc-entry equivalent `pi --mode rpc`.

units.title: SDK examples 01-14, RPC client examples, experimental Chord plugin example
units.notes:
Native examples (Rust: cargo examples under examples/; Go: example programs under examples/sdk/NN-name/main.go):
- sdk/01-14. Each must compile in CI, but only examples that don't call a provider (or that use the faux provider) should run in CI.
- 06-extensions currently loads a .ts path. Change it to register a native Extension implementation inline.
- 09 and 14 use the auth storage, codemode, and MCP native modules.

rpc-client.ts becomes a native RpcClient demo that spawns the pi binary.

rpc-extension-ui.ts (661 lines) is a full TUI client for the RPC extension-UI protocol. Port it natively on the native pi-tui; it pairs with examples/extensions/rpc-demo.

plugins/pi-example-plugin is JS-only. It uses Chord facets and the experimental/plugin TS entry. Keep it as a reference under legacy/ or docs. It is used by the experimental-presentation-facets and experimental-remote-runtime tests (another area); port it only if Chord itself is ported natively.

Rewrite README.md and sdk/README.md for cargo/go run commands.

units.title: Extension examples: lifecycle hooks, input transforms, tool gating/overrides, providers payload, compaction
units.notes:
All of these become native examples implementing the Extension trait/interface.

Recommended layout:
- Rust: crate `pi-examples` with one module per example, plus a binary that registers the chosen examples by name. For example, `pi-examples --example hello` builds the runtime with Hello registered. Dynamic loading does not exist.
- Go: package examples/extensions/<name> plus a cmd/pi-examples main.

Tests instantiate the extension against a fake or recording ExtensionAPI, the same way the TS tests do.

typebox schemas become serde_json::json! / Go map literals, or the native schema builder from the agent package.

Per-example notes:
- jev-router: uses VIRTUAL_MODEL_STATE_ENTRY.
- custom-compaction: session_before_compact returns a custom summary.
- trigger-compact: threshold 100_000 tokens; calls ctx.compact.
- tool-override: shadows `read`; regex blocklist; withFileMutationQueue; logs to getAgentDir()/read-access.log.

hazards: printHelp must be byte-identical, including chalk SGR sequences, padEnd(30) for extension flags, and the env-var list. Color detection must mirror chalk: NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, TTY. Golden-test it.
RPC parse errors embed the V8 JSON.parse message (`Failed to parse command: Unexpected token ...`). This text cannot match natively. Keep the prefix and command "parse", and document the divergence.
RPC input lines must be processed concurrently. A serial read-handle loop deadlocks when an extension dialog opened during prompt preflight waits for an extension_ui_response line.

stdout takeover in json/rpc modes: anything other than protocol records must go to stderr, including npm output, warnings and Usage text (stdout-cleanliness.test). In Rust, avoid println! in library code. In Go, never write to os.Stdout outside the guarded writer.
The stable cli must not dispatch experimental server/client commands (#9132). Keep the experimental registry separate and gated by PI_EXPERIMENTAL.
The -e/--extension flag and unknown extension flags must still parse. TS extension paths cannot load natively and must produce a clear diagnostic, not a crash.

RpcClient spawns the pi binary instead of node. The exit rejection text `Agent process exited (code=N signal=null)` must reproduce JS null/number formatting. Tests that used node child scripts need sh or helper-binary equivalents.

Session directory encoding `--<cwd with leading / or \\ removed and / \\ : replaced by ->--` must match migrations.ts and migrate-sessions.sh exactly. Session prefix lookup order is: path, then local exact/prefix, then global exact/prefix.
--connect URL validation (unix:///path, radius://<uuid>) relies on WHATWG URL semantics. Rust url and Go net/url differ on edge cases; restrict to the tested forms.

Docs and examples are referenced at runtime by the system prompt (Additional docs / Examples paths via config.ts helpers). The native binary must embed them or install them alongside, and resolve the paths the same way.
The subagent example re-invokes pi via process.execPath + argv[1]. Native code must use current_exe and must not assume a node interpreter.
Example extensions persist custom entries (appendEntry) and tool-result details in session files. Native versions must emit identical JSON shapes so sessions stay interchangeable with TS pi.
Bun-specific restore-sandbox-env behavior (reading /proc/self/environ when env is empty) is irrelevant to native binaries. Dropping it is a deliberate behavior change; note it in docs.
js_runtime_dependent: User TS extensions (-e path.ts, extensions found in settings/packages): not loaded. Parse the flags as before, then emit a diagnostic naming the skipped TS extension. Built-in extensions (mcp, codemode, llama, tool-search) are compiled in natively.

src/bun/* (Bun compiled-binary entry, Bun OAuth registration, quickjs.wasm import, sandbox env restore): replaced by a single native main. quickjs.wasm is embedded via include_bytes!/go:embed for codemode on wasmtime/wazero. Providers are registered statically. The /proc/self/environ fallback is optional.
rpc-entry.ts (npm export ./rpc-entry): replaced by `pi --mode rpc` on the native binary.

Package manager self-update via `npm ci --ignore-scripts` into releases/<version>: becomes a download of native release archives from PI_INSTALLER_API_BASE into the same releases-v1 layout with an atomic current-version switch.
pi install of npm/git packages: still shells out to npm/git to fetch resources. Skills, prompts and themes load. TS extensions in packages are listed as unloadable.
examples/extensions/with-deps: inherently about jiti npm resolution. Keep as legacy TS reference only.
examples/extensions/doom-overlay: Emscripten JS glue evaluated with new Function. Keep as JS-only, or optionally port by rebuilding doomgeneric for WASI and running it under wasmtime/wazero.
examples/extensions/gondolin and sandbox: depend on npm-only runtime libraries. Keep as JS-only. Sandbox could get a separate native sandbox-exec/bwrap rewrite.
examples/plugins/pi-example-plugin: Chord TS facets loaded by the experimental plugin entry. JS-only unless Chord is ported.

All other examples/extensions/*.ts and examples/sdk/*.ts: re-expressed as native Rust/Go code implementing the Extension trait/interface or calling the native SDK. They are registered at compile time through an examples binary, not loaded at runtime.
docs/sdk.md, extensions.md, tui.md, custom-provider.md: describe TS APIs. Rewrite them for the native trait/interface and SDK.

units.title: Experimental internal process spawning, coordinator socket router, Session catalog
units.notes:
process.ts: INTERNAL_PROCESS_ENV="__PI_INTERNAL_SPAWN" with roles coordinator|server|session-worker. consumeInternalProcessRole deletes the env var at startup so grandchildren do not inherit it.
- spawnInternalProcess spawns process.execPath [--import source-resolver.ts when running from .ts] entryUrl args, with detached:true, stdio ignore, windowsHide, cwd=process.cwd(), then unref().
- Native: re-exec std::env::current_exe() / os.Executable() with the role env.
  - Rust: Command::new(exe).env(..).stdin/stdout/stderr(Stdio::null()) plus CommandExt::process_group(0) (or setsid in pre_exec). Do not block on the child; reap it in a detached thread so no zombie remains while the parent lives.
  - Go: exec.Command with SysProcAttr{Setsid:true}, Start, then go cmd.Wait().
- terminateInternalProcess sends SIGKILL and awaits exit.
- defaultEntryUrl (dist/bundle/coordinator.js or cli.js) and source-resolver.ts (Node module.registerHooks tsconfig-path loader) have no native equivalent. Do not port source-resolver; coordinator-entry.ts becomes a role branch in main().

coordinator.ts, wire format:
- JSON lines, encodeControlLine = JSON.stringify(msg)+"\n", max line 128 MiB (MAX_CONTROL_LINE_BYTES). Reject or close on overflow.
- Messages are typebox Type.Object (extra properties allowed, unlike the worker protocol's StrictObject). Use serde internally tagged enums, #[serde(tag="type")], with camelCase fields (serverConnectionId, peerId, endpoint, protocol, peers, from, to, payload). payload is arbitrary JSON: serde_json::Value / json.RawMessage.
- COORDINATOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION=3. The peerId "server" is reserved. Only the server may broadcast.

coordinator.ts, coordinator process:
- The coordinator's module-global state should become a struct.
- Sockets: public `<dir>/<serverId>.sock`, control `<dir>/control-<serverId>.sock`, both chmod 0600 except on win32. Server endpoints are `server-<serverId>-<12 hex>.sock`.
- Public connections are piped bidirectionally to the current server endpoint (tokio::io::copy_bidirectional / two io.Copy goroutines). They are all closed when the server is replaced.
- Stale socket removal: lstat isSocket plus a connect probe. ECONNREFUSED or ENOENT means stale, so unlink.
- Empty shutdown: 30s after startup, otherwise 250ms. cleanupSocket is skipped on win32.
- ensureCoordinator spawns and retries connect every 10ms for up to 10s.
- macOS sun_path is limited to 104 bytes; long PI_SERVER_DIR paths fail the same way TS does.

session-catalog.ts:
- meta.json is exactly JSON.stringify({createdAt:<ms number>, cwd}, null, "\t")+"\n". Use serde_json PrettyFormatter::with_indent(b"\t"); in Go use json.Encoder with SetIndent("","\t") and SetEscapeHTML(false), and note that Go escapes U+2028/U+2029.
- Session id regex ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$. The default id is lowercase randomUUID (uuid v4).
- createSession maps an EEXIST mkdir to "Session <id> already exists". readSession tolerates missing or invalid metadata (it returns undefined).

units.title: Experimental chord service contracts and providers (agent controller, models, slash commands, transcript, sessions, plugins, connection sources)
units.notes:
Service contracts (defineService) become Rust traits / Go interfaces from the native chord port. Service ids must stay byte-identical because they travel on the CBOR protocol: pi.agent-controller, pi.models, pi.presentation-plugins, pi.session-plugins, pi.session-directory, pi.session-management, pi.transcript, plus local-only pi.local.presentation-ui and pi.local.slash-commands. Keep member names and argument/result JSON shapes exactly.

AgentController results:
- {accepted:boolean, operationId|entryId, error:{code:"busy"|"operation_failed", message}|null}. The busy path comes from durable ConversationBusy.
- waitForPrompt returns {status:"done",text,reason:null} | {status:"unanswered",text:null,reason}.
- cancelQueued outcomes: cancelled / already_consumed / not_found.
- parseSubmissionId uses regex ^[1-9][0-9]*$. Submission ids are positive JS safe integers: use u64 with a check of <= 2^53-1.

Models state:
- {catalog:{revision, availableModels:[{provider, modelId, name, reasoning}]}, configuration:{model|null, thinkingLevel}}, plus refresh.
- select persists the default model through SettingsManager (settings.json byte compatibility is owned by the settings area).

Slash commands:
- Name regex ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:-]*$ (u flag; ASCII only, so no unicode issue).
- Registry replace is staged.
- Builtins: /model, /thinking (THINKING_DESCRIPTIONS text), /compact, /reload.

services/server.ts:
- The replicated SessionDirectory {revision, sessions} uses serialized mutations, via a promise tail: use a tokio Mutex or a Go channel worker to keep FIFO order.
- Each client gets a RemoteServiceProvider.

services/connection.ts:
- ServerServiceSourceImpl states: connecting/connected/disconnected. SessionServiceSourceImpl states: detached/attaching/attached/degraded.
- Attachment revision fencing (drop stale hydration).
- whenAttached/whenDetached waiters.
- Timestamps come from new Date().toISOString(): millisecond precision with a Z suffix. Rust: chrono to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Millis, true). Go: t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z").

Cancellation uses chord Context (withCancel); map it to a CancellationToken / context.Context.

plugin.ts is the public plugin type surface: re-export the native traits.

Test support: experimental-durable-support.ts (openFauxConversation over MemoryStorage with the faux provider) is also used by the client-tui and plugin-reload tests in other units.

units.title: Experimental per-Session worker process, worker protocol, SessionWorkerManager, worker service composition
units.notes:
Worker protocol (session-worker.ts typebox):
- Commands and events use StrictObject (additionalProperties:false): #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] in Rust, json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields plus explicit validation in Go. Typebox also enforces integer/minimum constraints (instance.generation >= 1).
- Commands: shutdown, discover_workers, session_demand{serverConnectionId,requestId,attachmentId,attached}, operation{requestId, scope{serverConnectionId,attachmentId}, call{serviceId, instance?{key,generation}, member, args}}, operation_cancel.
- Events: worker_ready{token,sessionKey,sessionId,pid,metadata,pluginManifestPaths}, worker_failed, demand_applied, demand_rejected, operation_response{response: {type:"operation_result", result?} | {type:"operation_error", code?, message}}, service_update{scope, subscriptionId, update}.
- Optional fields must be omitted rather than serialized as null (skip_serializing_if / omitempty with pointer types).

Env vars:
- PI_SESSION_WORKER_CONTROL_ADDRESS, PI_SESSION_WORKER_CONTROL_TOKEN, PI_SESSION_WORKER_PEER_ID.
- PI_SESSION_WORKER_SESSION_KEY_BASE64 is Buffer.from(path).toString("base64url"), unpadded (Rust base64 URL_SAFE_NO_PAD, Go base64.RawURLEncoding).
- __PI_SESSION_WORKER_INITIAL_DEMAND_GRACE_MS (default 10000) and __PI_SESSION_WORKER_ORPHAN_DEMAND_GRACE_MS (default 30000).

WorkerLifecycle is a pure state machine (demand by attachment and generation, retirement holds while a demand ack is in flight, Harness activity, orphan and initial timers). Port it as a deterministic struct with an injectable clock and timers so the lifecycle tests can use fake time (vi.useFakeTimers equivalents: tokio::time::pause or a manual clock interface in Go).

The worker locks the Session dir with proper-lockfile: realpath:true, stale 2000ms, update 1000ms, retries 320 x 25ms, maxRetryTime 8000. The lock is the directory `<realpath>.lock`, its mtime is refreshed, and staleness is judged by mtime. Hand-port this for interop.

createCodingAgentHarness:
- ModelRuntime.create, SettingsManager.create(cwd), configureHarnessHttp, ExecutionEnvs.
- Harness.open on SQLite (rusqlite / modernc.org/sqlite), then findInitialAgentModel only when the root conversation is new.

SessionWorkerManager timeouts:
- startup 15s; shutdown 10s then SIGKILL; discovery 5s.
- Demand timeout 5s with compensation: send attached:false, and kill if that fails.
- No timeout on operations.

SessionWorkerManager bookkeeping:
- Subscription map key `${serverConnectionId}\0${attachmentId}\0${subscriptionId}`: use a tuple key natively.
- Pending calls are rejected on server replacement without stopping workers.
- SessionPluginSelectionConflictError when a different plugin selection targets a live Session.
- process.kill(pid,0) liveness and ESRCH handling.

services/worker.ts composes the builtin facets (agent-controller-runtime, session-plugins-runtime, models, transcript) and a plugin facet loader with reload/cutover. Natively the plugin loader becomes a registry of compiled-in facets; keep the reload generation semantics tested by experimental-plugin-reload.test.ts (the test uses an in-memory FacetLoader, so it is portable).

The lifecycle and manager tests use fake CoordinatorConnection objects and are fully portable.

units.title: Experimental server profile/activation/lifetime, Radius relay host+client transport, relay auth, plugin package profiles
skipped_tests: packages/coding-agent/test/experimental-presentation-facets.test.ts#builds conventional plugin entries into the server-owned plugin cache -- requires esbuild bundling of a TS plugin package (JS-only)

packages/coding-agent/test/experimental-presentation-facets.test.ts#builds the example plugin package without a package-owned build script -- builds examples/plugins/pi-example-plugin with esbuild (JS-only)
units.notes:
Server profile directory:
- Default ~/.pi/server, override PI_SERVER_DIR. It is created with mode 0700, and its owner must equal getuid(). Implement with nix/libc or x/sys/unix; on platforms without getuid it errors like TS.
- default-server-id is written with open flag wx (O_CREAT|O_EXCL), mode 0600. Its content must be a lowercase UUIDv4 (protocol isServerId); otherwise it is a corrupt-identity error. PI_SERVER_ID overrides it.
- Locks via proper-lockfile (hand-port):
  - launcher-<id>.lock: stale 30s, update 10s, retried every 25ms for up to 30s;
  - activation-<id>.lock: stale 20s, update 10s.
- plugin-packages-<id>.json is {"version":1,"packagePaths":[...]}: JSON.stringify(v,null,2)+"\n", mode 0600.
- session-plugin-packages-<id>-<sha256hex(sessionPath)[0:24]>.json is {version, sessionPath, packagePaths}.
- plugin-builds/<id>/<label>-plugin-<sha256hex(path)[0:12]>/.
- normalizePluginPackagePaths: path.resolve then dedupe, preserving first-seen order.

resolveSessionDirectory: default getAgentDir()/experimental/sessions; an explicit path gets ~ expansion and is resolved against cwd.

activateServer:
- Spawns role server with args [directory, serverId, sessionDir, JSON{provider?,model}?]. Keep the JSON key order.
- Polls connect every 10ms with a 10s timeout. Not-ready errors are ENOENT, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, EPIPE, ETIMEDOUT, DisconnectedError and ServerError code "version".

ServerLifetime: a foreground server has keepAlive. An auto server has a 10s startup grace and a 1s idle grace, and retires only when connections == 0 AND workers == 0. Port it as a pure struct with an injectable clock.

startServerBackend creates the pi-server unix listener with mode 0600. The serverNonce is randomUUID without dashes, first 12 chars.

Radius relay:
- URL: gateway origin + /v1/session-relays/<serverId>/connect, with https->wss and http->ws.
- Subprotocols pi-session-relay.host.v1 / pi-session-relay.client.v1; header authorization: Bearer <token>. Verify that the server-selected protocol matches.
- Host control JSON is {version:1, type: ping|pong|connection_open|connection_close, connection_id, code?}. The field name is snake_case connection_id. code must be in 1000-4999.
- Binary data frame: byte0 = version 1, byte1 = type 1, 16 raw UUID bytes, then the payload.
- connection_id regex: /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/u (lowercase v4 only).
- Backpressure: the pending bytes cap is 4 x 16 MiB. A drain wait polls bufferedAmount every 5ms until it is <= 1 MiB. tungstenite and coder/websocket expose no bufferedAmount, so track outstanding bytes in an OrderedWebSocketWriter equivalent (a single writer task with a byte-counted queue).
- Close codes: 4000 protocol error, 4001 transport error, 1012 when the server rejects the accept.
- Reconnect backoff doubles from 1s to 30s; it is 30s when unauthenticated.
- delay() uses unref'd timers. Natively, make sure the backoff sleeps are cancelled on close.
- Undici WebSocket error events can lack detail; the TS code synthesizes a useful message (the test asserts the text).

radius-auth:
- Explicit token or token file, else ModelRuntime OAuth provider "radius" with minOAuthValidityMs 5 min.
- PI_OFFLINE disables it.
- Exact error strings are in the summary hazards.

plugins/bundled.ts and plugins/package.ts are JS-only (esbuild build, then vm load). Natively, keep pluginBuildDirectoryName, profile read/write and normalization, but replace bundle building and loading with a compiled-in facet registry. createPresentationFacetData returns {presentationFacetBundles:[]} for native-only facets.

Tests:
- radius-relay tests use injected WebSocket factories plus allowNetwork() (vitest sets PI_OFFLINE=1 by default). Port them with an in-process WS server or a fake socket.
- presentation-facets tests 1-2 (reject local plugin paths for Radius servers; restore plugin package selections) are portable.
